**Deuteronomy 11:20**

And you shall write them on the doorposts of your houses and your gates,

**Deuteronomy 11:21**

so that your days and the days of your children may be many on the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.

**Deuteronomy 11:22**

And it shall be, if indeed you listen to all these commands that I command you today to do, to love the Lord our God and to walk in all his ways and cling to him,

**Deuteronomy 11:23**

then the Lord will cast out all these nations from before your face, and you will inherit nations greater and stronger than you.

**Deuteronomy 11:24**

Every place where the track of your foot treads shall be yours, from the wilderness and Anti-Lebanon, and from the great river, the river Euphrates, and as far as the western sea shall be your boundaries.

**Deuteronomy 11:25**

No one shall stand against your face. The Lord your God will put your terror and your fear on the face of all the land on which you step, in the way the Lord spoke to you.

**Deuteronomy 11:26**

Behold, I set before you today blessing and curse:

**Deuteronomy 11:27**

the blessing, if you hear the commands of the Lord your God that I command you today,

**Deuteronomy 11:28**

and the curse, if you do not hear the commands of the Lord your God that I command you today and wander from the way that I commanded you, going to serve other gods whom you do not know.

**Deuteronomy 11:29**

And it shall be, when the Lord your God brings you into the land into which you are crossing there to inherit it, then you shall place the blessing on Mount Garizin and the curse on Mount Gaibal.

**Deuteronomy 11:30**

Behold, are these not beyond the Jordan, behind the road of the sun's setting, in the land of Canaan that lies westward, near Golgol, beside the tall oak?

**Deuteronomy 11:31**

For you are crossing the Jordan, entering to inherit the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance all the days, and you shall inherit it and dwell in it.

**Deuteronomy 11:32**

And you shall keep to do all his ordinances and these judgments that I set before you today.

### Chapter 12

**Deuteronomy 12:1**

And these are the ordinances and the judgments that you shall keep to do on the land that the Lord God of your fathers gives you as an inheritance, all the days that you live on the land.

**Deuteronomy 12:2**

With destruction you shall destroy all the places in which those whom you inherit served their gods, on the high mountains and on the hills and under every dense tree.

**Deuteronomy 12:3**

And you shall dig down their altars and shatter their pillars and cut down their sacred groves, and the carved images of their gods you shall burn with fire, and their name shall perish from that place.

**Deuteronomy 12:4**

You shall not do thus to the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 12:5**

But only to the place that the Lord your God chooses in one of your tribes, to have his name called there, you shall seek, and you shall go in there.

**Deuteronomy 12:6**

And you shall bring there your whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices and your firstfruits and your vows and your freewill offerings and the firstborn of your cattle and your sheep,

**Deuteronomy 12:7**

and you shall eat there before the Lord your God and rejoice in everything to which you put your hand, you and your households, in the way the Lord your God blessed you.

**Deuteronomy 12:8**

You shall not do all that we do here today, each one what is pleasing before himself,

**Deuteronomy 12:9**

for you have not come until now to the rest and to the inheritance that the Lord your God gives you.

**Deuteronomy 12:10**

And you shall cross the Jordan and dwell on the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance, and he will give you rest from all your enemies around, and you shall dwell in safety.

**Deuteronomy 12:11**

And it shall be, the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there, there you shall bring everything that I command you today, your whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices and your tithes and the firstfruits of your hands and every choice gift that you vow to your God.

**Deuteronomy 12:12**

And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you and your sons and your daughters, your male servants and your female servants, and the Levite within your gates, because he has no portion or inheritance with you.

**Deuteronomy 12:13**

Watch yourself lest you bring up your whole burnt offerings in every place that you see,

**Deuteronomy 12:14**

but only at the place that the Lord your God chooses, that one, in one of your tribes, there you shall offer your whole burnt offerings and there you shall do everything that I command you today.

**Deuteronomy 12:15**

But according to all your desire, you may slaughter and eat meat according to the blessing of the Lord your God that he gave you in every city. The unclean among you and the clean alike shall eat it, as the gazelle or the deer.

**Deuteronomy 12:16**

Except the blood, you shall not eat it. You shall pour it out on the ground like water.

**Deuteronomy 12:17**

You shall not be able to eat in your cities the tithe of your grain and your wine and your oil, the firstborn of your cattle and your sheep, and all the vows that you vow and your confessions and the firstfruits of your hands,

**Deuteronomy 12:18**

but only before the Lord your God shall you eat them in the place that the Lord your God chooses for himself, you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant and the proselyte in your cities, and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God in everything to which you put your hand.

**Deuteronomy 12:19**

Watch yourself lest you abandon the Levite for all the time that you live on the land.

**Deuteronomy 12:20**

And if the Lord your God enlarges your boundaries, just as he spoke to you, and you say, I will eat meat, if your soul desires to eat meat, then by every desire of your soul you may eat meat.

**Deuteronomy 12:21**

And if the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there is farther from you, then you shall slaughter from your cattle and from your sheep that God gave you, in the way I commanded you, and you shall eat in your cities according to the desire of your soul.

**Deuteronomy 12:22**

Just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you shall eat it. The unclean among you and the clean alike shall eat it.

**Deuteronomy 12:23**

Watch strongly that you do not eat blood, because its blood is life. Life shall not be eaten with the flesh.

**Deuteronomy 12:24**

You shall not eat it. You shall pour it out on the ground like water.

**Deuteronomy 12:25**

You shall not eat it, so that it may be well with you and with your sons after you, if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 12:26**

Except your holy things that you may have, and your vows, taking them you shall come to the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there.

**Deuteronomy 12:27**

And you shall make your whole burnt offerings: the meat you shall offer on the altar of the Lord your God, and the blood of your sacrifices you shall pour out at the base of the altar of the Lord your God, but the meat you shall eat.

**Deuteronomy 12:28**

Keep and hear and do all these words that I command you, so that it may be well with you and with your sons forever, if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 12:29**

And if the Lord your God utterly destroys the nations into whose land you are entering there to inherit it from before your face, and you fully inherit them and dwell in their land,

**Deuteronomy 12:30**

watch yourself lest you seek to follow after them after they have been destroyed from before your face. You shall certainly not seek their gods, saying, How do these nations act toward their gods? I also will do likewise.

**Deuteronomy 12:31**

You shall not do thus to the Lord your God, for the abominations that the Lord hated they did to their gods, because they burn their sons and their daughters in fire to their gods.

### Chapter 13

**Deuteronomy 13:1**

Every word that I command you today, this you shall keep to do. You shall not add to it, nor take away from it.

**Deuteronomy 13:2**

And if a prophet arises among you, or one dreaming a dream, and he gives you a sign or a wonder,

**Deuteronomy 13:3**

and the sign or wonder comes that he spoke to you, saying, Let us go and serve other gods whom you do not know,

**Deuteronomy 13:4**

you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of the dream, because the Lord your God tests you, to know whether you love the Lord your God from your whole heart and from your whole soul.

**Deuteronomy 13:5**

After the Lord your God you shall walk, and him you shall fear, and his commands you shall keep, and his voice you shall hear, and to him you shall be joined.

**Deuteronomy 13:6**

And that prophet or that dreamer of the dream shall die, because he spoke to lead you astray from the Lord your God who brought you out from the land of Egypt, who redeemed you from slavery, to drive you out of the way that the Lord your God commanded you to walk in it. And you shall destroy the evil one from among you.

**Deuteronomy 13:7**

And if your brother from your father or from your mother or your son or your daughter or the wife in your bosom or the friend equal to your soul secretly urges you, saying, Let us go and serve other gods whom neither you nor your fathers knew,

**Deuteronomy 13:8**

from the gods of the nations around you, those near you or those far from you, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth,

**Deuteronomy 13:9**

you shall not agree with him, and you shall not listen to him, and your eye shall not spare him, and you shall not long for him, nor indeed hide him.

**Deuteronomy 13:10**

Reporting, you shall report concerning him. Your hands shall be upon him first to kill him, and the hands of all the people last.

**Deuteronomy 13:11**

And they shall stone him with stones, and he shall die, because he sought to turn you away from the Lord your God who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.

**Deuteronomy 13:12**

And all Israel, hearing, shall fear, and they shall not add again to do according to this evil word among you.

**Deuteronomy 13:13**

And if you hear in one of your cities that the Lord your God gives you to dwell there, people saying,

**Deuteronomy 13:14**

Lawless men have gone out from among you and turned away all those dwelling in their city, saying, Let us go and serve other gods whom you did not know,

**Deuteronomy 13:15**

then you shall inquire and search very carefully, and behold, if the matter has clearly become true, that this abomination happened among you,

**Deuteronomy 13:16**

killing, you shall kill all those dwelling in that city with the slaughter of the sword. With a devoted thing you shall devote it and everything in it.

**Deuteronomy 13:17**

And all its spoils you shall gather into its crossroads, and you shall burn the city with fire and all its spoils publicly before the Lord your God, and it shall be uninhabited forever. It shall not be built again.

**Deuteronomy 13:18**

Nothing from the devoted thing shall cling to your hand, so that the Lord may turn from the wrath of his anger and give you mercy and show you mercy and multiply you, in the way the Lord swore to your fathers,

**Deuteronomy 13:19**

if you hear the voice of the Lord your God, keeping all his commands that I command you today, to do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.

### Chapter 14

**Deuteronomy 14:1**

You are sons of the Lord your God. You shall not gash yourselves, nor put baldness between your eyes for the dead,

**Deuteronomy 14:2**

because you are a holy people to the Lord your God, and the Lord your God chose you to become for him a people of special possession from all the nations on the face of the earth.

**Deuteronomy 14:3**

You shall not eat any abomination.

**Deuteronomy 14:4**

These are the animals that you shall eat: calf from the cattle, lamb from the sheep, and kid from the goats,

**Deuteronomy 14:5**

stag and gazelle and buffalo and goat-deer and pygarg and oryx and giraffe.

**Deuteronomy 14:6**

Every animal that parts the hoof and splits the claws in two hoof-parts and brings up cud among the animals, these you shall eat.

**Deuteronomy 14:7**

And these you shall not eat from those that bring up cud and from those that part the hoof and split the claws: the camel and the hare and the hyrax, because they bring up cud but do not part the hoof. These are unclean for you.

**Deuteronomy 14:8**

And the pig, because it parts the hoof and splits the hoof-claws, but it does not chew the cud, this is unclean for you. From their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall not touch.

**Deuteronomy 14:9**

And these you shall eat from all that are in the waters: everything that has fins and scales in them you shall eat.

**Deuteronomy 14:10**

And everything that does not have fins and scales you shall not eat. They are unclean for you.

**Deuteronomy 14:11**

Every clean bird you shall eat.

**Deuteronomy 14:12**

And these are what you shall not eat from them: the eagle and the griffin and the sea-eagle,

**Deuteronomy 14:13**

and the vulture and the kite and those like it,

**Deuteronomy 14:14**

and every raven and those like it,

**Deuteronomy 14:15**

and the ostrich and the owl and the gull,

**Deuteronomy 14:16**

and the heron and the swan and the ibis,

**Deuteronomy 14:17**

and the diver and the hawk and those like it and the hoopoe and the night-raven,

**Deuteronomy 14:18**

and the pelican and the plover and those like it and the purple bird and the bat.

**Deuteronomy 14:19**

Every creeping thing of the birds is unclean for you. You shall not eat from them.

**Deuteronomy 14:20**

Every clean flying thing you shall eat.

**Deuteronomy 14:21**

You shall not eat any carcass. It shall be given to the resident alien in your cities, and he shall eat it, or you may sell it to the foreigner, because you are a holy people to the Lord your God. You shall not boil a lamb in its mother's milk.

**Deuteronomy 14:22**

Tithing, you shall tithe all the produce of your seed, the produce of your field, year by year.

**Deuteronomy 14:23**

And you shall eat it before the Lord your God in the place where the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there. You shall bring the tithes of your grain and your wine and your oil and the firstborn of your cattle and your sheep, so that you may learn to fear the Lord your God all the days.

**Deuteronomy 14:24**

And if the road is too long for you and you are not able to carry them, because the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there is far from you, because the Lord your God will bless you,

**Deuteronomy 14:25**

then you shall exchange them for silver and take the silver in your hands and go to the place that the Lord your God chooses, that one,

**Deuteronomy 14:26**

and you shall give the silver for everything your soul desires, for cattle or for sheep, for wine or for strong drink or for anything your soul desires, and you shall eat there before the Lord your God and rejoice, you and your household.

**Deuteronomy 14:27**

And the Levite who is in your cities, because he has no portion or inheritance with you,

**Deuteronomy 14:28**

after three years you shall bring out all the tithe of your produce in that year and place it in your cities,

**Deuteronomy 14:29**

and the Levite will come, because he has no portion or inheritance with you, and the proselyte and the orphan and the widow who are in your cities, and they shall eat and be filled, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works that you do.

### Chapter 15

**Deuteronomy 15:1**

At the end of seven years you shall make a release.

**Deuteronomy 15:2**

And this is the ordinance of the release: you shall release every personal debt that your neighbor owes you, and you shall not demand it from your brother, because a release has been proclaimed to the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 15:3**

From the foreigner you shall demand, but from your brother you shall make a release of your debt.

**Deuteronomy 15:4**

Because there shall not be one in need among you, because in blessing the Lord your God will bless you in the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance to inherit it,

**Deuteronomy 15:5**

if indeed you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, keeping and doing all these commands that I command you today.

**Deuteronomy 15:6**

Because the Lord your God blessed you in the way he spoke to you, and you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow, and you shall rule many nations, but they shall not rule you.

**Deuteronomy 15:7**

And if one in need arises among you from your brothers in one of your cities, in the land that the Lord your God gives you, you shall not harden your heart, nor indeed close your hand from your needy brother,

**Deuteronomy 15:8**

but opening, you shall open your hands to him. Lending, you shall lend to him as much as he needs, according to what he lacks.

**Deuteronomy 15:9**

Watch yourself lest a hidden matter of lawlessness arise in your heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, draws near, and your eye become evil toward your needy brother and you do not give to him, and he cries out against you to the Lord, and there will be great sin in you.

**Deuteronomy 15:10**

Giving, you shall give to him, and lending, you shall lend to him as much as he needs, and you shall not grieve in your heart while giving to him, because for this word the Lord your God will bless you in all your works and in everything to which you put your hand.

**Deuteronomy 15:11**

For one in need shall certainly not fail from the land. Because of this I command you to do this word, saying, Opening, you shall open your hands to your brother, to the poor and the needy one on your land.

**Deuteronomy 15:12**

And if your Hebrew brother or Hebrew sister is sold to you, he shall serve you six years, and in the seventh you shall send him away from you free.

**Deuteronomy 15:13**

And when you send him away from you free, you shall not send him away empty.

**Deuteronomy 15:14**

Furnishing, you shall furnish him from your sheep and from your grain and from your winepress. In the way the Lord your God blessed you, you shall give to him.

**Deuteronomy 15:15**

And you shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you from there. Because of this I command you to do this word.

**Deuteronomy 15:16**

And if he says to you, I will not go out from you, because he loved you and your household, because it is well for him with you,

**Deuteronomy 15:17**

then you shall take the awl and pierce his ear to the door, and he shall be your household servant forever. And you shall do likewise to your female servant.

**Deuteronomy 15:18**

It shall not be hard before you when you send them away free from you, because he served you six years for a yearly wage doubled from the hired worker, and the Lord your God will bless you in all that you do.

**Deuteronomy 15:19**

Every firstborn, whatever is born among your cattle and your sheep, the males, you shall consecrate to the Lord your God. You shall not work with your firstborn calf, nor shall you shear the firstborn of your sheep.

**Deuteronomy 15:20**

Before the Lord your God you shall eat it, year by year, in the place that the Lord your God chooses, you and your household.

**Deuteronomy 15:21**

And if there is a blemish in it, lame or blind or any evil blemish, you shall not sacrifice it to the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 15:22**

In your cities you shall eat it. The unclean among you and the clean alike shall eat it, as the gazelle or the deer.

**Deuteronomy 15:23**

Except the blood, you shall not eat it. You shall pour it out on the ground like water.

### Chapter 16

**Deuteronomy 16:1**

Keep the month of new grain, and you shall make the Passover to the Lord your God, because in the month of new grain you came out from Egypt by night.

**Deuteronomy 16:2**

And you shall sacrifice the Passover to the Lord your God, sheep and cattle, in the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there.

**Deuteronomy 16:3**

You shall not eat leaven on it. Seven days you shall eat on it unleavened bread, bread of affliction, because in haste you came out from Egypt, so that you may remember the day of your departure from the land of Egypt all the days of your life.

**Deuteronomy 16:4**

No leaven shall be seen to you in all your boundaries seven days, and none of the meat that you sacrifice in the evening on the first day shall remain overnight until morning.

**Deuteronomy 16:5**

You shall not be able to sacrifice the Passover in any of your cities that the Lord your God gives you,

**Deuteronomy 16:6**

but only at the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there, there you shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening, at the setting of the sun, at the time when you came out from Egypt.

**Deuteronomy 16:7**

And you shall cook and roast and eat it in the place that the Lord your God chooses, that one, and in the morning you shall turn and go away to your houses.

**Deuteronomy 16:8**

Six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day, departure feast to the Lord your God. You shall do no work in it except what shall be done for a life.

**Deuteronomy 16:9**

Seven full weeks you shall count for yourself. From when you begin to put the sickle to the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks.

**Deuteronomy 16:10**

And you shall make the Feast of Weeks to the Lord your God according to the strength of your hand, whatever you may give, in the way the Lord your God blessed you.

**Deuteronomy 16:11**

And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, and the Levite in your cities and the proselyte and the orphan and the widow among you, in the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there.

**Deuteronomy 16:12**

And you shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and you shall keep and do these commands.

**Deuteronomy 16:13**

You shall make the Feast of Booths for yourself seven days, when you gather in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.

**Deuteronomy 16:14**

And you shall rejoice in your feast, you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, and the Levite and the proselyte and the orphan and the widow who are in your cities.

**Deuteronomy 16:15**

Seven days you shall feast to the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God chooses for himself, because if the Lord your God blesses you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, then you shall be rejoicing.

**Deuteronomy 16:16**

Three times in the year every male among you shall appear before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord chooses: in the Feast of Unleavened Bread and in the Feast of Weeks and in the Feast of Tabernacle-making. You shall not appear before the Lord your God empty,

**Deuteronomy 16:17**

each according to the ability of your hands, according to the blessing of the Lord your God that he gave you.

**Deuteronomy 16:18**

You shall appoint judges and scribes for yourself in all your cities that the Lord your God gives you, according to tribes, and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.

**Deuteronomy 16:19**

They shall not turn aside judgment. They shall not recognize a face, nor take a gift, because gifts blind the eyes of the wise and remove the words of the righteous.

**Deuteronomy 16:20**

Justly pursue what is just, so that you may live and, entering in, inherit the land that the Lord your God gives you.

**Deuteronomy 16:21**

You shall not plant for yourself a grove, any tree, beside the altar of the Lord your God that you make for yourself.

**Deuteronomy 16:22**

You shall not set up for yourself a pillar, which the Lord your God hated.

### Chapter 17

**Deuteronomy 17:1**

You shall not sacrifice to the Lord your God a calf or a sheep in which there is a blemish, any evil thing, because it is an abomination to the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 17:2**

And if there is found among you in one of your cities that the Lord your God gives you, a man or a woman who does evil before the Lord your God by transgressing his covenant,

**Deuteronomy 17:3**

and they go and serve other gods and bow to them, to the sun or to the moon or to anything from the order of heaven, which he did not command,

**Deuteronomy 17:4**

and it is reported to you, and you search it out very carefully, and behold, the matter has truly happened, this abomination has occurred in Israel,

**Deuteronomy 17:5**

then you shall bring out that man or that woman, and you shall stone them with stones, and they shall die.

**Deuteronomy 17:6**

On two witnesses or on three witnesses the one dying shall die. He shall not die on one witness.

**Deuteronomy 17:7**

And the hand of the witnesses shall be upon him first to put him to death, and the hand of all the people last. And you shall destroy the evil one from among you.

**Deuteronomy 17:8**

And if a matter in judgment is too hard for you, between blood and blood, and between judgment and judgment, and between wound and wound, words of judgment in your cities, then, rising, you shall go up to the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there.

**Deuteronomy 17:9**

And you shall come to the Levitical priests and to the judge who may be in those days, and, after seeking, they shall report the judgment to you.

**Deuteronomy 17:10**

And you shall act according to the matter that they report to you from the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there, and you shall keep very carefully to do according to everything that may be legislated to you.

**Deuteronomy 17:11**

According to the law and according to the judgment that they tell you, you shall do. You shall not turn aside from the word that they report to you, right or left.

**Deuteronomy 17:12**

And the man who may act in pride by not listening to the priest who stands there ministering on the name of the Lord your God, or to the judge who may be in those days, that man shall die, and you shall destroy the evil one from Israel.

**Deuteronomy 17:13**

And all the people, hearing, shall fear and no longer act ungodly.

**Deuteronomy 17:14**

And if you enter into the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance and inherit it and dwell on it and say, I will set a ruler over myself, just as also the rest of the nations around me,

**Deuteronomy 17:15**

appointing, you shall appoint over yourself a ruler whom the Lord your God chooses. From your brothers you shall appoint a ruler over yourself. You shall not be able to appoint over yourself a foreign man, because he is not your brother.

**Deuteronomy 17:16**

Only he shall not multiply horses for himself, nor indeed turn the people back to Egypt so as to multiply horses for himself, because the Lord said, You shall not add to return by this road any longer.

**Deuteronomy 17:17**

And he shall not multiply wives for himself, nor shall his heart turn away, and silver and gold he shall not multiply for himself greatly.

**Deuteronomy 17:18**

And it shall be, when he sits on his rule, he shall write for himself this second law in a book from the priests, the Levites.

**Deuteronomy 17:19**

And it shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, keeping all these commands and these ordinances, to do them,

**Deuteronomy 17:20**

so that his heart may not be lifted up above his brothers, so that he may not transgress the commands right or left, so that he may be long-lived in his rule, he and his sons among the sons of Israel.

### Chapter 18

**Deuteronomy 18:1**

There shall not be for the priests, the Levites, the whole tribe of Levi, a portion or inheritance with Israel. They shall eat the Lord's offerings, which are their inheritance.

**Deuteronomy 18:2**

And inheritance shall not be for them among their brothers. The Lord himself is his inheritance, just as he said to him.

**Deuteronomy 18:3**

And this is the due of the priests from the people, from those sacrificing the sacrifices, whether calf or sheep: he shall give to the priest the arm and the jaws and the stomach.

**Deuteronomy 18:4**

And the firstfruits of your grain and your wine and your oil, and the firstfruits of the shearings of your sheep, you shall give to him,

**Deuteronomy 18:5**

because the Lord your God chose him from all your tribes to stand before the Lord your God to minister and bless in his name, he and his sons among the sons of Israel.

**Deuteronomy 18:6**

And if the Levite comes from one of your cities, from all the sons of Israel where he is residing as a stranger, because his soul desires the place that the Lord chooses,

**Deuteronomy 18:7**

then he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, just as all his brothers the Levites who stand there before the Lord.

**Deuteronomy 18:8**

He shall eat an equal portion, besides the sale according to patrimony.

**Deuteronomy 18:9**

And if you enter into the land that the Lord your God gives you, you shall not learn to do according to the abominations of those nations.

**Deuteronomy 18:10**

There shall not be found among you one purifying his son or his daughter through fire, one divining divination, one practicing omens, one reading signs, a sorcerer,

**Deuteronomy 18:11**

one chanting a chant, a ventriloquist, one observing signs, one consulting the dead,

**Deuteronomy 18:12**

because everyone doing these things is an abomination to the Lord your God, for because of these abominations the Lord will utterly destroy them from before your face.

**Deuteronomy 18:13**

You shall be complete before the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 18:14**

For these nations that you inherit, these will listen to omen-readers and diviners. But for you the Lord your God did not give thus.

**Deuteronomy 18:15**

A prophet from your brothers like me the Lord your God will raise up for you. To him you shall listen,

**Deuteronomy 18:16**

according to all that you asked from the Lord your God in Horeb on the day of the assembly, saying, We shall not add to hear the voice of the Lord our God, and we shall not see this great fire any more, nor indeed die.

**Deuteronomy 18:17**

And the Lord said to me, They spoke rightly all that they spoke.

**Deuteronomy 18:18**

I will raise up for them a prophet from their brothers like you, and I will put my word in his mouth, and he shall speak to them according to whatever I command him.

**Deuteronomy 18:19**

And the man who does not hear whatever the prophet speaks in my name, I will exact it from him.

**Deuteronomy 18:20**

But the prophet who may act ungodly by speaking in my name a word that I did not command him to speak, and who may speak in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.

**Deuteronomy 18:21**

And if you say in your heart, How shall we know the word that the Lord did not speak?

**Deuteronomy 18:22**

Whatever the prophet speaks in the name of the Lord and the matter does not happen and does not come to pass, this is the word that the Lord did not speak. In ungodliness that prophet spoke it. You shall not spare him.

### Chapter 19

**Deuteronomy 19:1**

And if the Lord your God utterly destroys the nations whose land your God gives you, and you fully inherit them and dwell in their cities and in their houses,

**Deuteronomy 19:2**

you shall set apart for yourself three cities in the midst of your land that the Lord your God gives you.

**Deuteronomy 19:3**

Prepare the road for yourself, and divide the boundaries of your land into three parts, the land that the Lord your God distributes to you, and there shall be refuge there for every killer.

**Deuteronomy 19:4**

And this shall be the ordinance of the killer who flees there and lives: whoever strikes his neighbor unintentionally, this one not hating him before yesterday or the third day,

**Deuteronomy 19:5**

and whoever enters with his neighbor into the forest to gather wood, and his hand swings with the axe while cutting the wood, and the iron flies from the wood and meets his neighbor and he dies, this one shall flee to one of these cities and live,

**Deuteronomy 19:6**

lest the avenger of blood, pursuing behind the one who killed, because his heart was heated, overtake him if the road is longer, and strike his life and he die, though for this one there is no judgment of death, because he was not hating him before yesterday or the third day.

**Deuteronomy 19:7**

Because of this I command you this word, saying, You shall set apart for yourself three cities.

**Deuteronomy 19:8**

And if the Lord your God enlarges your boundaries in the way he swore to your fathers and the Lord gives you all the land that he said to give to your fathers,

**Deuteronomy 19:9**

if you listen to do all these commands that I command you today, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways all the days, then you shall add for yourself three more cities to these three,

**Deuteronomy 19:10**

and innocent blood shall not be shed in your land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance, and bloodguilt shall not be in you.

**Deuteronomy 19:11**

And if there is a man hating his neighbor, and he lies in wait for him and rises against him and strikes his life and he dies, and he flees to one of these cities,

**Deuteronomy 19:12**

then the elders of his city shall send and take him from there and deliver him into the hands of the avenger of blood, and he shall die.

**Deuteronomy 19:13**

Your eye shall not spare him, and you shall cleanse innocent blood from Israel, and it shall be well with you.

**Deuteronomy 19:14**

You shall not move your neighbor's boundaries that your fathers set in your inheritance that you inherited in the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance.

**Deuteronomy 19:15**

A witness shall not remain to testify against a man for every injustice and for every sin and for every sin that he may sin. By the mouth of two witnesses and by the mouth of three witnesses every word shall stand.

**Deuteronomy 19:16**

And if an unjust witness stands against a man, charging him with ungodliness,

**Deuteronomy 19:17**

then the two men who have the dispute shall stand before the Lord and before the priests and before the judges who may be in those days.

**Deuteronomy 19:18**

And the judges shall investigate exactly, and behold, if the witness is unjust and he has testified unjust things, standing against his brother,

**Deuteronomy 19:19**

then you shall do to him in the way he wickedly intended to do against his brother, and you shall destroy the evil one from among you.

**Deuteronomy 19:20**

And the rest, hearing, shall fear and no longer add to do according to this evil word among you.

**Deuteronomy 19:21**

Your eye shall not spare him: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

### Chapter 20

**Deuteronomy 20:1**

And if you go out to war against your enemies and see horse and rider and a people more numerous than you, you shall not fear before them, because the Lord your God is with you, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.

**Deuteronomy 20:2**

And it shall be, when you draw near to the war, then the priest, drawing near, shall speak to the people,

**Deuteronomy 20:3**

and he shall say to them, Hear, Israel: you draw near today to war against your enemies. Do not let your heart grow weak. Do not fear, nor be broken, nor turn aside from before their face,

**Deuteronomy 20:4**

because the Lord your God, the one going before with you, will fight together with you against your enemies, to save you.

**Deuteronomy 20:5**

And the scribes shall speak to the people, saying, Who is the man who built a new house and did not dedicate it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the war and another man dedicate it.

**Deuteronomy 20:6**

And who is the man who planted a vineyard and did not rejoice from it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the war and another man rejoice from it.

**Deuteronomy 20:7**

And who is the man who is betrothed to a woman and did not take her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the war and another man take her.

**Deuteronomy 20:8**

And the scribes shall add to speak to the people and say, Who is the man who is fearful and cowardly in heart? Let him go and return to his house, lest he make his brother's heart cowardly like his own.

**Deuteronomy 20:9**

And it shall be, when the scribes finish speaking to the people, then they shall appoint leaders of the army to go before the people.

**Deuteronomy 20:10**

And if you draw near to a city to fight against it, then you shall call them with peace.

**Deuteronomy 20:11**

And if they answer you peaceably and open to you, then all the people found in it shall be tributary and subject to you.

**Deuteronomy 20:12**

And if they do not obey you and make war against you, then you shall besiege it.

**Deuteronomy 20:13**

And the Lord your God will give it into your hands, and you shall strike every male in it with the slaughter of the sword.

**Deuteronomy 20:14**

Except the women and the supplies and all the cattle and whatever is in the city and all its provisions, you shall plunder for yourself, and you shall eat all the spoil of your enemies that the Lord your God gives you.

**Deuteronomy 20:15**

Thus you shall do to all the cities that are very far from you, which are not from the cities of these nations.

**Deuteronomy 20:16**

But from the cities of these nations whose land the Lord your God gives you to inherit, you shall not keep alive from them anything breathing.

**Deuteronomy 20:17**

But with a devoted thing you shall devote them, the Hittite and Amorite and Canaanite and Pherezite and Hivite and Jebusite and Gergesite, in the way the Lord your God commanded you,

**Deuteronomy 20:18**

so that they may not teach you to do all their abominations that they did to their gods, and you would sin before the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 20:19**

And if you besiege a city many days to fight against it for its capture, you shall not utterly destroy its trees by putting iron to them. Rather, you may eat from it, but you shall not cut it down, because the tree in the field is not a human to enter before your face into siegeworks.

**Deuteronomy 20:20**

But a tree that you know is not for eating fruit, this you shall destroy and cut down, and you shall build siegeworks against the city that makes war against you until it is given up.

### Chapter 21

**Deuteronomy 21:1**

And if a wounded man is found in the land that the Lord your God gives you to inherit, fallen in the field, and they do not know the one who struck him,

**Deuteronomy 21:2**

then your elders and your judges shall come out and measure to the cities around the wounded man.

**Deuteronomy 21:3**

And it shall be, the city nearest to the wounded man, the elders of that city shall take a heifer from the herd that has not been worked and has not drawn a yoke,

**Deuteronomy 21:4**

and the elders of that city shall bring down the heifer into a rough ravine that has not been worked nor sown, and they shall hamstring the heifer in the ravine.

**Deuteronomy 21:5**

And the priests, the Levites, shall come near, because the Lord your God chose them to stand by him and bless in his name, and by their mouth shall be every dispute and every wound.

**Deuteronomy 21:6**

And all the elders of that city nearest to the wounded man shall wash their hands over the head of the heifer that was hamstrung in the ravine,

**Deuteronomy 21:7**

and answering they shall say, Our hands did not pour out this blood, and our eyes did not see.

**Deuteronomy 21:8**

Be merciful to your people Israel, whom you redeemed, O Lord, from the land of Egypt, so that innocent blood may not be among your people Israel, and the blood shall be atoned for them.

**Deuteronomy 21:9**

And you shall remove innocent blood from among you if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 21:10**

And if, going out to war against your enemies, the Lord your God gives them into your hands, and you plunder their spoil,

**Deuteronomy 21:11**

and you see in the spoil a woman beautiful in appearance and desire her and take her for yourself as a wife,

**Deuteronomy 21:12**

then you shall bring her inside your house, and she shall shave her head and pare her nails,

**Deuteronomy 21:13**

and she shall remove the garments of her captivity from herself and sit in your house and mourn her father and her mother a full month, and after these things you shall go in to her and live with her, and she shall be your wife.

**Deuteronomy 21:14**

And it shall be, if you do not want her, you shall send her away free, and she shall certainly not be sold for silver. You shall not treat her as nothing, because you humbled her.

**Deuteronomy 21:15**

And if a man has two wives, one loved and one hated, and the loved and the hated bear children to him, and the firstborn son belongs to the hated one,

**Deuteronomy 21:16**

then it shall be, on the day he distributes his possessions to his sons, he shall not be able to give firstborn rights to the son of the loved one, overlooking the son of the hated one, the firstborn.

**Deuteronomy 21:17**

But he shall acknowledge the firstborn son of the hated one, to give him a double share from everything found with him, because this one is the beginning of his children, and to him belong the rights of the firstborn.

**Deuteronomy 21:18**

And if a man has a disobedient and provoking son, not obeying the voice of his father and the voice of his mother, and they discipline him and he does not listen to them,

**Deuteronomy 21:19**

then his father and his mother, seizing him, shall bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place,

**Deuteronomy 21:20**

and they shall say to the men of their city, This son of ours disobeys and provokes, he does not listen to our voice, he is a glutton and a drunkard.

**Deuteronomy 21:21**

And the men of his city shall stone him with stones, and he shall die, and you shall destroy the evil one from among you. And the rest, hearing, shall fear.

**Deuteronomy 21:22**

And if in someone there is a sin, a judgment of death, and he dies, and you hang him on a tree,

**Deuteronomy 21:23**

his body shall not remain overnight on the tree, but burying you shall bury him on that day, because everyone hanging on a tree is cursed by God, and you shall not defile the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance.

### Chapter 22

**Deuteronomy 22:1**

Not seeing your brother's calf or his sheep wandering on the road shall you overlook them. Returning, you shall return them to your brother, and you shall give them back to him.

**Deuteronomy 22:2**

And if your brother is not near you, nor do you know him, you shall gather them into your house, and they shall be with you until your brother seeks them, and you shall give them back to him.

**Deuteronomy 22:3**

Thus you shall do with his donkey, and thus you shall do with his garment, and thus you shall do with every loss of your brother, whatever may be lost from him and you find. You shall not be able to overlook it.

**Deuteronomy 22:4**

You shall not see your brother's donkey or his calf fallen on the road and overlook them. Raising, you shall raise them with him.

**Deuteronomy 22:5**

There shall not be a man's gear on a woman, nor shall a man put on a woman's clothing, because everyone doing these things is an abomination to the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 22:6**

And if a brood of birds meets you on the road, or on any tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs and the mother warming over the chicks or over the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the children.

**Deuteronomy 22:7**

Sending, you shall send away the mother, but the young you shall take for yourself, so that it may be well with you and you may be long-lived.

**Deuteronomy 22:8**

And if you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, and you shall not make bloodguilt in your house if the one falling falls from it.

**Deuteronomy 22:9**

You shall not sow your vineyard with diversity, lest the produce and the seed that you sow with the produce of your vineyard be made holy.

**Deuteronomy 22:10**

You shall not plow with calf and donkey together.

**Deuteronomy 22:11**

You shall not wear mixed fabric, wool and linen together.

**Deuteronomy 22:12**

You shall make twisted threads for yourself on the four corners of your cloaks with which you clothe yourself.

**Deuteronomy 22:13**

And if a man takes a wife and lives with her and then hates her,

**Deuteronomy 22:14**

and places pretextual words against her and brings an evil name upon her and says, I took this woman, and after going in to her I did not find her virginity,

**Deuteronomy 22:15**

then, taking the tokens of the girl's virginity, the father of the girl and the mother shall bring them out to the elders at the gate,

**Deuteronomy 22:16**

and the father of the girl shall say to the elders, I gave this daughter of mine to this man as a wife, and, having hated her,

**Deuteronomy 22:17**

he now places pretextual words against her, saying, I did not find virginity for your daughter. And these are the girl's virginity. And they shall spread out the garment before the elders of the city.

**Deuteronomy 22:18**

And the elders of that city shall take that man and discipline him,

**Deuteronomy 22:19**

and they shall fine him one hundred shekels and give them to the father of the young woman, because he brought an evil name upon a virgin of Israel, and she shall be his wife. He shall not be able to send her away all his time.

**Deuteronomy 22:20**

But if this matter truly happened and virginity was not found for the young woman,

**Deuteronomy 22:21**

then they shall bring the young woman out to the doors of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones, and she shall die, because she did folly among the sons of Israel, prostituting herself in her father's house. And you shall destroy the evil one from among you.

**Deuteronomy 22:22**

And if a man is found lying with a woman living with a husband, you shall kill them both, the man lying with the woman and the woman, and you shall destroy the evil one from Israel.

**Deuteronomy 22:23**

And if there is a virgin girl betrothed to a man, and a man finding her in the city lies with her,

**Deuteronomy 22:24**

you shall bring them both out to the gate of their city, and they shall be stoned with stones and die, the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he humbled his neighbor's wife. And you shall destroy the evil one from among you.

**Deuteronomy 22:25**

But if a man finds the betrothed girl in the field and, forcing her, lies with her, you shall kill only the man lying with her.

**Deuteronomy 22:26**

And to the young woman you shall do nothing. The young woman has no sin worthy of death, because as when a man rises against his neighbor and murders his life, so is this matter,

**Deuteronomy 22:27**

because he found her in the field. The betrothed young woman cried out, and there was no one to help her.

**Deuteronomy 22:28**

And if a man finds the virgin girl who is not betrothed and, forcing her, lies with her and they are found,

**Deuteronomy 22:29**

then the man lying with her shall give the father of the young woman fifty silver didrachmas, and she shall be his wife, because he humbled her. He shall not be able to send her away all his time.

### Chapter 23

**Deuteronomy 23:1**

A man shall not take his father's wife, and he shall not uncover his father's covering.

**Deuteronomy 23:2**

One crushed in the testicles and one cut off shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord.

**Deuteronomy 23:3**

One from a prostitute shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord.

**Deuteronomy 23:4**

An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord, and even to the tenth generation he shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord, even forever,

**Deuteronomy 23:5**

because they did not meet you with bread and water on the road when you came out from Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam son of Beor from Mesopotamia to curse you.

**Deuteronomy 23:6**

And the Lord your God was not willing to listen to Balaam, and the Lord your God turned the curses into blessing, because the Lord your God loved you.

**Deuteronomy 23:7**

You shall not greet them with peace, nor seek what benefits them, all your days forever.

**Deuteronomy 23:8**

You shall not abhor an Idumean, because he is your brother. You shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you became a resident in his land.

**Deuteronomy 23:9**

If sons are born to them, the third generation shall enter into the assembly of the Lord.

**Deuteronomy 23:10**

And if you go out to encamp against your enemies, you shall keep yourself from every evil word.

**Deuteronomy 23:11**

And if there is in you a man who is not clean from his night-flow, then he shall go outside the camp and shall not enter into the camp.

**Deuteronomy 23:12**

And it shall be toward evening, he shall wash his body with water, and when the sun has set he shall enter into the camp.

**Deuteronomy 23:13**

And a place shall be for you outside the camp, and you shall go out there,

**Deuteronomy 23:14**

and a peg shall be for you on your belt, and it shall be, when you sit outside, then you shall dig with it and, turning back, you shall cover your indecency with it.

**Deuteronomy 23:15**

Because the Lord your God walks about in your camp to deliver you and hand over your enemy before your face, and your camp shall be holy, and indecency of a matter shall not be seen in you, and he shall turn away from you.

**Deuteronomy 23:16**

You shall not hand over a servant to his master who has been added to you from his master.

**Deuteronomy 23:17**

With you he shall dwell, among you he shall dwell, in every place that pleases him. You shall not afflict him.

**Deuteronomy 23:18**

There shall not be a prostitute from the daughters of Israel, and there shall not be one prostituting himself from the sons of Israel. There shall not be a consecrated woman from the daughters of Israel, and there shall not be a consecrated man from the sons of Israel.

**Deuteronomy 23:19**

You shall not bring the wages of a prostitute nor the price of a dog into the house of the Lord your God for any vow, because both are an abomination to the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 23:20**

You shall not lend at interest to your brother, interest of silver and interest of food and interest of anything that you lend.

**Deuteronomy 23:21**

To the foreigner you shall lend at interest, but to your brother you shall not lend at interest, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all your works on the land into which you are entering there to inherit it.

**Deuteronomy 23:22**

And if you vow a vow to the Lord your God, you shall not delay paying it, because in requiring the Lord your God will require it from you, and there will be sin in you.

**Deuteronomy 23:23**

And if you do not wish to vow, there is no sin in you.

**Deuteronomy 23:24**

What goes out through your lips you shall keep and do, in the way you vowed to the Lord your God, the gift that you spoke with your mouth.

**Deuteronomy 23:25**

And if you enter into your neighbor's standing grain, then you may gather ears with your hands, but you shall certainly not put a sickle to your neighbor's standing grain.

**Deuteronomy 23:26**

And if you enter into your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat grapes as much as your soul desires to be filled, but you shall not put any into a vessel.

### Chapter 24

**Deuteronomy 24:1**

And if a man takes a wife and lives with her, and it happens that she does not find favor before him because he found in her a shameful matter, then he shall write for her a document of divorce and give it into her hands and send her out from his house.

**Deuteronomy 24:2**

And after going out she becomes another man's wife,

**Deuteronomy 24:3**

and the later man hates her and writes for her a document of divorce and gives it into her hands and sends her out from his house, or the later man dies who took her to himself as a wife,

**Deuteronomy 24:4**

then the former man who sent her away shall not be able, after turning back, to take her to himself as a wife after she has been defiled, because it is an abomination before the Lord your God, and you shall not defile the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance.

**Deuteronomy 24:5**

And if a man has recently taken a wife, he shall not go out to war, and no matter shall be laid upon him. He shall be innocent in his house one year, and he shall cheer his wife whom he took.

**Deuteronomy 24:6**

You shall not take a mill or upper millstone as a pledge, because this one takes life as a pledge.

**Deuteronomy 24:7**

And if a man is caught stealing a life from his brothers, from the sons of Israel, and after oppressing him he sells him, that thief shall die, and you shall destroy the evil one from among you.

**Deuteronomy 24:8**

Watch yourself in the matter of leprosy, to keep very carefully to do according to all the law that the Levitical priests report to you. In the way I commanded you, keep to do.

**Deuteronomy 24:9**

Remember what the Lord your God did to Mariam on the road when you came out from Egypt.

**Deuteronomy 24:10**

And if some debt is in your neighbor, any debt whatever, you shall not enter into his house to take the pledge as a pledge.

**Deuteronomy 24:11**

You shall stand outside, and the man in whom your loan is shall bring the pledge out to you.

**Deuteronomy 24:12**

And if the man is poor, you shall not sleep in his pledge.

**Deuteronomy 24:13**

Returning, you shall return his pledge around the setting of the sun, and he shall sleep in his garment and bless you, and it shall be righteousness for you before the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 24:14**

You shall not do injustice to the wages of the poor and needy, whether from your brothers or from the proselytes in your cities.

**Deuteronomy 24:15**

On the same day you shall give his wages. The sun shall not set on it, because he is poor and has his hope in it, and he shall not cry out against you to the Lord, and it will be sin in you.

**Deuteronomy 24:16**

Fathers shall not die for children, and sons shall not die for fathers. Each one shall die in his own sin.

**Deuteronomy 24:17**

You shall not turn aside the judgment of a proselyte and orphan and widow, and you shall not take a widow's garment as a pledge.

**Deuteronomy 24:18**

And you shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you from there. Because of this I command you to do this word.

**Deuteronomy 24:19**

And if you reap a harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not turn back to take it. It shall be for the poor and the proselyte and the orphan and the widow, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works of your hands.

**Deuteronomy 24:20**

And if you gather your olives, you shall not go back to gather what is behind you. It shall be for the proselyte and the orphan and the widow. And you shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt. Because of this I command you to do this word.

**Deuteronomy 24:21**

And if you harvest your vineyard, you shall not glean what is behind you. It shall be for the proselyte and the orphan and the widow.

**Deuteronomy 24:22**

And you shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt. Because of this I command you to do this word.

### Chapter 25

**Deuteronomy 25:1**

And if there is a dispute between men and they come to judgment and they judge and justify the righteous and condemn the ungodly,

**Deuteronomy 25:2**

then it shall be, if the ungodly one is worthy of blows, you shall make him sit before the judges, and they shall whip him before them according to his ungodliness, by number.

**Deuteronomy 25:3**

Forty they shall whip him. They shall not add more. But if they add to whip him beyond these blows, more blows, then your brother will be disgraced before you.

**Deuteronomy 25:4**

You shall not muzzle an ox threshing.

**Deuteronomy 25:5**

And if brothers dwell together and one of them dies and has no seed, the wife of the dead one shall not be outside to a man not near. The brother of her husband shall go in to her and take her to himself as a wife and dwell with her.

**Deuteronomy 25:6**

And it shall be, the child whom she bears shall be established in the name of the one who died, and his name shall not be blotted out from Israel.

**Deuteronomy 25:7**

And if the man does not wish to take his brother's wife, then the woman shall go up to the gate, to the elders, and say, My husband's brother does not wish to raise up his brother's name in Israel. My husband's brother did not want to take me.

**Deuteronomy 25:8**

And the elders of his city shall call him and speak to him, and if he stands and says, I do not wish to take her,

**Deuteronomy 25:9**

then the wife of his brother, coming near before the elders, shall remove his sandal, the one on his foot, and spit into his face, and answering she shall say, Thus they shall do to the man who will not build up his brother's house.

**Deuteronomy 25:10**

And his name shall be called in Israel, House of the one whose sandal was removed.

**Deuteronomy 25:11**

And if men fight together, a man with his brother, and the wife of one comes near to rescue her husband from the hand of the one striking him, and, stretching out her hand, seizes his testicles,

**Deuteronomy 25:12**

you shall cut off her hand. Your eye shall not spare her.

**Deuteronomy 25:13**

There shall not be in your purse a weight and a weight, great or small.

**Deuteronomy 25:14**

There shall not be in your house a measure and a measure, great or small.

**Deuteronomy 25:15**

A true and righteous weight shall be for you, and a true and righteous measure shall be for you, so that you may be long-lived on the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance.

**Deuteronomy 25:16**

Because everyone doing these things, everyone doing injustice, is an abomination to the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 25:17**

Remember what Amalek did to you on the road when you came out from Egypt,

**Deuteronomy 25:18**

how he opposed you on the road and cut down your stragglers, those laboring behind you, while you were hungry and weary, and he did not fear God.

**Deuteronomy 25:19**

And it shall be, when the Lord your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you in the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance to inherit, you shall wipe out the name of Amalek from under heaven. You shall certainly not forget.

### Chapter 26

**Deuteronomy 26:1**

And it shall be, if you enter into the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance and inherit it and dwell on it,

**Deuteronomy 26:2**

then you shall take from the firstfruits of the fruits of your land that the Lord your God gives you and put them into a basket and go to the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there.

**Deuteronomy 26:3**

And you shall come to the priest who may be in those days and say to him, I declare today to the Lord my God that I have entered into the land that the Lord swore to our fathers to give us.

**Deuteronomy 26:4**

And the priest shall take the basket from your hands and set it before the altar of the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 26:5**

And answering you shall say before the Lord your God, My father abandoned Syria and went down into Egypt and lived there as a stranger, few in number, and there he became a nation great and many and large.

**Deuteronomy 26:6**

And the Egyptians afflicted us and humbled us and laid hard works on us.

**Deuteronomy 26:7**

And we cried out to the Lord, the God of our fathers, and the Lord heard our voice and saw our humiliation and our labor and our affliction.

**Deuteronomy 26:8**

And the Lord brought us out from Egypt, he himself, with great strength and with mighty hand and with his high arm and with great visions and with signs and wonders.

**Deuteronomy 26:9**

And he brought us into this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

**Deuteronomy 26:10**

And now, behold, I have brought the firstfruits of the produce of the land that you gave me, Lord, a land flowing with milk and honey. And you shall leave them there before the Lord your God and worship there before the Lord your God.

**Deuteronomy 26:11**

And you shall say before the Lord your God, I have cleansed the holy things out of my house, and I have given them to the Levite and the proselyte and the orphan and the widow, according to all the commands that you commanded me. I did not transgress your command and I did not forget.

**Deuteronomy 26:14**

**Deuteronomy 26:17**

**Deuteronomy 26:18**

**Deuteronomy 26:19**

**Deuteronomy 27:20**

**Deuteronomy 27:22**

**Deuteronomy 28:1**

**Deuteronomy 28:17**

**Deuteronomy 28:18**

Cursed are the offspring of your womb and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep.

**Deuteronomy 28:19**

Cursed are you in your going out, and cursed are you in your coming in.

**Deuteronomy 31:23**

**Deuteronomy 31:25**

**Deuteronomy 31:27**

**Deuteronomy 31:29**

**Deuteronomy 32:24**

**Deuteronomy 32:28**

**Deuteronomy 32:29**

**Deuteronomy 32:30**

**Deuteronomy 32:31**

**Deuteronomy 32:32**

**Deuteronomy 32:33**

**Deuteronomy 32:34**

**Deuteronomy 32:35**

**Deuteronomy 32:36**

**Deuteronomy 32:37**

**Deuteronomy 32:38**

**Deuteronomy 32:39**

**Deuteronomy 32:40**

**Deuteronomy 32:41**

**Deuteronomy 32:42**

**Deuteronomy 32:43**

Rejoice, O heavens, together with him, and let all sons of God worship him. Rejoice, O nations, with his people, and let all angels of God strengthen themselves in him, because he avenges the blood of his sons and will exact vengeance and repay justice to enemies, and to those hating him he will repay, and the Lord will cleanse the land of his people.

**Deuteronomy 32:46**

**Deuteronomy 32:47**

**Deuteronomy 32:48**

And the Lord spoke to Moses on that day, saying,

**Deuteronomy 32:49**

**Deuteronomy 32:50**

**Deuteronomy 32:51**

**Deuteronomy 32:52**

## Joshua

### Chapter 1

**Joshua 1:1**

And it happened after the death of Moses, the Lord said to Joshua son of Nun, minister of Moses, saying,

**Joshua 1:2**

Moses my servant has died. Now therefore, rising up, cross this Jordan, you and all this people, into the land that I give to them.

**Joshua 1:3**

Every place on which you step with the track of your feet, I will give it to you, in the way I told Moses.

**Joshua 1:4**

From the wilderness and Anti-Lebanon as far as the great river, the river Euphrates, and as far as the western sea from the setting of the sun, shall be your boundaries.

**Joshua 1:5**

No person shall stand before you all the days of your life, and as I was with Moses, so I will also be with you, and I will not forsake you nor overlook you.

**Joshua 1:6**

Be strong and act like a man, because you shall apportion to this people the land that I swore to your fathers to give to them.

**Joshua 1:7**

Be strong, therefore, and act like a man, keeping and doing as Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn away from them to the right or to the left, so that you may understand in everything you do.

**Joshua 1:8**

And the book of this law shall not depart from your mouth, and you shall meditate on it day and night, so that you may understand to do all the things written. Then you shall prosper and prosper your ways, and then you shall understand.

**Joshua 1:9**

Behold, I have commanded you: be strong and act like a man. Do not be cowardly, nor fear, because the Lord your God is with you in everything you may do.

**Joshua 1:10**

And Joshua commanded the scribes of the people, saying,

**Joshua 1:11**

Go through the midst of the camp of the people and command the people, saying, Prepare provisions, because in yet three days you cross this Jordan, entering to possess the land that the Lord God of your fathers gives you.

**Joshua 1:12**

And to Reuben and to Gad and to the half-tribe of Manasseh Joshua said,

**Joshua 1:13**

Remember the word that Moses, servant of the Lord, commanded you, saying, The Lord your God has given you rest and given you this land.

**Joshua 1:14**

Let your wives and your children and your cattle dwell in the land that he gave you, but you shall cross over well-armed before your brothers, every strong one, and you shall fight alongside them,

**Joshua 1:15**

until the Lord your God gives your brothers rest just as also to you, and they also inherit the land that the Lord our God gives them. And you shall go away, each one to his inheritance that Moses gave you beyond the Jordan from the sunrise.

**Joshua 1:16**

And answering Joshua they said, Everything that you command us we will do, and into every place where you send us we will go.

**Joshua 1:17**

According to everything that we listened to from Moses, we will listen to you. Only let the Lord our God be with you in the way he was with Moses.

**Joshua 1:18**

And the man whoever disobeys you and whoever does not listen to your words in whatever you command him, let him die. But be strong and act like a man.

### Chapter 2

**Joshua 2:1**

And Joshua son of Nun sent from Shittim two young men to spy, saying, Go up and see the land and Jericho. And going, the two young men entered into Jericho and entered into the house of a prostitute woman whose name was Rahab, and they lodged there.

**Joshua 2:2**

And it was reported to the king of Jericho, saying, Men from the sons of Israel have entered here to spy out the land.

**Joshua 2:3**

And the king of Jericho sent and said to Rahab, Bring out the men who entered into your house in the night, because they have come to spy out the land.

**Joshua 2:4**

And the woman, taking the men, hid them and said, The men did come to me,

**Joshua 2:5**

but when the gate was being shut in the dark, the men went out. I do not know where they have gone. Pursue after them, if you will overtake them.

**Joshua 2:6**

But she had brought them up to the roof and hid them in the flax stalks stacked for her on the roof.

**Joshua 2:7**

And the men pursued after them on the road by the Jordan to the crossings, and the gate was shut. And it happened, as those pursuing after them had gone out,

**Joshua 2:8**

that before the men lay down, she came up to the roof toward them

**Joshua 2:9**

and said to them, I know that the Lord has given you the land, for your fear has fallen on us,

**Joshua 2:10**

for we heard that the Lord God dried up the Red Sea from before your face when you came out from Egypt, and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon and Og, whom you utterly destroyed.

**Joshua 2:11**

And hearing, our heart was astonished, and spirit no longer stood in any of us before your face, because the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below.

**Joshua 2:12**

And now swear to me by the Lord God that as I do mercy to you, so you also will do mercy with the house of my father,

**Joshua 2:13**

and you will keep alive the house of my father and my mother and my brothers and all my house and everything that belongs to them, and you will rescue my life from death.

**Joshua 2:14**

And the men said to her, Our life for yours unto death. And she said, Whenever the Lord delivers the city to you, you shall do mercy and truth with me.

**Joshua 2:15**

And she let them down through the window.

**Joshua 2:16**

And she said to them, Go away into the hill country, lest those pursuing meet you, and hide yourselves there three days until those pursuing turn back from behind you, and after these things go away on your road.

**Joshua 2:17**

And the men said to her, We are guiltless from this oath of yours.

**Joshua 2:18**

Behold, when we enter into the city, this scarlet cord sign you shall bind in the window through which you brought us down through it, and your father and your mother and your brothers and all your father's house you shall gather to yourself into your house.

**Joshua 2:19**

And it shall be, everyone who may go out the door of your house outside shall be liable to himself, but we are guiltless of this oath of yours, and whoever may be with you in the house, we will be liable.

**Joshua 2:20**

And if anyone wrongs us or reveals these words of ours, we will be guiltless of this oath of yours.

**Joshua 2:21**

And she said to them, According to your word, so let it be. And she sent them away.

**Joshua 2:22**

And they went away and came to the hill country and remained there three days, and the pursuers searched all the roads and did not find them.

**Joshua 2:23**

And the two young men returned and came down from the mountain and crossed over to Joshua son of Nun and told him all the things that happened to them.

**Joshua 2:24**

And they said to Joshua, The Lord has delivered all the land into our hands, and every inhabitant of that land has cowered from before us.

**Joshua 3:1**

**Joshua 4:1**

And the people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth of the first month, and the sons of Israel encamped in Galgala at the part toward the sunrise from Jericho.

**Joshua 4:20**

**Joshua 4:21**

**Joshua 4:23**
