And the Lord left these nations so as not to remove them quickly, and he did not give them into the hand of Joshua.

### Chapter 3

**Judges 3:1**

And these are the nations Joshua left to test Israel by them, all who had not known all the wars of Canaan,

**Judges 3:2**

only for the generations of the sons of Israel, to teach them war, only those before them had not known them:

**Judges 3:3**

the five satrapies of the foreigners and all the Canaanite and the Sidonian and the Hivite dwelling on Lebanon from Mount Baal-hermon to Lobōēmath.

**Judges 3:4**

And it came to be in order to test Israel by them, to know whether they would listen to the commandments of the Lord that he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.

**Judges 3:5**

And the sons of Israel dwelt in the midst of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite,

**Judges 3:6**

and they took their daughters for themselves as wives and gave their daughters to their sons and served their gods.

**Judges 3:7**

And the sons of Israel did evil before the Lord and forgot the Lord their God and served the Baals and the groves.

**Judges 3:8**

And the Lord burned with anger against Israel and sold them into the hands of Chousarsathōm king of Syrian Mesopotamia, and they served him eight years.

**Judges 3:9**

And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, and the Lord raised up a savior for Israel and saved them, Gothoniēl son of Kenez, younger brother of Caleb, and he listened to him.

**Judges 3:10**

And the Spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he judged Israel and went out to war, and the Lord gave Chousarsathōm king of Syria into his hand, and his hand grew strong over Chousarsathōm.

**Judges 3:11**

And the land was at rest fifty years, and Gothoniēl son of Kenez died.

**Judges 3:12**

And the sons of Israel again added to do evil before the Lord, and the Lord strengthened Eglom king of Moab against Israel because they had done evil before the Lord.

**Judges 3:13**

And he brought to himself all the sons of Ammon and Amalek, and he went and struck Israel and inherited the City of Palms.

**Judges 3:14**

And the sons of Israel served Eglom king of Moab eighteen years.

**Judges 3:15**

And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, and the Lord raised up for them a savior, Aōd son of Gēra, son of the Jeminite, an ambidextrous man. And the sons of Israel sent gifts by his hand to Eglom king of Moab.

**Judges 3:16**

And Aōd made for himself a double-edged sword a span in length and girded it under his cloak on his right thigh.

**Judges 3:17**

And he brought the gifts to Eglom king of Moab, and Eglom was a very imposing man.

**Judges 3:18**

And it came to be, when Aōd finished presenting the gifts, he sent away those carrying the gifts.

**Judges 3:19**

And Eglom turned back from the carved images near Galgala, and Aōd said, I have a secret word for you, O king. And Eglom said, Silence, everyone out from my presence. And all those standing by him went out from him.

**Judges 3:20**

And Aōd went in to him, and he was sitting alone in his summer upper room. And Aōd said, I have a word of God for you, O king. And Eglom rose from the throne near him.

**Judges 3:21**

And it came to be, as he rose up, Aōd stretched out his left hand and took the sword from his right thigh and drove it into the belly of Eglom.

**Judges 3:22**

And indeed he drove in the hilt behind the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, because he did not pull the sword out of his belly.

**Judges 3:23**

And Aōd went out into the vestibule and shut the doors of the upper room upon him and locked them.

**Judges 3:24**

And he went out, and his servants came in and saw, and behold, the doors of the upper room were shut. And they said, Perhaps he is relieving himself in the private room of the bedchamber.

**Judges 3:25**

And they waited until they were ashamed, and behold, there was no one opening the doors of the upper room. And they took the key and opened them, and behold, their lord had fallen dead upon the ground.

**Judges 3:26**

And Aōd escaped while they were in confusion, and there was no one paying him heed, and he himself passed by the carved images and escaped to Seirōtha.

**Judges 3:27**

And it came to be when he arrived, he sounded a horn in the hill-country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel went down with him, and he was before them.

**Judges 3:28**

And he said to them, Come down after me, because the Lord God has given your enemies, Moab, into your hands. And they came down after him and seized the crossings of the Jordan of Moab and did not allow a man to cross over.

**Judges 3:29**

And they struck Moab at that time, about ten thousand men, every fighting man among them and every man of strength, and not a man escaped.

**Judges 3:30**

And Moab was put to shame on that day under the hand of Israel, and the land was at rest eighty years. And Aōd judged them until he died.

**Judges 3:31**

And after him arose Samegar son of Anath, and he struck the foreigners, six hundred men, apart from the calves of the cattle, and he too saved Israel.

### Chapter 4

**Judges 4:1**

And the sons of Israel again added to do evil before the Lord.

**Judges 4:2**

And the Lord sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Asor, and the commander of his force was Sisara, and he dwelt in Arisōth of the nations.

**Judges 4:3**

And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, because he had nine hundred iron chariots, and he oppressed Israel with force for twenty years.

**Judges 4:4**

And Debbōra, a woman prophet, wife of Lapidōth, she was judging Israel at that time.

**Judges 4:5**

And she sat under the palm of Debbōra between Rama and between Baethel in the hill-country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel went up to her there for judgment.

**Judges 4:6**

And Debbōra sent and called Barak son of Abineem from Kedes of Naphtali and said to him, Has not the Lord God of Israel commanded you? And you shall depart to Mount Thabor and take with yourself ten thousand men from the sons of Naphtali and from the sons of Zebulun.

**Judges 4:7**

And I will draw to you, to the torrent Kishōn, Sisara the commander of Jabin's force and his chariots and his multitude, and I will give him into your hand.

**Judges 4:8**

And Barak said to her, If you go with me, I will go, and if you do not go with me, I will not go, because I do not know the day in which the Lord prospers the angel with me.

**Judges 4:9**

And Debbōra said to him, Going, I will go with you. Only know that the advantage shall not be yours on the way by which you are going, because into a woman's hand the Lord will give Sisara. And Debbōra rose and went with Barak to Kedes.

**Judges 4:10**

And Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedes, and ten thousand men went up at his feet, and Debbōra went up with him.

**Judges 4:11**

And those near the Kenite had separated from the sons of Jōbab, son-in-law of Moses, and he pitched his tent by the oak of those resting, which is near Kedes.

**Judges 4:12**

And they reported to Sisara that Barak son of Abineem had gone up to Mount Thabor.

**Judges 4:13**

And Sisara called together all his chariots, because he had nine hundred iron chariots, and all the people with him, from Arisōth of the nations to the torrent Kishōn.

**Judges 4:14**

And Debbōra said to Barak, Rise up, because this is the day in which the Lord has given Sisara into your hand. Look, the Lord will go out before you. And Barak went down from Mount Thabor, and ten thousand men after him.

**Judges 4:15**

And the Lord threw Sisara and all his chariots and all his camp into confusion by the edge of the sword before Barak, and Sisara came down from his chariot and fled on his feet.

**Judges 4:16**

And Barak pursued after the chariots and after the camp as far as the oak grove of the nations, and all the camp of Sisara fell by the edge of the sword; not even one was left.

**Judges 4:17**

And Sisara withdrew on his feet to the tent of Jaēl, wife of Chaber the Kenite, because there was peace between Jabin king of Asor and the house of Chaber the Kenite.

**Judges 4:18**

And Jaēl went out to meet Sisara and said to him, Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me, do not fear. And he turned aside to her into the tent, and she covered him with her cloak.

**Judges 4:19**

And Sisara said to her, Give me to drink a little water, because I thirsted. And she opened the skin of milk and gave him drink and covered his face.

**Judges 4:20**

And he said to her, Stand at the door of the tent, and it shall be, if someone comes to you and asks you and says to you, Is there a man here? you shall say, There is not. And she covered him with her cloak.

**Judges 4:21**

And Jaēl wife of Chaber took the tent peg and put the hammer in her hand and came in to him quietly and drove the peg into his jaw and it went through into the ground. And he writhed between her knees and breathed out and died.

**Judges 4:22**

And behold, Barak was pursuing Sisara, and Jaēl went out to meet him and said to him, Come, and I will show you the man whom you seek. And he went in to her, and behold, Sisara had fallen dead, and the peg was in his jaw.

**Judges 4:23**

And God humbled Jabin king of Canaan on that day before the sons of Israel.

**Judges 4:24**

And the hand of the sons of Israel went on, going and hardening against Jabin king of Canaan, until they destroyed him.

### Chapter 5

**Judges 5:1**

And Debbōra sang, and Barak son of Abineem, on that day, and said,

**Judges 5:2**

When leaders began in Israel, in the willing offering of the people, bless the Lord.

**Judges 5:3**

Hear, kings; give ear, satraps. I will sing to the Lord; I will make melody to the God of Israel.

**Judges 5:4**

Lord, in your going out from Seir, in your marching from the field of Edom, earth shook, and heaven was shaken, and the clouds dripped water.

**Judges 5:5**

Mountains were shaken from before the Lord, this Sinai, from before the Lord God of Israel.

**Judges 5:6**

In the days of Samegar son of Anath, in the days of Jaēl, kings ceased, and ways went on twisted roads.

**Judges 5:7**

Rule ceased in Israel, it ceased until Debbōra arose, because a mother arose in Israel.

**Judges 5:8**

They chose new gods, like barley bread. A shield, if I should see, or spear among forty thousand?

**Judges 5:9**

My heart is toward the appointed ones of Israel, the mighty ones of the people. Bless the Lord.

**Judges 5:10**

You who ride on beasts of burden, you who sit on carpets,

**Judges 5:11**

sound forth the voice of those striking up among rejoicing ones. There they will give righteousness to the Lord; the righteous ones were strengthened in Israel. Then the people of the Lord went down to his cities.

**Judges 5:12**

Awake, awake, Debbōra. Awaken myriads with the people. Awake, awake, speak with song. Strengthening one, rise up, Barak, and strengthen, Debbōra, Barak. Take captive your captivity, son of Abineem.

**Judges 5:13**

Then his strength was magnified. Lord, humble for me my stronger ones.

**Judges 5:14**

The people of Ephraim punished them in the valley. Benjamin, your brother, among your peoples. From me, Machir came down, searching out, and from Zebulun the Lord fought for me among mighty ones, from there with the scepter of strengthening leadership.

**Judges 5:15**

In Issachar with Debbōra he sent his footmen into the valley. Why do you dwell between the lips? He stretched out at his feet. In the divisions of Reuben were great searchings of heart.

**Judges 5:16**

Why do you sit among the sheepfolds, to hear the whistlings of those stirring up to pass through? In the matters of Reuben were great searchings of heart.

**Judges 5:17**

Gilead camped beyond the Jordan, and Dan, why does he dwell among ships? Asher settled by the seashore and camped by his inlets.

**Judges 5:18**

Zebulun, a people that reproached its soul to death, and Naphtalim on the heights of the field.

**Judges 5:19**

Kings came and arrayed themselves, then the kings of Canaan fought at Thennach by the water of Mageddō. They took no gain of silver.

**Judges 5:20**

From heaven stars fought; from their order they fought with Sisara.

**Judges 5:21**

The torrent Kishōn swept them away, torrent of former days, torrent Kishōn. My soul, you shall trample the mighty.

**Judges 5:22**

Then the heels of the horse were cut off by the prancings of his mighty ones.

**Judges 5:23**

Curse Marōz, said the angel of the Lord; with a curse curse its inhabitants, because they did not come to the help of the Lord. The Lord is our helper, mighty in warriors.

**Judges 5:24**

Blessed among women be Jaēl, wife of Chaber the Kenite; among women in the tent let her be blessed.

**Judges 5:25**

He asked water of her, and she gave him milk. In a bowl of the mighty she brought him butter.

**Judges 5:26**

Her left hand she stretched to the peg, and her right hand to the work of laborers, and she struck Sisara, she shattered his head and crushed and pierced through his jaw.

**Judges 5:27**

Between her feet, bending down, he fell; he slept between her feet. Where he bent down, there he fell, exhausted.

**Judges 5:28**

Through the window the mother of Sisara leaned out, looking through the lattice at those returning with Sisara. Why has his chariot delayed to come? Why have the tracks of his chariots tarried?

**Judges 5:29**

Wise women of her princesses answered her, and she answered in her own words,

**Judges 5:30**

Will they not find him dividing spoil, making friends for friends? A spoil of dyed cloths for the head of a mighty man, spoil of dyed cloths of variegated embroidery, dyed embroidered things around his neck, spoil.

**Judges 5:31**

So let all your enemies perish, O Lord, but those loving him are as the rising of the sun in his might. And the land was at rest forty years.

### Chapter 6

**Judges 6:1**

And the sons of Israel did evil before the Lord, and the Lord gave them into the hand of Midian seven years.

**Judges 6:2**

And the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel, and the sons of Israel made for themselves, because of Midian, hideouts in the mountains and caves and strongholds.

**Judges 6:3**

And it happened when a man of Israel sowed, Midian and Amalek and the sons of the east would come up against him.

**Judges 6:4**

And they would encamp against them and destroy the produce of the land as far as Gaza, and they would leave no sustenance of life in Israel, and no sheep and no calf and no donkey.

**Judges 6:5**

For they and their cattle came up, and they carried their tents and came like locusts for multitude, and there was no number for them or for their camels, and they came into the land of Israel to ruin it.

**Judges 6:6**

And Israel became very poor before Midian, and the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord.

**Judges 6:7**

And it came to be, when the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord because of Midian,

**Judges 6:8**

that the Lord sent a man, a prophet, to the sons of Israel and said to them, Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I am the one who brought you up out of Egypt and brought you out of the house of slavery.

**Judges 6:9**

And I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all oppressing you, and I drove them out from before you and gave you their land.

**Judges 6:10**

And I said to you, I am the Lord your God. You shall not fear the gods of the Amorite among whom you dwell in their land, and you did not listen to my voice.

**Judges 6:11**

And an angel of the Lord came and sat under the oak that was in Ephratha, that belonged to Jōas father of Abiezri, and Gideon his son was beating out wheat in a winepress to escape from before Midian.

**Judges 6:12**

And an angel of the Lord appeared to him and said to him, The Lord is with you, mighty in strength.

**Judges 6:13**

And Gideon said to him, In me, my lord? And if the Lord is with us, why have all these evils found us, and where are all his wonders that our fathers recounted to us, saying, Did not the Lord bring us up out of Egypt? But now he has cast us off and given us into the hand of Midian.

**Judges 6:14**

And the angel of the Lord looked upon him and said to him, Go in your strength, and you shall save Israel. See, I have sent you.

**Judges 6:15**

And Gideon said to him, In me, my lord? By what shall I save Israel? Behold, my thousand is the humblest in Manasseh, and I am small in my father's house.

**Judges 6:16**

And the angel of the Lord said to him, The Lord will be with you, and you will strike Midian as one man.

**Judges 6:17**

And Gideon said to him, If I found favor in your eyes, then do for me a sign that you are the one speaking with me.

**Judges 6:18**

Do not move from here until I come to you and bring out my sacrifice and set it before you. And he said, I am; I will stay until you return.

**Judges 6:19**

And Gideon went in and made a kid of the goats and unleavened loaves from an ephah of flour, and he put the meat in the basket and poured the broth into the pot, and he brought them out to him under the oak and bowed down.

**Judges 6:20**

And the angel of the Lord said to him, Take the meat and the unleavened loaves and lay them on that rock, and pour out the broth. And he did so.

**Judges 6:21**

And the angel of the Lord stretched out the tip of the staff in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened loaves, and fire sprang up from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened loaves, and the angel of the Lord departed from his sight.

**Judges 6:22**

And Gideon saw that he was an angel of the Lord and said, Ah, Lord, Lord, because I saw the angel of the Lord face to face.

**Judges 6:23**

And the Lord said to him, Peace to you. Do not fear; you shall not die.

**Judges 6:24**

And Gideon built there an altar to the Lord and called it Peace of the Lord. Until this day it still stands in Ephratha of the father of Ezri.

**Judges 6:25**

And it came to be that night that the Lord said to him, Take your father's fatted calf, the seven-year-old bull, and pull down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the grove upon it.

**Judges 6:26**

And you shall build an altar to the Lord your God, who appeared to you, on the top of this stronghold mountain in the arrangement, and you shall take the bull and offer a whole burnt offering with the wood of the grove that you cut down.

**Judges 6:27**

And Gideon took ten and three men from among his servants and did as the Lord spoke to him. And it came to be, because he feared his father's house and the men of the city, not to do it by day, he did it by night.

**Judges 6:28**

And the men of the city rose early in the morning, and behold, the altar of Baal had been dug down and the grove upon it had been cut down, and the fatted bull had been offered as a whole burnt offering on the altar that had been built.

**Judges 6:29**

And each man said to his neighbor, Who did this thing? And they searched and inquired and said, Gideon son of Jōas did this thing.

**Judges 6:30**

And the men of the city said to Jōas, Bring out your son and let him die, because he dug down the altar of Baal and because he cut down the grove upon it.

**Judges 6:31**

And Jōas said to the men standing against him, Will you now judge on behalf of Baal, or will you save him? Whoever pleads his case shall die by morning. If he is a god, let him avenge himself, because his altar was dug down.

**Judges 6:32**

And on that day he called him Tribunal of Baal, because he dug down his altar.

**Judges 6:33**

And all Midian and Amalek and the sons of the east gathered together, and they crossed over and encamped in the valley of Jezrael.

**Judges 6:34**

And the Spirit of God clothed Gideon, and he sounded the horn, and Abiezer cried out after him.

**Judges 6:35**

And he sent messengers through all Manasseh, and it also cried out after him, and he sent messengers in Asher and in Zebulun and in Naphtali, and they went up to meet him.

**Judges 6:36**

And Gideon said to God, If you are saving Israel by my hand, just as you said,

**Judges 6:37**

behold, I lay the fleece of wool on the threshing floor, and if dew comes upon the fleece alone and drought upon all the land, then I will know that you are saving Israel by my hand, just as you said.

**Judges 6:38**

And it happened so, and Gideon rose early the next day and squeezed the fleece, and the dew ran out of the fleece, a bowl full of water.

**Judges 6:39**

And Gideon said to God, Let not your anger burn in me, and let me speak once more. Let me test once more with the fleece. Let there be drought upon the fleece alone, but upon all the land let there be dew.

**Judges 6:40**

And God did so in that night, and there was drought upon the fleece alone, but upon all the land there was dew.

### Chapter 7

**Judges 7:1**

And Jerobaal, that is Gideon, rose early, and all the people with him, and encamped upon the land of Arōed, and the camp of Midian and Amalek was to his north, from the hill of Abōr in the valley.

**Judges 7:2**

And the Lord said to Gideon, The people with you are too many for me to give Midian into their hand, lest Israel boast against me, saying, My hand saved me.

**Judges 7:3**

And the Lord said to him, Speak now in the ears of the people, saying, Whoever is fearful and afraid, let him turn back. And twenty-two thousand turned back from the people, and ten thousand were left.

**Judges 7:4**

And the Lord said to Gideon, The people are still many. Bring them down to the water, and there I will test them for you, and it shall be that whoever I say to you, This one shall go with you, he shall go with you, and whoever I say to you, This one shall not go with you, he shall not go with you.

**Judges 7:5**

And he brought the people down to the water. And the Lord said to Gideon, Everyone who laps with his tongue from the water, as a dog laps, you shall set him apart by himself; and everyone who bends on his knees to drink, you shall place by himself.

**Judges 7:6**

And the number of those lapping with their tongues came to three hundred men, and all the rest of the people bent on their knees to drink water.

**Judges 7:7**

And the Lord said to Gideon, By the three hundred men who lapped I will save you and deliver Midian into your hand, and let all the people turn back, each man to his place.

**Judges 7:8**

And they took the food of the people in their hands and their horns, and he sent every man of Israel away, each to his tent, but the three hundred men he kept. And the camp of Midian was beneath him in the valley.

**Judges 7:9**

And it came to be in that night that the Lord said to him, Rise, go down from here into the camp, because I have given it into your hand.

**Judges 7:10**

But if you fear to go down, go down, you and Phara your servant, into the camp,

**Judges 7:11**

and you will hear what they are saying, and after these things your hands will be strengthened, and you will go down into the camp. And he went down, he and Phara his servant, to the edge of the fifty in the camp.

**Judges 7:12**

And Midian and Amalek and all the sons of the east were camped in the valley like locusts in multitude, and their camels had no number, but were like the sand on the lip of the sea in multitude.

**Judges 7:13**

And Gideon came, and behold, a man was recounting a dream to his neighbor and said, Behold, the dream that I dreamed: behold, a cake of barley bread rolling into the camp of Midian, and it came as far as the tent of Midian and struck it and overturned it, and the tent fell.

**Judges 7:14**

And his neighbor answered and said, This is nothing else than the sword of Gideon son of Jōas, a man of Israel. The Lord has given Midian and all the camp into his hand.

**Judges 7:15**

And it came to be, when Gideon heard the recounting of the dream and its interpretation, he bowed down to the Lord and returned to the camp of Israel and said, Rise up, because the Lord has given the camp of Midian into your hands.

**Judges 7:16**

And he divided the three hundred men into three companies and gave horns into the hands of all of them and empty jars and torches in the midst of the jars.

**Judges 7:17**

And he said to them, You shall watch from me, and thus you shall do. Behold, I am entering into the midst of the camp, and it shall be, as I do, so you shall do.

**Judges 7:18**

And I will sound the horn, I and all those with me, and you also shall sound the horns all around the camp and say, For the Lord and for Gideon.

**Judges 7:19**

And Gideon went in, and the hundred men with him, into the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just as they had roused the watchmen, and they sounded the horns and smashed the jars in their hands.

**Judges 7:20**

And the three companies sounded with the horns and shattered the jars, and they held in their left hand the torches and in their right hand the horns for sounding, and they cried, Sword for the Lord and for Gideon.

**Judges 7:21**

And each stood in his place all around the camp, and all the camp ran and gave a signal and fled.

**Judges 7:22**

And the three hundred horns sounded, and the Lord set each man's sword against his neighbor and throughout all the camp, and the camp fled as far as Bethaseitta, gathered as far as the border of Abelmeoula and toward Tabath.

**Judges 7:23**

And a man of Israel from Naphtali and from Asher and from all Manasseh cried out, and they pursued after Midian.

**Judges 7:24**

And Gideon sent messengers through all the hill-country of Ephraim, saying, Come down to meet Midian, and seize the waters for yourselves as far as Bethbera and the Jordan. And every man of Ephraim cried out and seized the waters as far as Bethbera and the Jordan.

**Judges 7:25**

And they captured the two leaders of Midian, Ōrēb and Zēb, and they killed Ōrēb at Sourin, and they killed Zēb at Jakephzēb, and they pursued Midian, and the head of Ōrēb and Zēb they brought to Gideon from beyond the Jordan.

### Chapter 8

**Judges 8:1**

And a man of Ephraim said to him, What is this thing you did to us, not calling us when you went out to fight against Midian? And they contended with him strongly.

**Judges 8:2**

And he said to them, What have I done now like you? Is not the gleaning of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer?

**Judges 8:3**

Into your hand the Lord gave the leaders of Midian, Ōrēb and Zēb. And what was I able to do like you? Then their spirit toward him relaxed when he spoke this word.

**Judges 8:4**

And Gideon came to the Jordan and crossed over, he and the three hundred men with him, faint in soul and hungry.

**Judges 8:5**

And he said to the men of Sokchōth, Give now loaves to the people with me, because they are hungry, and I am pursuing after Zēbee and Salmana, kings of Midian.

**Judges 8:6**

And the leaders of Sokchōth said, Is the hand of Zēbee and Salmana now in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?

**Judges 8:7**

And Gideon said, Not so. When the Lord gives Zēbee and Salmana into my hand, I will thresh your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with the barkonnim.

**Judges 8:8**

And he went up from there to Phanouēl and spoke to them in the same way, and the men of Phanouēl answered him just as the men of Sokchōth answered him.

**Judges 8:9**

And he said to the men of Phanouēl, saying, When I return in peace, I will dig down this tower.

**Judges 8:10**

And Zēbee and Salmana were in Karkar, and their camp with them was about fifteen thousand, those left in all the camp of the sons of the east, and those fallen were one hundred twenty thousand men drawing sword.

**Judges 8:11**

And Gideon went up by the way of those dwelling in tents east of Nabeth, opposite Zēbee, and struck the camp, and the camp was confident.

**Judges 8:12**

And Zēbee and Salmana fled, and he pursued after them and seized the two kings of Midian, Zēbee and Salmana, and crushed all their camp.

**Judges 8:13**

And Gideon son of Jōas returned from the war by the ascent of Ares.

**Judges 8:14**

And he captured a young servant from the men of Sokchōth and questioned him, and he wrote down for him the leaders of Sokchōth and its elders, seventy-seven men.

**Judges 8:15**

And Gideon came to the leaders of Sokchōth and said to them, Behold, Zēbee and Salmana, about whom you reproached me, saying, Is the hand of Zēbee and Salmana now in your hand, that we should give loaves to your exhausted men?

**Judges 8:16**

And he took the leaders and the elders of the city and threshed them with the thorns of the wilderness and the bramble bushes, and with them he threshed the men of Sokchōth.

**Judges 8:17**

And he dug down the tower of Phanouēl and killed the men of the city.

**Judges 8:18**

And he said to Zēbee and Salmana, Where are the men whom you killed at Thabor? And they said, As you are, so were they, like the appearance, the form, of sons of kings.

**Judges 8:19**

And Gideon said, They are my brothers and sons of my mother. As the Lord lives, if you had kept them alive, I would not kill you.

**Judges 8:20**

And he said to Jether his firstborn, Rise, kill them. But the young man did not draw his sword, because he was afraid, because he was younger.

**Judges 8:21**

And Zēbee and Salmana said, Rise yourself and fall upon us, because as the man is, so is his strength. And Gideon rose and killed Zēbee and Salmana and took the crescents that were on the necks of their camels.

**Judges 8:22**

And a man of Israel said to Gideon, Rule over us, you and your sons, because you saved us from the hand of Midian.

**Judges 8:23**

And Gideon said to them, I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you; the Lord will rule over you.

**Judges 8:24**

And Gideon said to them, I will ask from you a request, and give me, each man, an earring from his spoil, because they had many gold earrings, for they were Ishmaelites.

**Judges 8:25**

And they said, Giving, we will give. And he spread out his garment, and there each man threw a gold earring from his spoil.

**Judges 8:26**

And the weight of the gold earrings that he requested came to one thousand seven hundred shekels of gold, apart from the little moons and the necklaces and the purple garments that were upon the kings of Midian, and apart from the gold collars that were on the necks of their camels.

**Judges 8:27**

And Gideon made it into an ephod and set it in his city in Ephratha, and all Israel prostituted themselves after it there, and it became for Gideon and for his house as a snare.

**Judges 8:28**

And Midian was put to shame before the sons of Israel, and they no longer lifted up their head, and the land was at rest forty years in the days of Gideon.

**Judges 8:29**

And Jerobaal son of Jōas went and dwelt in his house.

**Judges 8:30**

And Gideon had seventy sons coming out from his loins, because he had many wives.

**Judges 8:31**

And his concubine who was in Sikimois also bore him a son, and he set his name Abimelech.

**Judges 8:32**

And Gideon son of Jōas died in a good old age and was buried in the tomb of Jōas his father in Ephratha of the father of Abiezri.

**Judges 8:33**

And it came to be, when Gideon died, the sons of Israel turned back and prostituted themselves after the Baals and made Baal-berith their covenant, for him to be a god to them.

**Judges 8:34**

And the sons of Israel did not remember the Lord their God, the one who delivered them from the hand of all their enemies all around.

**Judges 8:35**

And they did not show mercy with the house of Jerobaal Gideon according to all the goodness that he did with Israel.

### Chapter 9

**Judges 9:1**

And Abimelech son of Jerobaal went to Sikima to the brothers of his mother and spoke to them and to all the kin of his mother's house, saying,

**Judges 9:2**

Speak now in the ears of the men of Sikima, Which is better, that seventy men, all the sons of Jerobaal, rule over you, or that one man rule over you? And remember that I am your flesh and your bone.

**Judges 9:3**

And his mother's brothers spoke concerning him in the ears of all the men of Sikima all these words, and their heart inclined after Abimelech, because they said, He is our brother.

**Judges 9:4**

And they gave him seventy silver pieces from the house of Baal-covenant, and with them Abimelech hired empty and stunned men, and they went after him.

**Judges 9:5**

And he entered into his father's house at Ephratha and killed his brothers, the sons of Jerobaal, seventy men, on one stone. And Jōatham, the youngest son of Jerobaal, was left, because he hid himself.

**Judges 9:6**

And all the men of Sikima and all the house of Maallōn were gathered together, and they went and made Abimelech king by the oak of the standing place in Sikimois.

**Judges 9:7**

And they reported it to Jōatham, and he went and stood on the top of Mount Garizin and lifted up his voice and cried out and said to them, Hear me, men of Sikima, and may God hear you.

**Judges 9:8**

Going, the trees went to anoint for themselves a king, and they said to the olive tree, Reign over us.

**Judges 9:9**

And the olive tree said to them, Shall I leave my fatness, by which God and men are glorified in me, and go to rule the trees?

**Judges 9:10**

And the trees said to the fig tree, Come, reign over us.

**Judges 9:11**

And the fig tree said to them, Shall I leave my sweetness and my good produce and go to rule over trees?

**Judges 9:12**

And the trees said to the vine, Come, reign over us.

**Judges 9:13**

And the vine said to them, Shall I leave my wine, the gladness from God of men, and go to rule trees?

**Judges 9:14**

And the trees said to the thorn bush, Come, you reign over us.

**Judges 9:15**

And the thorn bush said to the trees, If in truth you anoint me as king over you, come and trust in my shade, but if not, let fire come out from the thorn bush and consume the cedars of Lebanon.

**Judges 9:16**

And now, if in truth and in perfection you acted and made Abimelech king, and if you acted well with Jerobaal and with his house, and if you acted toward him according to the repayment of his hand,

**Judges 9:17**

as my father fought for you and cast his life in front and delivered you from the hand of Midian,

**Judges 9:18**

but you rose up against my father's house today and killed his sons, seventy men, on one stone, and made Abimelech, son of his maidservant, king over the men of Sikima because he is your brother,

**Judges 9:19**

then if in truth and perfection you acted with Jerobaal and with his house on this day, may you be blessed, and rejoice in Abimelech, and may he also rejoice in you.

**Judges 9:20**

But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and consume the men of Sikima and the house of Maallōn, and if not, let fire come out from the men of Sikima and from the house of Maallōn and consume Abimelech.

**Judges 9:21**

And Jōatham ran away and went on the road and fled to Rara and dwelt there away from the face of Abimelech his brother.

**Judges 9:22**

And Abimelech ruled over Israel three years.

**Judges 9:23**

And God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and between the men of Sikima, and the men of Sikima acted treacherously in the house of Abimelech,

**Judges 9:24**

to bring the injustice of the seventy sons of Jerobaal and to lay their blood upon Abimelech their brother who killed them, and upon the men of Sikima who strengthened his hands so as to kill his brothers.

**Judges 9:25**

And the men of Sikima set an ambush for him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed all who passed by them on the road, and it was reported to Abimelech.

**Judges 9:26**

And Gaal son of Abed came, and his brothers, into Sikima, and the men of Sikima trusted in him.

**Judges 9:27**

And they went out into the field and gathered the grapes of their vineyards and trod them and made dances and entered the house of their god and ate and drank and cursed Abimelech.

**Judges 9:28**

And Gaal son of Abed said, What is Abimelech, and who is the son of Sychem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerobaal, and Zeboul his overseer, his servant with the men of Emmōr father of Sychem? And why should we serve him?

**Judges 9:29**

And if someone would give this people into my hand, then I would remove Abimelech, and I would say to Abimelech, Increase your force and come out.

**Judges 9:30**

And Zeboul the ruler of the city heard the words of Gaal son of Abed and his anger burned.

**Judges 9:31**

And he sent messengers to Abimelech with gifts, saying, Behold, Gaal son of Abed and his brothers have arrived in Sikima, and behold, they are besieging the city against you.

**Judges 9:32**

And now rise by night, you and the people with you, and lie in ambush in the field.

**Judges 9:33**

And it shall be in the morning, with the sun rising, you shall rise early and spread out against the city, and behold, he and the people with him are coming out to you, and you shall do to him just as your hand finds.

**Judges 9:34**

And Abimelech rose, and all the people with him, by night, and they lay in ambush against Sikima in four companies.

**Judges 9:35**

And it came to be in the morning, Gaal son of Abed went out and stood at the doorway of the city gate, and Abimelech rose, and the people with him, out of the ambushes.

**Judges 9:36**

And Gaal son of Abed saw the people and said to Zeboul, Behold, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains. And Zeboul said to him, You are seeing the shadow of the mountains as men.

**Judges 9:37**

And Gaal continued yet to speak and said, Behold, people are coming down by the sea from near the navel of the land, and one company is coming by way of the oak of the lookouts.

**Judges 9:38**

And Zeboul said to him, Where is your mouth now, the one saying, Who is Abimelech that we should serve him? Behold, this is the people whom you despised. Go out now and fight against him.

**Judges 9:39**

And Gaal went out before the men of Sikima and fought against Abimelech.

**Judges 9:40**

And Abimelech pursued him, and he fled from before him, and many wounded fell as far as the doors of the city.

**Judges 9:41**

And Abimelech sat in Arima, and Zeboul drove out Gaal and his brothers from dwelling in Sikimois.

**Judges 9:42**

And it came to be the next day, the people went out into the plain, and it was reported to Abimelech.

**Judges 9:43**

And he took the people and divided it into three companies and lay in ambush in it, and he saw, and behold, the people were coming out of the city, and he rose up against them and struck them.

**Judges 9:44**

And Abimelech and the companies with him spread out and stood by the gate of the city, and the two companies rushed upon all who were in the field and struck them.

**Judges 9:45**

And Abimelech fought against the city all that day and took the city, and he killed the people in it and tore down the city and sowed it with salt.

**Judges 9:46**

And all the men of the tower of Sikima heard, and they entered into the stronghold of the house of Baal-covenant.

**Judges 9:47**

And it was reported to Abimelech that all the men of the tower of Sikima had gathered together.

**Judges 9:48**

And Abimelech went up to Mount Selmōn, he and all the people with him, and Abimelech took an axe in his hand and cut a load of wood and took it and put it on his shoulders and said to the people with him, What you saw me doing, quickly do as I also did.

**Judges 9:49**

And they also each cut a load and took it and went after Abimelech and put it against the stronghold and burned the stronghold upon them with fire, and all the men of the tower of Sikima died, about a thousand men and women.

**Judges 9:50**

And Abimelech went to Thebes and encamped against it and seized it first.

**Judges 9:51**

And there was a strong tower in the midst of the city, and all the men and women and all the leaders of the city fled there and shut themselves in and went up to the roof of the tower.

**Judges 9:52**

And Abimelech came as far as the tower and made war against it, and Abimelech came near the door of the tower to burn it with fire.

**Judges 9:53**

And one woman threw a fragment of millstone upon the head of Abimelech and shattered his skull.

**Judges 9:54**

And he quickly called to the young man carrying his armor and said to him, Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say, A woman killed him. And his young man pierced him through, and Abimelech died.

**Judges 9:55**

And the men of Israel saw that Abimelech had died, and each man went to his place.

**Judges 9:56**

And God returned the evil of Abimelech that he did to his father in killing his seventy brothers.

**Judges 9:57**

And all the evil of the men of Sikima God returned upon their head, and the curse of Jōatham son of Jerobaal came upon them.

### Chapter 10

**Judges 10:1**

And after Abimelech there arose to save Israel Thōla son of Phoua, son of his father's brother, a man of Issachar, and he dwelt in Samaria in the hill-country of Ephraim.

**Judges 10:2**

And he judged Israel twenty-three years, and he died and was buried in Samaria.

**Judges 10:3**

And after him arose Jair the Gileadite, and he judged Israel twenty-two years.

**Judges 10:4**

And there were to him thirty-two sons riding on thirty-two foals, and thirty-two cities belonged to them, and he called them Villages of Jair until this day; they are in the land of Gilead.

**Judges 10:5**

And Jair died and was buried in Rammō.

**Judges 10:6**

And the sons of Israel again added to do evil before the Lord, and they served the Baals and the Astarōths and the gods of Sidon and the gods of Moab and the gods of the sons of Ammon and the gods of the foreigners, and they forsook the Lord and did not serve him.

**Judges 10:7**

And the anger of the Lord burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of foreigners and into the hand of the sons of Ammon.

**Judges 10:8**

And they crushed and oppressed the sons of Israel in that year, eighteen years, all the sons of Israel beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorite in Gileaditis.

**Judges 10:9**

And the sons of Ammon crossed the Jordan to make war also in Judah and Benjamin and in the house of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel were greatly oppressed.

**Judges 10:10**

And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, saying, We sinned against you because we forsook our God and served the Baals.

**Judges 10:11**

And the Lord said to the sons of Israel, Was it not the Egyptians and the Amorites and the sons of Ammon and Moab and the foreigners

**Judges 10:12**

and Sidonians and Midian and Amalek who oppressed you? And you cried out to me, and I saved you from their hand.

**Judges 10:13**

Yet you forsook me and served other gods; therefore I will not continue to save you.

**Judges 10:14**

Go and cry out to the gods you chose for yourselves, and let them save you in the time of your distress.

**Judges 10:15**

And the sons of Israel said to the Lord, We sinned. Do to us according to all that is pleasing before you; only, Lord, deliver us in this day.

**Judges 10:16**

And they removed the foreign gods from their midst and served the Lord. And it was not pleasing in the people, and he grew short of soul in the toil of Israel.

**Judges 10:17**

And the sons of Ammon went up and encamped in Gilead, and the sons of Israel went out and encamped in Massēpha.

**Judges 10:18**

And the leaders of the people of Gilead said, each man to his neighbor, Who is the man that will begin to fight against the sons of Ammon? He shall be head over all dwelling in Gilead.

### Chapter 11

**Judges 11:1**

And Jephthae the Gileadite was mighty in strength, and he was the son of a prostitute woman, and Gilead fathered Jephthae.

**Judges 11:2**

And the wife of Gilead bore sons to him, and the sons of the wife grew up and cast out Jephthae and said to him, You shall not inherit in the house of our father, because you are the son of another woman.

**Judges 11:3**

And Jephthae fled from before his brothers and dwelt in the land of Tōb, and idle men gathered to Jephthae and went out with him.

**Judges 11:4**

And it came to be after days that the sons of Ammon made war with Israel.

**Judges 11:5**

And it came to be when the sons of Ammon were making war with Israel, the elders of Gilead went to take Jephthae from the land of Tōb.

**Judges 11:6**

And they said to Jephthae, Come and be for us as leader, and let us fight against the sons of Ammon.

**Judges 11:7**

And Jephthae said to the elders of Gilead, Was it not you who hated me and cast me out from my father's house and sent me away from you? And why have you now come to me when you are in distress?

**Judges 11:8**

And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthae, Not so now; we have come to you, and you shall go with us, and we shall fight against the sons of Ammon, and you shall be for us as head over all dwelling in Gilead.

**Judges 11:9**

And Jephthae said to the elders of Gilead, If you turn me back to fight against the sons of Ammon, and the Lord delivers them before me, I will be head for you.

**Judges 11:10**

And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthae, The Lord shall be the one hearing between us if we do not do according to your word.

**Judges 11:11**

And Jephthae went with the elders of Gilead, and they placed him over them as head, as leader, and Jephthae spoke all his words before the Lord in Massēpha.

**Judges 11:12**

And Jephthae sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon, saying, What is to me and to you, that you came against me to fight me in my land?

**Judges 11:13**

And the king of the sons of Ammon said to the messengers of Jephthae, Because Israel took my land in its going up out of Egypt, from Arnon to Jabbok and to the Jordan, and now return them in peace.

**Judges 11:14**

And the messengers turned back to Jephthae, and Jephthae again sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon,

**Judges 11:15**

saying, Thus says Jephthae: Israel did not take the land of Moab and the land of the sons of Ammon.

**Judges 11:16**

For in their going up from Egypt, Israel went in the wilderness as far as the Red Sea and came as far as Kades.

**Judges 11:17**

And Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, I will pass through your land, and the king of Edom did not listen. And indeed he sent also to the king of Moab, and he was not willing, and Israel stayed at Kades.

**Judges 11:18**

And it passed through in the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab and came on the east side of the land of Moab, and they encamped beyond the Arnon, and they did not enter the border of Moab, because Arnon was the border of Moab.

**Judges 11:19**

And Israel sent messengers to Sēōn king of Hesebon the Amorite and said to him, Israel will pass through your land to my place.

**Judges 11:20**

And Sēōn was not willing for Israel to pass through his borders, and Sēōn gathered all his people and encamped at Jassa and made war with Israel.

**Judges 11:21**

And the Lord God of Israel gave Sēōn and all his people into the hand of Israel, and he struck them. And Israel inherited all the land of the Amorite dwelling in the land.

**Judges 11:22**

And it inherited all the border of the Amorite from Arnon to Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.

**Judges 11:23**

And now the Lord God of Israel removed the Amorite from before his people Israel, and will you inherit it against him?

**Judges 11:24**

Will you not inherit whatever Chamos your god caused you to inherit? And all that the Lord our God inherited from before us, these things we will inherit.

**Judges 11:25**

And now are you at all better than Balak son of Sepphor, king of Moab? Did he by fighting fight with Israel, or by warring war against them?

**Judges 11:26**

While Israel dwelt in Hesebon and in its daughters and in Jazēr and in its daughters and in all the cities beside the Jordan three hundred years, why did they not rescue them at that time?

**Judges 11:27**

And I have not sinned against you, but you are doing evil with me by fighting against me. Let the Lord, the judge, judge today between the sons of Israel and between the sons of Ammon.

**Judges 11:28**

And the king of the sons of Ammon did not listen to the words of Jephthae that he sent to him.

**Judges 11:29**

And the Spirit of the Lord came upon Jephthae, and he passed through the land of Gilead and Manasseh and passed through the watchtower of Gilead, and from the watchtower of Gilead to the far side of the sons of Ammon.

**Judges 11:30**

And Jephthae vowed a vow to the Lord and said, If indeed you deliver the sons of Ammon into my hand,

**Judges 11:31**

then it shall be that whoever comes out from the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the sons of Ammon, that one shall be the Lord's, and I will offer him up as a whole burnt offering.

**Judges 11:32**

And Jephthae crossed over to the sons of Ammon to fight against them, and the Lord gave them into his hand.

**Judges 11:33**

And he struck them from Aroēr and until one comes to Semōith, twenty cities, and as far as Abel of vineyards, a very great blow, and the sons of Ammon were put to shame from before the sons of Israel.

**Judges 11:34**

And Jephthae came to Massēpha, to his house, and behold, his daughter was coming out to meet him with tambourines and dances, and she was his only child, beloved, and besides her he had neither son nor daughter.

**Judges 11:35**

And it came to be when he saw her, he tore his garments and said, Alas, my daughter, by stumbling you have made me stumble; you have become as a pain in my eyes. And I opened my mouth concerning you to the Lord, and I cannot turn back.

**Judges 11:36**

And she said to him, Father, if in me you opened your mouth to the Lord, do to me according to what went out from your mouth, because the Lord made for you acts of vengeance from your enemies, from the sons of Ammon.

**Judges 11:37**

And she said to her father, Do this word for me: let me alone two months, and I will go and go down upon the mountains and weep for my virginity, I and my companions.

**Judges 11:38**

And he said, Go, and he sent her away two months. And she went, she and her companions, and she wept for her virginity upon the mountains.

**Judges 11:39**

And it came to be at the end of two months that she returned to her father, and Jephthae fulfilled his vow that he had vowed, and she had not known a man. And it became an ordinance in Israel.

**Judges 11:40**

From days to days the daughters of Israel went to lament the daughter of Jephthae the Gileadite, four days in the year.

### Chapter 12

**Judges 12:1**

And the sons of Ephraim were gathered, and they came to Sephina and said to Jephthae, Why did you go to fight against the sons of Ammon and not call us to go with you? We will burn your house upon you with fire.

**Judges 12:2**

And Jephthae said to them, I and my people were men of contention, and the sons of Ammon were humbling me greatly, and I cried out to you, and you did not save me from their hand.

**Judges 12:3**

And I saw that there was no savior, and I put my life in my own hand and crossed over to the sons of Ammon, and the Lord gave them into my hand. And why did you come up to me this day to fight against me?

**Judges 12:4**

And Jephthae gathered all the men of Gilead and fought Ephraim, and the men of Gilead struck Ephraim, because they said, You, Gilead, are fugitives of Ephraim in the midst of Ephraim and in the midst of Manasseh.

**Judges 12:5**

And the men of Gilead seized the crossings of the Jordan of Ephraim, and it happened that the fugitives of Ephraim said, Let us cross over, and the men of Gilead said to them, Are you from Ephraim? And they said, We are not.

**Judges 12:6**

And they said to them, Speak now a watchword. And they did not direct themselves to speak thus, and they seized them and slaughtered them at the crossings of the Jordan. And there fell from Ephraim at that time forty-two thousand.

**Judges 12:7**

And Jephthae judged Israel six years, and Jephthae the Gileadite died and was buried in his city, Gilead.

**Judges 12:8**

And after him Esebōn from Baithleem judged Israel.

**Judges 12:9**

And there were to him thirty sons and thirty daughters sent outside, and he brought in thirty wives from outside for his sons, and he judged Israel seven years.

**Judges 12:10**

And Esebōn died and was buried in Bēthleem.

**Judges 12:11**

And after him Ailōn the Zebulunite judged Israel, and he judged Israel ten years.

**Judges 12:12**

And Ailōn the Zebulunite died in Ailim, and they buried him in the land of Zebulun.

**Judges 12:13**

And after him Labdōn son of Sellēm the Phraathōnite judged Israel.

**Judges 12:14**

And there were to him forty sons and thirty sons of his sons, riding on seventy foals, and he judged Israel eight years.

**Judges 12:15**

And Labdōn son of Sellēm the Phraathōnite died and was buried in Phraathōn in the land of Ephraim, in the mountain of Lanak.

### Chapter 13

**Judges 13:1**

And the sons of Israel again added to do evil before the Lord, and the Lord gave them into the hand of the foreigners forty years.

**Judges 13:2**

And there was a man from Saraa, from the tribe of Dan, and his name was Manōe, and his wife was barren and did not bear.

**Judges 13:3**

And an angel of the Lord appeared to the woman and said to her, Behold now, you are barren and have not borne, yet you shall conceive and bear a son.

**Judges 13:4**

And now take care and do not drink wine and strong drink and do not eat any unclean thing.

**Judges 13:5**

For behold, you shall conceive and bear a son, and iron shall not come upon his head, because the child shall be a consecrated Nazirite to God from the womb, and he will begin to save Israel from the hand of the foreigners.

**Judges 13:6**

And the woman came and said to her husband, saying, A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of an angel of God, very glorious, and I asked where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.

**Judges 13:7**

And he said to me, Behold, you shall conceive and bear a son, and now do not drink wine and strong drink and do not eat any uncleanness, because the child shall be a Nazirite of God from the womb until the day of his death.

**Judges 13:8**

And Manōe prayed to the Lord and said, In me, Lord, may the man of God whom you sent to us please come to us again and enlighten us what we should do for the child being born.

**Judges 13:9**

And God listened to the voice of Manōe, and the angel of God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field, and Manōe her husband was not with her.

**Judges 13:10**

And the woman hurried and ran and reported to her husband and said to him, Behold, the man who came to me on that day has appeared to me.

**Judges 13:11**

And Manōe rose and went after his wife to the man and said to him, Are you the man who spoke to the woman? And the angel said, I am.

**Judges 13:12**

And Manōe said, Now then, when your word comes, what shall be the ordinance for the child and his deeds?

**Judges 13:13**

And the angel of the Lord said to Manōe, From all that I said to the woman, let her keep herself.

**Judges 13:14**

From everything that comes out of the vine she shall not eat, and wine and strong drink she shall not drink, and every unclean thing she shall not eat. Everything that I commanded her let her keep.

**Judges 13:15**

And Manōe said to the angel of the Lord, Let us constrain you now, and we will prepare before you a kid of the goats.

**Judges 13:16**

And the angel of the Lord said to Manōe, If you constrain me, I will not eat your bread, but if you make a whole burnt offering, you shall offer it to the Lord. For Manōe did not know that he was an angel of the Lord.

**Judges 13:17**

And Manōe said to the angel of the Lord, What is your name, so that when your word comes we may glorify you?

**Judges 13:18**

And the angel of the Lord said to him, Why is this that you ask my name? It is wonderful.

**Judges 13:19**

And Manōe took the kid of the goats and the sacrifice and offered it on the rock to the Lord, to the Lord who does wonders, while Manōe and his wife were watching.

**Judges 13:20**

And it came to be when the flame went up from the altar to heaven, the angel of the Lord went up in the flame, and Manōe and his wife were watching, and they fell on their faces to the ground.

**Judges 13:21**

And the angel of the Lord did not continue any longer to appear to Manōe and to his wife; then Manōe knew that he was an angel of the Lord.

**Judges 13:22**

And Manōe said to his wife, We shall surely die, because we have seen God.

**Judges 13:23**

And his wife said to him, If the Lord desired to kill us, he would not have received from our hands a whole burnt offering and sacrifice, and he would not have enlightened us with all these things and would not have made such things heard to us.

**Judges 13:24**

And the woman bore a son and called his name Sampsōn, and the Lord blessed him, and the child grew.

**Judges 13:25**

And the Spirit of the Lord began to go with him in the camp of Dan, between Saraa and between Esthaol.

### Chapter 14

**Judges 14:1**

And Sampsōn went down to Thamnatha and saw a woman in Thamnatha from the daughters of the foreigners, and she was pleasing before him.

**Judges 14:2**

And he went up and reported to his father and to his mother and said, I saw a woman in Thamnatha from the daughters of the foreigners, and now take her for me as wife.

**Judges 14:3**

And his father and his mother said to him, Is there no woman from the daughters of your brothers and among all my people, that you are going to take a wife from the uncircumcised foreigners? And Sampsōn said to his father, Take this one for me, because she is pleasing in my eyes.

**Judges 14:4**

And his father and his mother did not know that it was from the Lord, because he was seeking repayment from the foreigners, and at that time the foreigners ruled over the sons of Israel.

**Judges 14:5**

And Sampsōn and his father and his mother went down to Thamnatha and turned aside into the vineyard of Thamnatha, and behold, a lion cub roaring to meet him.

**Judges 14:6**

And the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon him, and he tore it apart as one tears apart a kid of the goats, and there was nothing in his hand. And he did not report to his father or his mother what he had done.

**Judges 14:7**

And they went down and spoke to the woman, and she was pleasing before Sampsōn.

**Judges 14:8**

And he returned after days to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion, and behold, a swarm of bees was in the mouth of the lion, and there was honey.

**Judges 14:9**

And he took it out into his mouth, and he went on walking and eating, and he went to his father and to his mother and gave to them, and they ate. And he did not report to them that he took the honey from the carcass of the lion.

**Judges 14:10**

And his father went down to the woman, and Sampsōn made there a drinking feast seven days, because so the young men used to do.

**Judges 14:11**

And it came to be, in their fearing him, they appointed thirty companions for him, and they were with him.

**Judges 14:12**

And Sampsōn said to them, I will now put forth a riddle to you, and if you tell me the riddle within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen cloths and thirty changes of garments.

**Judges 14:13**

But if you are not able to tell me, then you shall give me thirty linen cloths and thirty changes of clothing. And they said to him, Put forth your riddle, and we will hear it.

**Judges 14:14**

And he said to them, Out of the eater came food, and out of the strong came sweetness. And they were not able to tell the riddle for three days.

**Judges 14:15**

And it came to be on the fourth day they said to Sampsōn's wife, Deceive your husband, and let him tell you the riddle, lest we burn you and your father's house with fire. Did you call us to impoverish us?

**Judges 14:16**

And Sampsōn's wife wept over him and said to him, You hate me and do not love me, because the riddle that you set forth to the sons of my people you have not told to me. And Sampsōn said to her, Behold, to my father and to my mother I have not told it, and shall I tell you?

**Judges 14:17**

And she wept over him during the seven days in which the feast was with them, and it came to be on the seventh day he told her, because she pressed him hard, and she told the sons of her people.

**Judges 14:18**

And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went down, What is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion? And Sampsōn said to them, If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found my riddle.

**Judges 14:19**

And the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon him, and he went down to Ascalon and struck from there thirty men and took their garments and gave them to those telling the riddle. And the anger of Sampsōn burned, and he went up to his father's house.

**Judges 14:20**

And Sampsōn's wife lived with his bridal companion, who had been his associate.

### Chapter 15

**Judges 15:1**

And it came to be after days, in the days of wheat harvest, Sampsōn visited his wife, bringing a kid of the goats, and said, I will go in to my wife in the bedroom. And her father did not allow him to go in to her.

**Judges 15:2**

And her father said, Saying, I said that in hating you hated her, and I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister better than she? Let her be yours instead of her.

**Judges 15:3**

And Sampsōn said to him, This once I am innocent from the foreigners, because I am doing evil things with you.

**Judges 15:4**

And Sampsōn went and caught three hundred foxes and took torches and tied tail to tail and put one torch between two tails in the middle.

**Judges 15:5**

And he set fire in the torches and let them loose into the sheaves of the foreigners and burned up the ears of grain and the pre-harvested grain from the stack and to what was standing and to vineyard and olive tree.

**Judges 15:6**

And the foreigners said, Who did this? And they said, Sampsōn, son-in-law of the Thamnathite, because he took his wife and gave her to his companion. And the foreigners went up and burned the house of her father and her and her father with fire.

**Judges 15:7**

And Sampsōn said to them, If you do this, I will not be pleased until I make my vengeance on each one of you.

**Judges 15:8**

And he struck them hip upon thigh, a great blow, and he went down and dwelt by the torrent in the cave of Etam.

**Judges 15:9**

And the foreigners went up and encamped against Judah and were spread out in Lechi.

**Judges 15:10**

And every man of Judah said to them, Why did you come up against us? And the foreigners said, We came up to bind Sampsōn and do to him as he did to us.

**Judges 15:11**

And three thousand men from Judah went down to the cleft of the rock Etam and said to Sampsōn, Do you not know that the foreigners rule over us? And why did you do these things to us? And Sampsōn said to them, Just as they did to me, so I did to them.

**Judges 15:12**

And they said to him, We came down to bind you and hand you over into the hands of the foreigners. And Sampsōn said to them, Swear to me that you yourselves will not kill me and hand me over to them, lest you yourselves fall upon me.

**Judges 15:13**

And they swore to him, saying, No, but we will surely bind you and hand you over into their hands, but with death we will not kill you. And they bound him with two new cords and brought him up from the rock.

**Judges 15:14**

And he came as far as the jawbone, and the foreigners shouted to meet him and ran to meet him. And the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon him, and the cords on his arms became like tow when it smells fire, and his bonds were dissolved from his arms.

**Judges 15:15**

And he found a jawbone of a donkey thrown on the road and stretched out his hand and took it and struck with it a thousand men.

**Judges 15:16**

And Sampsōn said, With the jawbone of a donkey, wiping out, I wiped them out, because with the jawbone of a donkey I struck a thousand men.

**Judges 15:17**

And it came to be when he finished speaking, he threw the jawbone from his hand and called that place Slaughter of Jawbone.

**Judges 15:18**

And he thirsted greatly and cried out to the Lord and said, You gave by the hand of your servant this great salvation, and now shall I die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?

**Judges 15:19**

And God opened the wound of the jawbone, and waters came out of it, and he drank, and his spirit returned in him and he revived. Therefore the name of it was called Spring, called of Jawbone, until this day.

**Judges 15:20**

And he judged Israel in the days of the foreigners twenty years.

### Chapter 16

**Judges 16:1**

And Sampsōn went from there to Gaza and saw there a prostitute woman and went in to her.

**Judges 16:2**

And it was reported to the Gazites, saying, Sampsōn came here. And they surrounded and lay in ambush for him all night at the gate of the city and kept quiet all night, saying, Let us wait until morning light and kill him.

**Judges 16:3**

And Sampsōn slept until midnight and rose about midnight and took hold of the doors of the gate of the city and the two posts and lifted them up with the bar and put them on his shoulders and carried them up to the top of the mountain that is opposite Hebron and put them there.

**Judges 16:4**

And it came to be after these things that he loved a woman by the torrent Sōrēch, and her name was Dalila.

**Judges 16:5**

And the satraps of the foreigners went up to her and said to her, Deceive him and see wherein his great strength lies and in what way we may prevail against him and bind him so as to humble him, and we will give you, each man, one thousand one hundred silver pieces.

**Judges 16:6**

And Dalila said to Sampsōn, Tell me wherein your great strength lies and in what way you may be bound for your humbling.

**Judges 16:7**

And Sampsōn said to her, If they bind me with seven fresh sinews not dried out, I will grow weak and become like one of the men.

**Judges 16:8**

And the satraps of the foreigners brought up to her seven fresh sinews not dried out, and she bound him with them.

**Judges 16:9**

And the ambush was sitting in the inner room, and she said to him, Foreigners are upon you, Sampsōn. And he tore the sinews just as a strand of tow is torn when it smells fire, and his strength was not known.

**Judges 16:10**

And Dalila said to Sampsōn, Behold, you mocked me and spoke lies to me. Now then tell me in what you may be bound.

**Judges 16:11**

And he said to her, If they bind me with seven new cords in which no work has been done, I will grow weak and become like one of the men.

**Judges 16:12**

And Dalila took new cords for him and bound him with them and said to him, The foreigners are upon you, Sampsōn. And the ambush was sitting in the inner room. And he tore them from his arms like thread.

**Judges 16:13**

And Dalila said to Sampsōn, Until now you have mocked me and spoken lies to me. Tell me in what you may be bound. And he said to her, If you weave the seven locks of my head with the web and fasten it with the peg into the wall, I will become weak like one of the men.

**Judges 16:14**

And Dalila put him to sleep and wove the seven curls of his head with the web and fastened them with the pegs into the wall and said to him, The foreigners are upon you, Sampsōn. And he woke from his sleep and pulled out the pegs together with the woven cloth from the wall and the web, and his strength was not known.

**Judges 16:15**

And Dalila said to him, How can you say, I loved you, and your heart is not with me? This third time you mocked me and did not tell me wherein your great strength lies.

**Judges 16:16**

And it came to be when she wore him down with her words all night and troubled him, he grew short of soul unto death.

**Judges 16:17**

And he told her everything from his heart and said to her, A razor has not come upon my head, because I am a Nazirite of God from my mother's womb, and if I am shaved, my strength will depart from me, and I will grow weak and become like all men.

**Judges 16:18**

And Dalila saw that he had told her everything from his heart, and she sent and called all the satraps of the foreigners, saying, Come up this once, because he told me all his heart. And all the satraps of the foreigners came up to her and brought the silver in their hands.

**Judges 16:19**

And she put him to sleep between her knees and called the barber and shaved the seven curls of his head, and he began to be humbled, and his strength departed from him.

**Judges 16:20**

And Dalila said to him, The foreigners are upon you, Sampsōn. And he woke from his sleep and said, I will go out and do as always and shake myself free. And he did not know that the Lord had departed from him.

**Judges 16:21**

And the foreigners seized him and gouged out his eyes and brought him down to Gaza and bound him with bronze fetters, and he was grinding in the prison house.

**Judges 16:22**

And the hair of his head began to grow back when he was shaved.

**Judges 16:23**

And the satraps of the foreigners gathered to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to rejoice, and they said, Our god gave Sampsōn our enemy into our hand.

**Judges 16:24**

And the people saw him and praised their gods and said, Our god gave our enemy into our hand, the one ravaging our land, who multiplied our wounded.

**Judges 16:25**

And it came to be when their heart grew good, they said, Call Sampsōn out of the prison house and let him play before us. And they called Sampsōn out of the prison house, and they mocked him, and they set him between the two pillars.

**Judges 16:26**

And Sampsōn said to the young servant guiding his hand, Let me rest now and let me feel the pillars upon which the house has been supported, and I will lean upon them. And the boy did so.

**Judges 16:27**

And the house was full of men and women, and all the satraps of the foreigners were there, and on the roof were about three thousand men and women looking on as Sampsōn was mocked.

**Judges 16:28**

And Sampsōn cried out to the Lord and said, Lord, Lord, remember me and strengthen me now, only this once, and I will exact one vengeance for my two eyes from the foreigners.

**Judges 16:29**

And Sampsōn took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house had been supported and leaned upon them, one with his right hand and one with his left.

**Judges 16:30**

And Sampsōn said, Let my soul die with the foreigners. And he bent in strength, and the house fell upon the satraps and upon all the people in it, and the dead whom Sampsōn killed in his death were more than those whom he killed in his life.

**Judges 16:31**

And his brothers and all the house of his father went down and took him and went up and buried him between Saraa and between Esthaol in the tomb of Manōe his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.

### Chapter 17

**Judges 17:1**

And there was a man from the hill-country of Ephraim, and his name was Micha.

**Judges 17:2**

And he said to his mother, The eleven hundred silver pieces taken from you, about which you pronounced an oath and spoke in my ears, behold, the silver is with me; I took it. And his mother said, Blessed be my son to the Lord.

**Judges 17:3**

And he returned the eleven hundred silver pieces to his mother, and his mother said, With consecration I consecrated the silver to the Lord from my hand alone, to make a carved image and a molten image, and now I will return them to you and give it back to you.

**Judges 17:4**

And he returned the silver to his mother, and his mother took two hundred silver pieces and gave it to the metalworker, and he made it into a carved image and a molten image, and it came to be in the house of Micha.

**Judges 17:5**

And the man Micha had a house of God, and he made an ephod and teraphim and filled the hand of one of his sons, and he became priest for him.

**Judges 17:6**

In those days there was no king in Israel; each man did what was good in his own eyes.

**Judges 17:7**

And there was a young man from Bethleem, clan of Judah, from the family of Judah, and he was a Levite, and he was staying there as a resident.

**Judges 17:8**

And the man went from the city of Judah, from Bethleem, to reside wherever he might find, and he came to the hill-country of Ephraim, as far as the house of Micha, to make his way.

**Judges 17:9**

And Micha said to him, From where do you come? And he said to him, I am a Levite from Bethleem of Judah, and I am going to reside wherever I may find.

**Judges 17:10**

And Micha said to him, Stay with me and become to me as father and as priest, and I will give you ten silver pieces for days, and a pair of garments, and your living. And the Levite went.

**Judges 17:11**

And he began to reside with the man, and the young man became to him like one of his sons.

**Judges 17:12**

And Micha filled the hand of the Levite, and the young man became his priest and was in the house of Micha.

**Judges 17:13**

And Micha said, Now I know that the Lord has done me good, because the Levite has become my priest.

### Chapter 18

**Judges 18:1**

In those days there was no king in Israel, and in those days the tribe of Dan was seeking for itself an inheritance to dwell in, because until those days no inheritance had fallen to it in the midst of the tribes of Israel.

**Judges 18:2**

And the sons of Dan sent from their families five men from among them, sons of strength, from Saraa and Esthaol, to inspect the land and to search it out, and they said to them, Go and search out the land. And they came to the hill-country of Ephraim as far as the house of Micha and rested there.

**Judges 18:3**

While they were by the house of Micha, they recognized the voice of the young Levite, and they turned aside there and said to him, Who brought you here, and what are you doing in this place, and what do you have here?

**Judges 18:4**

And he said to them, Thus and thus Micha did for me, and he hired me, and I became his priest.

**Judges 18:5**

And they said to him, Inquire now of God, and we will know whether our way on which we are going will prosper.

**Judges 18:6**

And the priest said to them, Go in peace. Before the Lord is your way in which you are going.

**Judges 18:7**

And the five men went and came to Laisa and saw the people dwelling in it, sitting in confidence according to the judgment of the Sidonians, being quiet in confidence and unable to speak a word, because they are far from Sidon and have no dealings with Syria.

**Judges 18:8**

And the five men came to their brothers at Saraa and Esthaol, and their brothers said to them, Why are you sitting here?

**Judges 18:9**

And they said, Rise and let us go up against them, because we entered and walked through the land as far as Laisa and saw the people dwelling in it in confidence according to the custom of the Sidonians, and they are far from Sidon and have no dealings with Syria. But rise and let us go up against them, because we found the land, and behold, it is very good, and you keep silent. Do not hesitate to go, to enter and inherit the land.

**Judges 18:10**

When you enter, you will come to a trusting people, and the land is broad, because God has given it into your hand, a place where there is no lack of anything that is in the land.

**Judges 18:11**

And from the family of Dan, from Saraa and Esthaol, six hundred men girded with weapons of war set out.

**Judges 18:12**

And they went up and encamped in Kariathiarim in Judah. Therefore that place was called Camp of Dan until this day; behold, it is behind Kariathiarim.

**Judges 18:13**

They passed on from there and came to the hill-country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micha.

**Judges 18:14**

And the five men going to inspect the land answered and said to their brothers, Do you know that in these houses there are an ephod and teraphim and a carved image and a molten image? And now know what you will do.

**Judges 18:15**

And they turned aside there and entered into the house of the young Levite, into the house of Micha, and greeted him.

**Judges 18:16**

And the six hundred men girded with weapons of war, from the sons of Dan, stood by the doorway of the gate.

**Judges 18:17**

And the five men going to inspect the land went up there and took the carved image and the ephod and the teraphim and the molten image, while the priest stood by the doorway of the gate and the six hundred men girded with weapons of war.

**Judges 18:18**

And these entered into the house of Micha and took the carved image and the ephod and the teraphim and the molten image. And the priest said to them, What are you doing?

**Judges 18:19**

And they said to him, Be silent; put your hand upon your mouth and come with us, and you shall be to us as father and as priest. Is it not better for you to be priest to the house of one man than for you to become priest to a tribe and a family in Israel?

**Judges 18:20**

And the heart of the priest was gladdened, and he took the ephod and the teraphim and the carved image and the molten image and entered into the midst of the people.

**Judges 18:21**

And they turned and went away, and they placed the household and the possessions and his glorious things before them.

**Judges 18:22**

And when they had gone a good distance from the house of Micha, behold, Micha and the men with the house with Micha cried out after the sons of Dan.

**Judges 18:23**

And the sons of Dan turned their faces and said to Micha, What is wrong with you, that you cried out?

**Judges 18:24**

And Micha said, My carved image that I made for myself you took, and the priest, and you went away. And what remains to me now? And why do you say to me, Why do you cry out?

**Judges 18:25**

And the sons of Dan said to him, Let your voice not be heard with us, lest bitter-souled men fall upon you and you lose your life and the life of your household.

**Judges 18:26**

And the sons of Dan went on their way, and Micha saw that they were stronger than he, and he turned aside and returned to his house.

**Judges 18:27**

And they took what Micha had made and the priest who was his, and they came to Laisa, to a people quiet and confident, and struck them with the edge of the sword and burned the city with fire.

**Judges 18:28**

And there was no deliverer, because it is far from the Sidonians, and they have no dealings with men, and it is in the valley that belongs to the house of Roōb. And they built the city and dwelt in it.

**Judges 18:29**

And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of their father who was born to Israel, though the name of the city formerly was Lais.

**Judges 18:30**

And the sons of Dan set up for themselves the carved image of Micha, and Jonathan son of Gērsōm, son of Moses, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.

**Judges 18:31**

And they set up for themselves the carved image of Micha that he made all the days that the house of God was in Shiloh.

### Chapter 19

**Judges 19:1**
