And Abessalom said, Call now also Chousi the Arachite, and let us hear what too is in his mouth.

**2 Samuel 17:6**

And Chousi came to Abessalom, and Abessalom said to him, saying, Achitophel has spoken according to this word. Shall we do according to his word? But if not, you speak.

**2 Samuel 17:7**

And Chousi said to Abessalom, This time the counsel that Achitophel has counseled is not good.

**2 Samuel 17:8**

And Chousi said, You know your father and his men, that they are very mighty and bitter in soul, like a bear robbed of cubs in the field, and like a wild boar in the open country. And your father is a man of war and will not lodge with the people.

**2 Samuel 17:9**

For behold, even now he is hidden in one of the hills or in one of the places, and it will happen, when some fall among them at the first attack, that whoever hears will say, A slaughter has happened among the people following Abessalom.

**2 Samuel 17:10**

Then even a son of strength, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will utterly melt, because all Israel knows that your father is mighty and the men with him are sons of strength.

**2 Samuel 17:11**

But this is the counsel I have counseled: let all Israel from Dan to Bersabee be gathered to you, like the sand by the sea in multitude, and let your own face go in their midst.

**2 Samuel 17:12**

And we will come upon him in one of the places where we find him there, and we will camp against him as the dew falls on the ground, and we will not leave among him and the men with him even one.

**2 Samuel 17:13**

And if he withdraws into a city, all Israel will take ropes to that city, and we will drag it down into the torrent-bed until not even a stone is left there.

**2 Samuel 17:14**

And Abessalom and every man of Israel said, The counsel of Chousi the Arachite is better than the counsel of Achitophel. For the Lord commanded the good counsel of Achitophel to be scattered, so that the Lord might bring all these evils upon Abessalom.

**2 Samuel 17:15**

And Chousi the Arachite said to Sadok and Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus Achitophel counseled Abessalom and the elders of Israel, and thus and thus I counseled.

**2 Samuel 17:16**

And now send quickly and report to David, saying, Do not lodge tonight at the crossings of the wilderness, but hurry and cross over, lest the king and all the people with him be swallowed up.

**2 Samuel 17:17**

And Ionathan and Achimaas had been standing at the spring Rhogel, and the maidservant went and reported to them, and they were going to report to King David, because they could not be seen entering the city.

**2 Samuel 17:18**

But a young man saw them and reported it to Abessalom, and the two went quickly and entered the house of a man in Baourim, and he had a well in his court, and they went down there.

**2 Samuel 17:19**

And the woman took the covering and spread it over the face of the well, and she scattered crushed grain over it, and no matter was known.

**2 Samuel 17:20**

And the servants of Abessalom came to the woman at the house and said, Where are Achimaas and Ionathan? And the woman said to them, They passed a little beyond the water. And they searched and did not find them and returned to Ierousalem.

**2 Samuel 17:21**

And it came to be after they left, that they came up out of the well and went and reported to King David, and they said to David, Rise and cross the water quickly, because thus Achitophel has counseled against you.

**2 Samuel 17:22**

And David rose, and all the people with him, and they crossed the Jordan until the morning light. Not one was missing who had not crossed the Jordan.

**2 Samuel 17:23**

And Achitophel saw that his counsel had not been done, and he saddled his donkey and rose and went to his home, to his own city, and he gave orders to his house and hanged himself, and he died and was buried in the tomb of his father.

**2 Samuel 17:24**

And David crossed over to Manaim, and Abessalom crossed the Jordan, he and every man of Israel with him.

**2 Samuel 17:25**

And Abessalom appointed Amessai in place of Ioab over the army. And Amessai was son of a man whose name was Iothor the Israelite, who went in to Abigaia daughter of Naas, sister of Sarouia the mother of Ioab.

**2 Samuel 17:26**

And Israel and Abessalom camped in the land of Galaad.

**2 Samuel 17:27**

And it came to be when David came to Manaim, Ouesbi son of Naas from Rabbath of the sons of Ammon, and Machir son of Ammiel from Lodabar, and Berzelli the Galaadite from Rhogellim,

**2 Samuel 17:28**

brought ten beds and coverings and ten cauldrons and earthenware vessels and wheat and barley and flour and parched grain and beans and lentils,

**2 Samuel 17:29**

and honey and butter and sheep and curds from cattle. And they brought them to David and to the people with him to eat, because they said, The people are hungry and faint and thirsty in the wilderness.

### Chapter 18

**2 Samuel 18:1**

And David mustered the people with him and appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

**2 Samuel 18:2**

And David sent out the people, one third by the hand of Ioab, one third by the hand of Abessa son of Sarouia, brother of Ioab, and one third by the hand of Eththi the Gethite. And David said to the people, I myself will surely go out with you.

**2 Samuel 18:3**

But they said, You must not go out, because if we flee they will not set their heart on us, and if half of us die they will not set their heart on us, because you are like ten thousand of us. And now it is better that you be for us help from the city by helping.

**2 Samuel 18:4**

And the king said to them, Whatever is good in your eyes I will do. And the king stood by the side of the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.

**2 Samuel 18:5**

And the king commanded Ioab and Abessa and Eththi, saying, Spare for my sake the young man Abessalom. And all the people heard when the king gave orders to all the commanders concerning Abessalom.

**2 Samuel 18:6**

And all the people went out into the forest opposite Israel, and the battle came to be in the forest of Ephraim.

**2 Samuel 18:7**

And the people of Israel stumbled there before the servants of David, and the great slaughter there on that day was twenty thousand men.

**2 Samuel 18:8**

And the battle there was spread over the face of all the land, and the forest multiplied to devour more of the people than the sword devoured of the people on that day.

**2 Samuel 18:9**

And Abessalom met the servants of David. And Abessalom was mounted on his mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of the great oak, and his head was caught in the oak, and he was suspended between heaven and earth, and the mule under him passed on.

**2 Samuel 18:10**

And one man saw and reported to Ioab and said, Behold, I saw Abessalom hanging in the oak.

**2 Samuel 18:11**

And Ioab said to the man reporting to him, And behold, you saw him. Why then did you not strike him there to the ground? Then I would have given you ten silver pieces and one belt.

**2 Samuel 18:12**

But the man said to Ioab, Even if a thousand silver shekels were weighed into my hands, I would never put my hand against the king's son. For in our hearing the king charged you and Abessa and Eththi, saying, Guard for my sake the young man Abessalom.

**2 Samuel 18:13**

Otherwise, if I had done lawlessness against his life, no word would be hidden from the king, and you yourself would have stood opposite.

**2 Samuel 18:14**

And Ioab said, I will not linger thus before you. And Ioab took three darts in his hand and drove them into the heart of Abessalom while he was still alive in the heart of the oak.

**2 Samuel 18:15**

And ten young men carrying the armor of Ioab surrounded Abessalom and struck him and put him to death.

**2 Samuel 18:16**

And Ioab sounded with the trumpet, and the people turned back from pursuing after Israel, because Ioab spared the people.

**2 Samuel 18:17**

And they took Abessalom and cast him into a great pit in the forest and raised over him a very large heap of stones, and all Israel fled, a man to his tent.

**2 Samuel 18:18**

And Abessalom had taken and set up for himself in his lifetime the pillar in the King's Valley, because he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance. And he called the pillar by his own name, and it is called Hand of Abessalom to this day.

**2 Samuel 18:19**

And Achimaas son of Sadok said, Let me run now and bring good news to the king, because the Lord has judged for him against the hand of his enemies.

**2 Samuel 18:20**

And Ioab said to him, You are not a bearer of good news on this day, but you may bring good news on another day. On this day you shall not bring good news, because the king's son is dead.

**2 Samuel 18:21**

And Ioab said to Chousi, Go, report to the king what you have seen. And Chousi bowed to Ioab and ran.

**2 Samuel 18:22**

And Achimaas son of Sadok again added and said to Ioab, Whatever may happen, let me run too after Chousi. And Ioab said, Why would you run, my son, since no payment of good news is for you?

**2 Samuel 18:23**

And he said, Whatever may happen, I will run. And he said to him, Run. And Achimaas ran by the way of the plain and passed Chousi.

**2 Samuel 18:24**

And David was sitting between the two gates. And the watchman went up to the roof of the gate by the wall and lifted his eyes and saw, and behold, one man was running alone.

**2 Samuel 18:25**

And the watchman called out and reported to the king. And the king said, If he is alone, good news is in his mouth. And he came, going and coming near.

**2 Samuel 18:26**

And the watchman saw another man running, and the watchman called out to the gatekeeper and said, Behold, another man runs alone. And the king said, This one too is bringing good news.

**2 Samuel 18:27**

And the watchman said, I see the running of the first like the running of Achimaas son of Sadok. And the king said, He is a good man and comes in good news.

**2 Samuel 18:28**

And Achimaas called out and said to the king, Peace. And he bowed before the king with his face to the ground and said, Blessed be the Lord your God, who shut up the men who lifted their hand against my lord the king.

**2 Samuel 18:29**

And the king said, Is it well with the young man Abessalom? And Achimaas said, I saw the great crowd when Ioab sent the servant of the king and your servant, and I did not know what was there.

**2 Samuel 18:30**

And the king said, Turn aside, stand here. And he turned aside and stood.

**2 Samuel 18:31**

And behold, Chousi arrived and said to the king, Let my lord the king receive good news, because the Lord has judged for you today against the hand of all those rising against you.

**2 Samuel 18:32**

And the king said to Chousi, Is it well with the young man Abessalom? And Chousi said, May the enemies of my lord the king and all who have risen up against him for evil become like that young man.

### Chapter 19

**2 Samuel 19:1**

And the king was troubled and went up to the upper room of the gate and wept, and thus he said as he went, My son Abessalom, my son, my son Abessalom. Who will give my death in place of you? I, in place of you, Abessalom, my son, my son.

**2 Samuel 19:2**

And it was reported to Ioab, saying, Behold, the king is weeping and mourning over Abessalom.

**2 Samuel 19:3**

And the victory on that day became mourning for all the people, because the people heard on that day, saying, The king grieves over his son.

**2 Samuel 19:4**

And the people were slipping into the city on that day, as the people slip in ashamed when they flee in battle.

**2 Samuel 19:5**

And the king hid his face, and the king cried out with a loud voice, saying, My son Abessalom, Abessalom, my son, my son.

**2 Samuel 19:6**

And Ioab came to the king in the house and said, Today you have put to shame the face of all your servants, those who are rescuing you today and the lives of your sons and your daughters and the lives of your wives and your concubines,

**2 Samuel 19:7**

by loving those who hate you and hating those who love you. For you declared today that your commanders and servants are nothing, because I know today that if Abessalom were alive and all of us today dead, then it would have been right in your eyes.

**2 Samuel 19:8**

And now rise, go out, and speak to the heart of your servants, because by the Lord I have sworn that if you do not go out, not a man will lodge with you tonight, and know for yourself that this will be worse for you than all the evil that has come upon you from your youth until now.

**2 Samuel 19:9**

And the king rose and sat in the gate, and all the people reported, saying, Behold, the king sits in the gate. And all the people came before the king. And Israel fled, a man to his tents.

**2 Samuel 19:10**

And all the people were disputing in all the tribes of Israel, saying, King David rescued us from all our enemies and himself delivered us from the hand of the foreigners, and now he has fled from the land and from his kingdom because of Abessalom.

**2 Samuel 19:11**

And Abessalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. So now why are you silent about bringing back the king? And the word of all Israel came to the king.

**2 Samuel 19:12**

And King David sent to Sadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak to the elders of Iouda, saying, Why do you become the last to bring back the king to his house, since the word of all Israel has come to the king?

**2 Samuel 19:13**

You are my brothers; you are my bones and my flesh. Why then do you become the last to bring back the king to his house?

**2 Samuel 19:14**

And you shall say to Amessai, Are you not my bone and my flesh? Thus may God do to me, and thus may he add, if you shall not be commander of the army before me all the days in place of Ioab.

**2 Samuel 19:15**

And he inclined the heart of every man of Iouda as one man, and they sent to the king, saying, Return, you and all your servants.

**2 Samuel 19:16**

And the king returned and came as far as the Jordan, and the men of Iouda came to Galgala to go and meet the king, to bring the king across the Jordan.

**2 Samuel 19:17**

And Semei son of Gera son of the Jeminaian from Baourim hurried and came down with the men of Iouda to meet King David.

**2 Samuel 19:18**

And with him were one thousand men from Benjamin and Siba the servant of the house of Saoul, and his fifteen sons with him and his twenty servants with him, and they made straight for the Jordan before the king.

**2 Samuel 19:19**

And they performed the service of bringing the king across, and the crossing went over to carry the house of the king across and to do what was right in his eyes. And Semei son of Gera fell on his face before the king as he was crossing the Jordan.

**2 Samuel 19:20**

And he said to the king, Let not my lord reckon lawlessness against me, and do not remember how your servant did wrong on the day when my lord the king went out from Ierousalem, so that the king should put it to heart.

**2 Samuel 19:21**

For your servant knows that I have sinned. And behold, I came today first of all the house of Ioseph to come down and meet my lord the king.

**2 Samuel 19:22**

And Abessa son of Sarouia answered and said, Shall not Semei be put to death for this, because he cursed the anointed of the Lord?

**2 Samuel 19:23**

And David said, What is it to me and to you, sons of Sarouia, that today you become an enemy to me? Today shall any man in Israel be put to death? For do I not know that today I reign over Israel?

**2 Samuel 19:24**

And the king said to Semei, You shall not die. And the king swore to him.

**2 Samuel 19:25**

And Mephibosthe son of Ionathan son of Saoul came down to meet the king, and he had not cared for his feet, nor trimmed his nails, nor tended his mustache, nor washed his garments from the day the king left until the day he came in peace.

**2 Samuel 19:26**

And it came to be when he entered Ierousalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, Why did you not go with me, Mephibosthe?

**2 Samuel 19:27**

And Mephibosthe said to him, My lord king, my servant deceived me. For your servant said to him, Saddle the donkey for me, and I will mount it and go with the king, because your servant is lame.

**2 Samuel 19:28**

And he schemed against your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like an angel of God. So do what is good in your eyes.

**2 Samuel 19:29**

For all the house of my father were nothing but men of death to my lord the king, yet you set your servant among those eating at your table. And what right have I still, even to cry out further to the king?

**2 Samuel 19:30**

And the king said to him, Why do you still speak your words? I have said, You and Siba shall divide the field.

**2 Samuel 19:31**

And Mephibosthe said to the king, Indeed, let him take all, after my lord the king has come in peace to his house.

**2 Samuel 19:32**

And Berzelli the Galaadite came down from Rhogellim and crossed with the king over the Jordan to escort him over the Jordan.

**2 Samuel 19:33**

And Berzelli was a very old man, a son of eighty years, and he had sustained the king while he stayed in Manaim, because he was a very great man.

**2 Samuel 19:34**

And the king said to Berzelli, You shall cross over with me, and I will sustain your old age with me in Ierousalem.

**2 Samuel 19:35**

And Berzelli said to the king, How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Ierousalem?

**2 Samuel 19:36**

I am eighty years old today. Will I still know between good and evil? Will your servant still taste what I eat or what I drink? Will I still hear the voice of singers and singing women? Why then should your servant still be a burden to my lord the king?

**2 Samuel 19:37**

Your servant will just cross the Jordan a little way with the king. Why should the king repay me with this repayment?

**2 Samuel 19:38**

Let your servant sit now, and I will die in my city, beside the tomb of my father and my mother. And behold, your servant Chamaam will cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your eyes.

**2 Samuel 19:39**

And the king said, Chamaam shall cross with me, and I will do for him what is good in your eyes, and whatever you choose from me, I will do for you.

**2 Samuel 19:40**

And all the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed. And the king kissed Berzelli and blessed him, and he returned to his place.

**2 Samuel 19:41**

And the king crossed into Galgala, and Chamaam crossed with him, and all the people of Iouda crossing with the king, and also half the people of Israel.

**2 Samuel 19:42**

And behold, every man of Israel came to the king and said to the king, Why did our brothers, the men of Iouda, steal you away and bring the king and his house across the Jordan, and all David's men with him?

**2 Samuel 19:43**

And every man of Iouda answered the man of Israel, and they said, Because the king is near to me. And why have you been angered about this matter? Did we eat by eating from the king, or did he give us a gift, or did he lift something for us?

**2 Samuel 19:44**

And the man of Israel answered the man of Iouda and said, I have ten hands in the kingdom, and I am firstborn more than you, and indeed I have more claim in David than you. So why did you treat me lightly? And was not my word first for bringing back my king? But the word of the men of Iouda was harsher than the word of the men of Israel.

### Chapter 20

**2 Samuel 20:1**

And there happened to be there a lawless man, and his name was Sabee son of Bochori, a Jeminaian man. And he sounded the horn and said, We have no share in David, nor inheritance for us in the son of Iessai. Each man to your tents, O Israel.

**2 Samuel 20:2**

And every man of Israel went up from following David after Sabee son of Bochori, but the men of Iouda clung to their king, from the Jordan even to Ierousalem.

**2 Samuel 20:3**

And David entered his house at Ierousalem, and the king took the ten women, his concubines, whom he had left to guard the house, and gave them into a house of custody and sustained them, but he did not go in to them. And they were shut away until the day of their death, living as widows.

**2 Samuel 20:4**

And the king said to Amessai, Summon for me the men of Iouda within three days, and you yourself stand here.

**2 Samuel 20:5**

And Amessai went to summon Iouda, but he delayed beyond the set time that David had appointed for him.

**2 Samuel 20:6**

And David said to Abessa, Now Sabee son of Bochori will do us more harm than Abessalom. So now take with you the servants of your lord and pursue after him, lest he find fortified cities for himself and hide from our eyes.

**2 Samuel 20:7**

And after him went out the men of Ioab and the Cherethite and the Phelethite and all the mighty men, and they went out from Ierousalem to pursue after Sabee son of Bochori.

**2 Samuel 20:8**

And they were by the great stone that is in Gabaon, and Amessai came before them. And Ioab was girded with his cloak, his garment, and over it he was girded with a sword fastened at his waist in its sheath, and the sword came out and fell.

**2 Samuel 20:9**

And Ioab said to Amessai, Are you well, my brother? And the right hand of Ioab took hold of the beard of Amessai to kiss him.

**2 Samuel 20:10**

And Amessai did not guard against the sword in the hand of Ioab, and Ioab struck him with it in the belly, and his entrails poured out on the ground, and he did not strike him a second time, and he died. And Ioab and Abessa his brother pursued after Sabee son of Bochori.

**2 Samuel 20:11**

And a man from the young men of Ioab stood over him and said, Whoever delights in Ioab and whoever belongs to David, after Ioab.

**2 Samuel 20:12**

And Amessai lay wallowing in blood in the middle of the road, and the man saw that all the people stood still. And he turned Amessai out of the road into a field and threw a garment over him, because he saw that everyone coming upon him had stopped.

**2 Samuel 20:13**

And when he was removed from the road, every man of Israel passed on after Ioab, to pursue after Sabee son of Bochori.

**2 Samuel 20:14**

And he passed through all the tribes of Israel into Abel and into Baithmaacha, and all the men in Charri gathered and came after him.

**2 Samuel 20:15**

And they came and besieged him at Abel and Baithmaacha, and they poured out a siege mound against the city, and it stood at the outer wall, and all the people with Ioab were intending to throw down the wall.

**2 Samuel 20:16**

And a wise woman cried out from the wall and said, Hear, hear. Tell Ioab now, Come near here, and I will speak to him.

**2 Samuel 20:17**

And he came near to her, and the woman said, Are you Ioab? And he said, I am. And she said to him, Hear the words of your servant. And Ioab said, I am listening.

**2 Samuel 20:18**

And she said, saying, In earlier times they spoke a word, saying, They surely asked in Abel and in Dan whether what the faithful of Israel established had failed, and thus they ended matters.

**2 Samuel 20:19**

I am one of the peaceful, of the strongholds of Israel, but you seek to put to death a city and a mother-city in Israel. Why are you drowning the inheritance of the Lord?

**2 Samuel 20:20**

And Ioab answered and said, Far be it from me, far be it from me, if I should drown or if I should destroy.

**2 Samuel 20:21**

This is not the matter, but a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sabee son of Bochori is his name, and he lifted his hand against King David. Give him to me alone, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said to Ioab, Behold, his head will be thrown to you through the wall.

**2 Samuel 20:22**

And the woman went to all the people and spoke to all the city in her wisdom, and they removed the head of Sabee son of Bochori and threw it to Ioab. And he sounded the horn, and they were scattered from the city, each man to his tents. And Ioab returned to Ierousalem to the king.

**2 Samuel 20:23**

And Ioab was over all the army of Israel, and Banaias son of Iodae was over the Cherethite and over the Phelethite.

**2 Samuel 20:24**

And Adoniram was over the tribute, and Iosaphat son of Achilouth was recorder.

**2 Samuel 20:25**

And Sousa was secretary, and Sadok and Abiathar were priests.

**2 Samuel 20:26**

And Ira the Iairite too was priest to David.

### Chapter 21

**2 Samuel 21:1**

And there was famine in the days of David three years, year following year. And David sought the face of the Lord, and the Lord said, There is guilt on Saoul and on his house for blood, because he put the Gabaonites to death.

**2 Samuel 21:2**

And King David called the Gabaonites and said to them. Now the Gabaonites are not from the sons of Israel, but from the remnant of the Amorrite, and the sons of Israel had sworn to them, yet Saoul sought to strike them in his zeal for the sons of Israel and Iouda.

**2 Samuel 21:3**

And David said to the Gabaonites, What shall I do for you, and by what shall I make atonement, so that you may bless the inheritance of the Lord?

**2 Samuel 21:4**

And the Gabaonites said to him, There is no silver or gold for us with Saoul and with his house, and it is not for us to put a man to death in Israel. And he said, What you say, I will do for you.

**2 Samuel 21:5**

And they said to the king, The man brought us to an end and pursued us, he who schemed to wipe us out. Let us destroy him from having any standing in all the border of Israel.

**2 Samuel 21:6**

Let seven men be given to us from his sons, and we will expose them to the sun before the Lord in Gabaon of Saoul, chosen of the Lord. And the king said, I will give them.

**2 Samuel 21:7**

But the king spared Mephibosthe son of Ionathan son of Saoul, because of the oath of the Lord that was between them, between David and between Ionathan son of Saoul.

**2 Samuel 21:8**

And the king took the two sons of Respha daughter of Aia, whom she bore to Saoul, Hermoni and Mephibosthe, and the five sons of Michol daughter of Saoul, whom she bore to Esdriel son of Berzelli the Moulathite.

**2 Samuel 21:9**

And he gave them into the hand of the Gabaonites, and they exposed them to the sun on the mountain before the Lord. And the seven fell together, and they were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, at the beginning of barley harvest.

**2 Samuel 21:10**

And Respha daughter of Aia took sackcloth and spread it for herself on the rock from the beginning of barley harvest until water dripped on them from heaven, and she did not allow the birds of heaven to rest on them by day nor the beasts of the field by night.

**2 Samuel 21:11**

And it was reported to David what Respha daughter of Aia, concubine of Saoul, had done, and they were released, and Dan son of Ioa from the offspring of the giants took hold of them.

**2 Samuel 21:12**

And David went and took the bones of Saoul and the bones of Ionathan his son from the men, sons of Iabis Galaad, who stole them from the square of Baithsan, because the foreigners had set them there on the day the foreigners struck Saoul on Gelboue.

**2 Samuel 21:13**

And he brought up from there the bones of Saoul and the bones of Ionathan his son, and they gathered the bones of the ones exposed to the sun.

**2 Samuel 21:14**

And they buried the bones of Saoul and the bones of Ionathan his son and of the ones exposed to the sun in the land of Benjamin at the side, in the tomb of Kis his father, and they did all that the king commanded, and afterward God listened to the land.

**2 Samuel 21:15**

And again there was war for the foreigners with Israel, and David went down, and his servants with him, and they fought with the foreigners, and David grew faint.

**2 Samuel 21:16**

And Iesbi, who was among the offspring of Rapha, and the weight of whose spear was three hundred shekels of bronze, and he was girded with a club, intended to strike David.

**2 Samuel 21:17**

And Abessa son of Sarouia helped him, and he struck the foreigner and put him to death. Then the men of David swore, saying, You shall no longer go out with us to battle, and you shall not extinguish the lamp of Israel.

**2 Samuel 21:18**

And after these things there was again war at Geth with the foreigners. Then Sebocha the Astathothite struck Sepph, one of the offspring of Rapha.

**2 Samuel 21:19**

And there was war at Gob with the foreigners, and Eleanan son of Ariorgim the Baithleemite struck Goliath the Gethite, and the shaft of his spear was like a weavers' beam.

**2 Samuel 21:20**

And again there was war at Geth, and there was a man of measure, and the fingers of his hands and the fingers of his feet were six and six, twenty-four in number, and he too was born to Rapha.

**2 Samuel 21:21**

And he reproached Israel, and Ionathan son of Semei brother of David struck him.

**2 Samuel 21:22**

These four were born as offspring of the giants in Geth, in the house of Rapha, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

### Chapter 22

**2 Samuel 22:1**

And David spoke to the Lord the words of this song in the day when the Lord delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saoul.

**2 Samuel 22:2**

And he said, O Lord, my rock and my fortress and my rescuer for me,

**2 Samuel 22:3**

my God will be my guard; I will trust in him, my shield and horn of my salvation, my supporter and my refuge of salvation; from injustice you will save me.

**2 Samuel 22:4**

I will call upon the Lord, worthy of praise, and I will be saved from my enemies.

**2 Samuel 22:5**

For breakers of death surrounded me; torrents of lawlessness terrified me.

**2 Samuel 22:6**

Birth-pangs of death encircled me; hardnesses of death came before me.

**2 Samuel 22:7**

When I was afflicted, I will call on the Lord, and I will cry out to my God, and he will hear my voice from his temple, and my cry will be in his ears.

**2 Samuel 22:8**

And the earth was shaken and quaked, and the foundations of heaven were troubled and convulsed, because the Lord was angry with them.

**2 Samuel 22:9**

Smoke went up in his anger, and fire from his mouth devours; coals were kindled from it.

**2 Samuel 22:10**

And he bent the heavens and came down, and gloom was under his feet.

**2 Samuel 22:11**

And he rode on cheroubin and flew, and he was seen on wings of wind.

**2 Samuel 22:12**

And he made darkness his hiding place around him, his tent, dark water thickened in clouds of air.

**2 Samuel 22:13**

From the brightness before him coals of fire were kindled.

**2 Samuel 22:14**

The Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice.

**2 Samuel 22:15**

And he sent arrows and scattered them, lightning and threw them into panic.

**2 Samuel 22:16**

And the channels of the sea were seen, and the foundations of the world were uncovered at the rebuke of the Lord, from the breath of the spirit of his wrath.

**2 Samuel 22:17**

He sent from on high and took me; he drew me out of many waters.

**2 Samuel 22:18**

He rescued me from my strong enemies, from those hating me, because they were stronger than I.

**2 Samuel 22:19**

They came before me in the day of my affliction, and the Lord became my support.

**2 Samuel 22:20**

And he brought me out into breadth and delivered me, because he delighted in me.

**2 Samuel 22:21**

And the Lord repaid me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he repaid me.

**2 Samuel 22:22**

Because I kept the ways of the Lord and did not act impiously away from my God.

**2 Samuel 22:23**

Because all his judgments were before me, and his ordinances I did not turn away from.

**2 Samuel 22:24**

And I will be blameless with him, and I will keep myself from my lawlessness.

**2 Samuel 22:25**

And the Lord will repay me according to my righteousness and according to the cleanness of my hands before his eyes.

**2 Samuel 22:26**

With the holy one you will be holy, and with the perfect man you will be perfect.

**2 Samuel 22:27**

And with the chosen one you will be chosen, and with the crooked you will be twisted.

**2 Samuel 22:28**

And you will save the poor people, and the eyes of the proud you will humble.

**2 Samuel 22:29**

Because you are my lamp, O Lord, and the Lord will light up my darkness.

**2 Samuel 22:30**

Because in you I will run as a raider, and in my God I will leap over a wall.

**2 Samuel 22:31**

The Mighty One, blameless is his way; the word of the Lord is strongly refined by fire; he is a shield for all who trust in him.

**2 Samuel 22:32**

For who is mighty besides the Lord, and who will be a creator besides our God?

**2 Samuel 22:33**

The Mighty One who strengthens me with power and made my way blameless,

**2 Samuel 22:34**

making my feet like deer's feet and setting me upon the heights,

**2 Samuel 22:35**

teaching my hands for war and bending a bronze bow with my arms.

**2 Samuel 22:36**

And you gave me the shield of my salvation, and your attentive hearing multiplied me.

**2 Samuel 22:37**

You widened my steps under me, and my ankles did not give way.

**2 Samuel 22:38**

I will pursue my enemies and destroy them, and I will not turn back until I finish them.

**2 Samuel 22:39**

And I will crush them, and they will not rise; they will fall under my feet.

**2 Samuel 22:40**

And you will strengthen me with power for battle; you will bend under me those rising against me.

**2 Samuel 22:41**

And you gave me the back of my enemies, those hating me, and I destroyed them.

**2 Samuel 22:42**

They will cry out, and there is no helper, to the Lord, and he did not answer them.

**2 Samuel 22:43**

And I beat them small as dust of the earth; like the mud of exits I crushed them thin.

**2 Samuel 22:44**

And you will rescue me from the strivings of peoples; you will keep me as head of nations. A people I had not known served me.

**2 Samuel 22:45**

Sons of foreigners lied to me; at hearing of the ear they listened to me.

**2 Samuel 22:46**

Sons of foreigners will fall away and stagger out of their enclosures.

**2 Samuel 22:47**

The Lord lives, and blessed is my guard, and the God, the guard of my salvation, will be exalted,

**2 Samuel 22:48**

the mighty Lord who gives avenges to me, disciplining peoples under me,

**2 Samuel 22:49**

and bringing me out from my enemies. And you will lift me high above those rising against me; from a man of injustices you will rescue me.

**2 Samuel 22:50**

Because of this I will confess you, Lord, among the nations, and to your name I will sing psalms,

**2 Samuel 22:51**

magnifying the salvations of his king and doing mercy for his anointed, for David and for his seed forever.

### Chapter 23

**2 Samuel 23:1**

And these are the last words of David: Faithful is David son of Iessai, and faithful the man whom the Lord raised up concerning the anointed of the God of Iakob, and beautiful are the psalms of Israel.

**2 Samuel 23:2**

The Spirit of the Lord spoke in me, and his word was on my tongue.

**2 Samuel 23:3**

The God of Israel says; the guard of Israel spoke to me: I will speak a parable. In humanity, how will you make strong the fear of God?

**2 Samuel 23:4**

And in God: morning light, when the sun rises at morning, a morning not passed over from brightness, and as grass from the earth after rain.

**2 Samuel 23:5**

For not so is my house with the Mighty One? For he set for me an everlasting covenant, ready in every time, guarded, because all my salvation and every desire, shall not the lawless one sprout?

**2 Samuel 23:6**

But all the lawless are like a thorn thrown out, because they are not taken by hand.

**2 Samuel 23:7**

And the man who touches them will arm himself with full iron and the shaft of a spear, and they shall be utterly burned with fire in their shame.

**2 Samuel 23:8**

These are the names of the mighty men of David: Iebosthe the Chananite, chief of the third. This is Adinon the Asonaean. He drew his sword over eight hundred wounded at one time.

**2 Samuel 23:9**

And after him Eleazar son of his father's brother, son of a Sousite, among the three mighty men. He was with David at Serran, and when he reproached him among the foreigners, they were gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel went up.

**2 Samuel 23:10**

He rose and struck among the foreigners until his hand grew weary and his hand clung to the sword. And the Lord worked a great deliverance on that day, and the people returned after him only to strip the slain.

**2 Samuel 23:11**

And after him Sammaia son of Asa the Aruchite. And the foreigners gathered into a troop, and there was a plot of the field full of lentils, and the people fled from before the foreigners.

**2 Samuel 23:12**

And he stood firm in the middle of the plot and rescued it and struck the foreigners, and the Lord worked a great deliverance.

**2 Samuel 23:13**

And three from the thirty went down and came at harvest to David at the cave of Odollam, and a troop of foreigners had camped in the valley of Rhaphaim.

**2 Samuel 23:14**

And David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the foreigners was then in Baithleem.

**2 Samuel 23:15**

And David desired and said, Who will give me water to drink from the well at Baithleem that is by the gate? And the station of the foreigners was then in Baithleem.

**2 Samuel 23:16**

And the three mighty men broke through the camp of the foreigners and drew water from the well at Baithleem that is by the gate and took it and came to David, but he would not drink it, and poured it out to the Lord.

**2 Samuel 23:17**

And he said, Be it far from me, Lord, to do this. Shall I drink the blood of the men who went in their lives? And he would not drink it. These things the three mighty men did.

**2 Samuel 23:18**

And Abessa brother of Ioab son of Sarouia, he was chief among the three, and he lifted his spear against three hundred wounded, and he had a name among the three.

**2 Samuel 23:19**

From those three he was honored and became their commander, yet he did not come up to the three.

**2 Samuel 23:20**

And Banaias son of Iodae, he was a man abundant in deeds, from Kabeseel. He struck the two sons of Ariel of Moab, and he himself went down and struck the lion in the midst of the pit on the day of snow.

**2 Samuel 23:21**

He struck the Egyptian man, a man worth seeing, and in the hand of the Egyptian was a spear like a weavers' beam. And he went down to him with a staff and snatched the spear from the hand of the Egyptian and killed him with his own spear.

**2 Samuel 23:22**

These things Banaias son of Iodae did, and he had a name among the three mighty men.

**2 Samuel 23:23**

He was honored among the three, but to the three he did not come, and David set him over his audience.

**2 Samuel 23:24**

And these are the names of the mighty men of David the king: Asael brother of Ioab was among the thirty, Eleanan son of Doudi his father's brother in Baithleem,

**2 Samuel 23:25**

Samma the Aroudite, Elika the Aroudite,

**2 Samuel 23:26**

Elles the Phelothite, Hira son of Ekkas the Thekoite,

**2 Samuel 23:27**

Abiezer the Anathothite, from the sons of the Asothite,

**2 Samuel 23:28**

Selmon the Aonite, Moore the Netophathite,

**2 Samuel 23:29**

Ela son of Baana the Netophathite, Eththi son of Riba from Gabaeth of Benjamin,

**2 Samuel 23:30**

Banaias the Pharathonite, Ouri from Nachaligaias,

**2 Samuel 23:31**

Abiel son of the Arabothite, Azmoth the Barsamite,

**2 Samuel 23:32**

Eliasou the Salabonite, sons of Iasan, Ionathan,

**2 Samuel 23:33**

Samma the Arodite, Achian son of Sarad the Araourite,

**2 Samuel 23:34**

Eliphaleth son of the Asbite, son of the Maachathite, Eliab son of Achitophel the Gelonite,

**2 Samuel 23:35**

Asarai the Karmelite, Pharai the Erchi,

**2 Samuel 23:36**

Igaal son of Nathan from Dynaimea, son of Gaddi,

**2 Samuel 23:37**

Elie the Ammanite, Gelorai the Berothaean, carrying the arms of Ioab son of Sarouia,

**2 Samuel 23:38**

Hiras the Iethiraean, Gareb the Iethiraean,

**2 Samuel 23:39**

Ourias the Chettite, altogether thirty-seven.

### Chapter 24

**2 Samuel 24:1**

And again the anger of the Lord burned in Israel, and he shook David among them, saying, Go, number Israel and Iouda.

**2 Samuel 24:2**

And the king said to Ioab, commander of the strength with him, Go now through all the tribes of Israel from Dan to Bersabee and count the people, and I will know the number of the people.

**2 Samuel 24:3**

And Ioab said to the king, May the Lord your God add to the people as they are and a hundredfold more, with the eyes of my lord the king seeing. But why does my lord the king delight in this thing?

**2 Samuel 24:4**

But the word of the king prevailed against Ioab and against the commanders of the force, and Ioab and the commanders of the force went out from before the king to count the people of Israel.

**2 Samuel 24:5**

And they crossed the Jordan and camped at Aroer, to the right of the city in the middle of the ravine, Gad and Eliezer.

**2 Samuel 24:6**

And they came to Galaad and to the land of Thabason, which is Adasai, and they came to Danidan and Udan and went around to Sidon.

**2 Samuel 24:7**

And they came to Mapsar of Tyre and all the cities of the Heuite and the Chananite, and they came south of Iouda to Bersabee.

**2 Samuel 24:8**

And they went around in all the land and came at the end of nine months and twenty days to Ierousalem.

**2 Samuel 24:9**

And Ioab gave the number of the counting of the people to the king, and Israel became eight hundred thousand men of strength drawing sword, and the men of Iouda five hundred thousand fighting men.

**2 Samuel 24:10**

And David's heart struck him after he had counted the people. And David said to the Lord, I have sinned greatly in what I have done. And now, Lord, please cause the lawlessness of your servant to pass over, because I have acted very foolishly.

**2 Samuel 24:11**

And David rose in the morning, and the word of the Lord came to Gad the prophet, the seer of David, saying,

**2 Samuel 24:12**

Go and speak to David, saying, Thus says the Lord: Three things I am lifting upon you, and choose for yourself one of them, and I will do it to you.

**2 Samuel 24:13**

And Gad came to David and reported to him and said to him, Choose for yourself whether three years of famine shall come to you in your land, or three months of your fleeing before your enemies while they pursue you, or three days of death to be in your land. Now then know and see what word I should answer the one who sent me.

**2 Samuel 24:14**

And David said to Gad, Distress presses me greatly from every side. Let me now fall into the hand of the Lord, because his mercies are very many. But into the hands of man I will not fall. And David chose death for himself.

**2 Samuel 24:15**

And it was days of wheat harvest, and the Lord gave death in Israel from morning until the dinner hour, and the break in the people began, and from the people, from Dan to Bersabee, seventy thousand men died.

**2 Samuel 24:16**

And the angel of God stretched out his hand toward Ierousalem to destroy it, and the Lord relented concerning the evil and said to the angel destroying among the people, Enough now, let your hand go. And the angel of the Lord was by the threshing floor of Orna the Iebousaian.

**2 Samuel 24:17**

And David said to the Lord when he saw the angel striking among the people, and he said, Behold, I am the one who did wrong, and I am the shepherd who did evil. But these sheep, what have they done? Let your hand now be against me and against my father's house.

**2 Samuel 24:18**

And Gad came to David on that day and said to him, Go up and set up an altar to the Lord on the threshing floor of Orna the Iebousaian.

**2 Samuel 24:19**

And David went up according to the word of Gad, just as the Lord commanded him.

**2 Samuel 24:20**

And Orna looked down and saw the king and his servants passing along above him, and Orna went out and bowed to the king with his face to the ground.

**2 Samuel 24:21**

And Orna said, Why has my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to the Lord, and the plague will be restrained from upon the people.

**2 Samuel 24:22**

And Orna said to David, Let my lord the king take and offer to the Lord what is good in his eyes. Behold, the oxen are for whole burnt offerings, and the wheels and the implements of the oxen are for wood.

**2 Samuel 24:23**

Orna gave all these things to the king. And Orna said to the king, May the Lord your God bless you.

**2 Samuel 24:24**

And the king said to Orna, No, because in buying I will buy from you for a price, and I will not offer to the Lord my God a whole burnt offering for nothing. And David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

**2 Samuel 24:25**

And David built there an altar to the Lord and offered whole burnt offerings and peace offerings, and Solomon added upon the altar at the end, because it had been small at first. And the Lord listened to the land, and the plague was restrained from over Israel.

## 1 Kings

### Chapter 1

**1 Kings 1:1**

And King David was old, advanced in days, and they covered him with garments, but he did not get warm.

**1 Kings 1:2**

And his servants said, Let them seek for my lord the king a virgin young woman, and she will stand before the king and be warming him and will lie with him, and my lord the king will get warm.

**1 Kings 1:3**

And they sought a beautiful young woman from all the border of Israel, and they found Abisak the Somanite and brought her to the king.

**1 Kings 1:4**

And the young woman was very beautiful, and she was warming the king and ministering to him, but the king did not know her.

**1 Kings 1:5**

And Adonias son of Anggith exalted himself, saying, I will reign. And he made for himself chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run before him.

**1 Kings 1:6**

And his father had never restrained him, saying, Why have you done thus? And he too was very handsome in appearance, and she had borne him after Abessalom.

**1 Kings 1:7**

And his words were with Ioab son of Sarouia and with Abiathar the priest, and they were helping after Adoniou.

**1 Kings 1:8**

But Sadok the priest and Banaias son of Iodae and Nathan the prophet and Semei and Rhei and the mighty men of David were not after Adoniou.

**1 Kings 1:9**

And Adonias sacrificed sheep and calves and lambs beside the stone of Zoeleth, which was near the spring Rhogel, and he called all his brothers and all the nobles of Iouda, the servants of the king.

**1 Kings 1:10**

But Nathan the prophet and Banaian and the mighty men and Solomon his brother he did not call.

**1 Kings 1:11**

And Nathan said to Bersabee mother of Solomon, saying, Have you not heard that Adonias son of Anggith has become king, and our lord David did not know?

**1 Kings 1:12**

And now come, let me counsel you with counsel, and rescue your life and the life of your son Solomon.

**1 Kings 1:13**

Come, go in to King David and say to him, Did you not, my lord king, swear to your servant, saying, Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne? Then why has Adonias become king?

**1 Kings 1:14**

And behold, while you are still speaking there with the king, I will come in after you and fill out your words.

**1 Kings 1:15**

And Bersabee entered to the king in the chamber. And the king was very old, and Abisak the Somanite was ministering to the king.

**1 Kings 1:16**

And Bersabee bowed and did obeisance to the king, and the king said, What is with you?

**1 Kings 1:17**

And she said, My lord king, you swore by the Lord your God to your servant, saying, Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.

**1 Kings 1:18**

And now behold, Adonias has become king, and you, my lord king, did not know.

**1 Kings 1:19**

And he sacrificed calves and lambs and sheep in abundance and called all the sons of the king and Abiathar the priest and Ioab commander of the force, but Solomon your servant he did not call.

**1 Kings 1:20**

And you, my lord king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, for you to report to them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

**1 Kings 1:21**

And it will be, when my lord the king sleeps with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon will be sinners.

**1 Kings 1:22**

And behold, while she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came.

**1 Kings 1:23**

And it was reported to the king, Behold, Nathan the prophet. And he entered before the king and bowed to the king with his face to the ground.

**1 Kings 1:24**

And Nathan said, My lord king, did you say, Adonias will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne?

**1 Kings 1:25**

For he went down today and sacrificed calves and lambs and sheep in abundance and called all the sons of the king and the commanders of the force and Abiathar the priest. And behold, they are eating and drinking before him, and they said, Long live King Adonias.

**1 Kings 1:26**

But me, your servant, and Sadok the priest and Banaias son of Iodae and Solomon your servant he did not call.

**1 Kings 1:27**

Has this thing happened by my lord the king, and have you not made known to your servant who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?

**1 Kings 1:28**

And David answered and said, Call Bersabee to me. And she entered before the king and stood before him.

**1 Kings 1:29**

And the king swore and said, As the Lord lives, who redeemed my life from every affliction,

**1 Kings 1:30**

that as I swore to you by the Lord God of Israel, saying, Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne instead of me, so I will do on this day.

**1 Kings 1:31**

And Bersabee bowed with her face to the ground and did obeisance to the king and said, May my lord King David live forever.

**1 Kings 1:32**

And King David said, Call Sadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Banaias son of Iodae to me. And they entered before the king.

**1 Kings 1:33**

And the king said to them, Take the servants of your lord with you and mount my son Solomon on my mule and lead him down to Gion.

**1 Kings 1:34**

And let Sadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there as king over Israel, and sound the horn and say, Long live King Solomon.

**1 Kings 1:35**

And he will sit on my throne, and he will reign instead of me, and I have commanded him to be ruler over Israel and Iouda.

**1 Kings 1:36**

And Banaias son of Iodae answered the king and said, May it be so. May the Lord God of my lord the king confirm it.

**1 Kings 1:37**

Just as the Lord was with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he enlarge his throne beyond the throne of my lord King David.

**1 Kings 1:38**

And Sadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Banaias son of Iodae and the Cherethite and the Phelethite went down and set Solomon upon the mule of King David and led him to Gion.

**1 Kings 1:39**

And Sadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon, and they sounded the horn, and all the people said, Long live King Solomon.

**1 Kings 1:40**

And all the people went up after him, and they were dancing in dances and rejoicing with great joy, and the earth split at their sound.

**1 Kings 1:41**

And Adonias heard, and all his invited guests with him, and they themselves finished eating. And Ioab heard the sound of the horn and said, What is the sound of the city in uproar?

**1 Kings 1:42**

While he was still speaking, behold, Ionathan son of Abiathar the priest came, and Adonias said, Come in, for you are a man of strength and bring good news.

**1 Kings 1:43**

And Ionathan answered and said, And truly, our lord King David has made Solomon king.

**1 Kings 1:44**

And the king sent with him Sadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Banaias son of Iodae and the Cherethite and the Phelethite, and they set him upon the mule of the king.

**1 Kings 1:45**

And Sadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him as king at Gion, and they came up from there rejoicing, and the city rang. This is the sound that you heard.

**1 Kings 1:46**

And Solomon has sat upon the throne of the kingdom.

**1 Kings 1:47**

And the servants of the king entered to bless our lord King David, saying, May God make the name of Solomon your son better than your name, and may he enlarge his throne beyond your throne. And the king bowed on his bed.

**1 Kings 1:48**

And thus too the king said, Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who gave today one from my seed sitting on my throne, and my eyes are seeing it.

**1 Kings 1:49**

And all the invited guests of Adonias were terrified and rose up, and each man went on his way.

**1 Kings 1:50**

And Adonias feared before Solomon, and he rose and went away and took hold of the horns of the altar.

**1 Kings 1:51**

And it was reported to Solomon, saying, Behold, Adonias feared King Solomon and has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put his servant to death by the sword.

**1 Kings 1:52**

And Solomon said, If he becomes a son of strength, not one hair of his will fall to the ground, but if evil is found in him, he will die.

**1 Kings 1:53**

And King Solomon sent and brought him down from the altar, and he entered and bowed to King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, Go to your house.

### Chapter 2

**1 Kings 2:1**

And the days drew near for David to die, and he commanded Solomon his son, saying,

**1 Kings 2:2**

I am going on the way of all the earth, and you must be strong and become a man.

**1 Kings 2:3**

And you must keep the charge of the Lord your God, to walk in his ways, to keep his commandments and his ordinances and his judgments, the things written in the law of Moyses, so that you may understand what you will do according to all that I command you.

**1 Kings 2:4**

So that the Lord may establish his word that he spoke, saying, If your sons guard their way to walk before me in truth, with all their heart and with all their soul, there will not be destroyed for you a man from upon the throne of Israel.

**1 Kings 2:5**

And indeed, you know what Ioab son of Sarouia did to me, what he did to the two commanders of the forces of Israel, to Abenner son of Ner and to Amessai son of Iether, and he killed them and assigned blood of war in peace and put innocent blood on the belt on his waist and on the sandal on his foot.

**1 Kings 2:6**

And you will do according to your wisdom, and you will not bring his gray hair down in peace to Hades.

**1 Kings 2:7**

And to the sons of Berzelli the Galaadite you will do mercy, and they will be among those eating at your table, because thus they came near to me when I was fleeing from before Abessalom your brother.

**1 Kings 2:8**

And behold, with you is Semei son of Gera son of the Jeminaian from Baourim, and he cursed me with a grievous curse on the day when I was going to the Camps. And he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, saying, I will not put you to death by the sword.

**1 Kings 2:9**

And now do not hold him guiltless, because you are a wise man and will know what you will do to him, and you will bring his gray hair down in blood to Hades.

**1 Kings 2:10**

And David slept with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.

**1 Kings 2:11**

And the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years. In Chebron he reigned seven years, and in Ierousalem thirty-three years.

**1 Kings 2:12**

And Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, a son of twelve years, and his kingdom was greatly prepared.

**1 Kings 2:13**

And Adonias son of Anggith entered to Bersabee mother of Solomon and bowed to her. And she said, Is your coming peace? And he said, Peace.

**1 Kings 2:14**

And he said, A word is mine to you. And she said to him, Speak.

**1 Kings 2:15**

And he said to her, You know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel set its face on me for king, but the kingdom turned and became my brother's, because it came to him from the Lord.

**1 Kings 2:16**

And now I ask one request from you. Do not turn away your face. And Bersabee said to him, Speak.

**1 Kings 2:17**

And he said to her, Speak now to King Solomon, for he will not turn his face from you, and let him give me Abisak the Somanite as wife.

**1 Kings 2:18**

And Bersabee said, Good. I will speak to the king concerning you.

**1 Kings 2:19**

And Bersabee entered to King Solomon to speak to him concerning Adonias. And the king rose to meet her and kissed her and sat on his throne, and a throne was set for the mother of the king, and she sat at his right hand.

**1 Kings 2:20**

And she said to him, I ask one small request from you. Do not turn away your face. And the king said to her, Ask, my mother, for I will not turn you away.

**1 Kings 2:21**

And she said, Let Abisak the Somanite be given to Adonias your brother as wife.

**1 Kings 2:22**

And King Solomon answered and said to his mother, And why did you ask Abisak for Adonias? Ask the kingdom for him too, because he is my elder brother greater than I, and he has Abiathar the priest and Ioab son of Sarouia the commander as companion.

**1 Kings 2:23**

And King Solomon swore by the Lord, saying, Thus may God do to me, and thus may he add, because Adonias spoke this word against his own life.

**1 Kings 2:24**

And now, as the Lord lives, who prepared me and set me on the throne of David my father and made me a house as the Lord spoke, today Adonias will be put to death.

**1 Kings 2:25**

And King Solomon sent by the hand of Banaiou son of Iodae, and he struck him and Adonias died on that day.

**1 Kings 2:26**

And to Abiathar the priest the king said, Run away to Anathoth, to your field, because you are a man of death on this day. But I will not put you to death, because you carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord before my father and because you were afflicted in all the things in which my father was afflicted.

**1 Kings 2:27**

And Solomon cast out Abiathar from being priest of the Lord, for the word of the Lord to be fulfilled, which he spoke against the house of Eli at Selom.

**1 Kings 2:28**

And the report came to Ioab son of Sarouia, because Ioab had inclined after Adonias, but after Solomon he did not incline. And Ioab fled to the tent of the Lord and took hold of the horns of the altar.

**1 Kings 2:29**

And it was reported to Solomon, saying that Ioab fled to the tent of the Lord, and behold, he holds the horns of the altar. And Solomon sent to Ioab, saying, What has happened to you that you fled to the altar? And Ioab said, Because I feared from before you, and I fled to the Lord. And King Solomon sent Banaiou son of Iodae, saying, Go and kill him and bury him.

**1 Kings 2:30**

And Banaiou son of Iodae came to Ioab at the tent of the Lord and said to him, Thus says the king: Come out. And Ioab said, I will not come out, because I will die here. And Banaias son of Iodae turned back and said to the king, Thus Ioab has spoken, and thus he answered me.

**1 Kings 2:31**

And the king said to him, Go and do to him just as he said, and kill him and bury him, and you will remove today the blood that Ioab poured out for nothing from me and from the house of my father.

**1 Kings 2:32**

And the Lord turned the blood of his injustice onto his head, because he met two men more righteous and better than he and killed them by the sword, and my father David did not know their blood: Abenner son of Ner, commander of Israel, and Amessa son of Iether, commander of Iouda.

**1 Kings 2:33**

And their blood returned upon his head and upon the head of his seed forever, but for David and for his seed and for his house and for his throne, may there be peace forever from the Lord.

**1 Kings 2:34**

And Banaiou son of Iodae met Ioab and killed him and buried him at his house in the wilderness.

**1 Kings 2:35**

And the king gave Banaiou son of Iodae in his place over the generalship, and the kingdom was being set right in Ierousalem, and the king gave Sadok the priest as first priest instead of Abiathar. And the Lord gave understanding to Solomon and very much wisdom and breadth of heart like the sand that is beside the sea. And the understanding of Solomon was multiplied greatly beyond the understanding of all the ancients and beyond all the wise of Egypt. And he took the daughter of Pharao and brought her into the City of David until he finished his own house and the house of the Lord first and the wall of Ierousalem all around. In seven years he made it and finished it. And Solomon had seventy thousand carrying burdens and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain. And Solomon made the Sea and the bases and the great basins and the pillars and the fountain of the court and the bronze sea. And he built the citadel and its battlements and cut through the City of David. Thus the daughter of Pharao was going up from the City of David into her house that he built for her. Then he built the citadel. And Solomon offered up three times in the year whole burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar that he built to the Lord and was burning incense before the Lord and finished the house. And these were the rulers set over the works of Solomon, three thousand six hundred overseers of the people doing the works. And he built Assour and Magdo and Gazer and upper Baithoron and Baalath. But after he built the house of the Lord and the wall of Ierousalem all around, after these things he built these cities. And while David was still living he commanded Solomon, saying, Behold, with you is Semei son of Gera, son of the seed of the Jeminaian from Chebron. He cursed me with a grievous curse on the day when I was going to the Camps, and he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, saying, He shall not be put to death by the sword. And now do not hold him guiltless, because you are a prudent man and you will know what you will do to him, and you will bring his gray hair down in blood to Hades.

**1 Kings 2:36**

And the king called Semei and said to him, Build yourself a house in Ierousalem and dwell there, and do not go out from there anywhere.

**1 Kings 2:37**

And it will be on the day of your going out and crossing the torrent Kedron, knowing you will know that you will die by death. Your blood will be on your head. And the king made him swear on that day.

**1 Kings 2:38**

And Semei said to the king, Good is the word that you spoke, my lord king. Thus your servant will do. And Semei sat in Ierousalem three years.

**1 Kings 2:39**

And it came to be after three years that two slaves of Semei ran away to Anchous son of Maacha king of Geth, and it was reported to Semei, saying, Behold, your slaves are in Geth.

**1 Kings 2:40**

And Semei rose and saddled his donkey and went to Geth to Anchous to seek his slaves, and Semei went and brought his slaves from Geth.

**1 Kings 2:41**

And it was reported to Solomon, saying that Semei went from Ierousalem to Geth and brought back his slaves.

**1 Kings 2:42**

And the king sent and called Semei and said to him, Did I not make you swear by the Lord and testify against you, saying, On whatever day you go out from Ierousalem and go to the right or to the left, knowing you will know that you will die by death?

**1 Kings 2:43**

And why did you not keep the oath of the Lord and the commandment that I commanded against you?

**1 Kings 2:44**

And the king said to Semei, You know all your evil, which your heart knew, what you did to David my father, and the Lord has returned your evil upon your head.

**1 Kings 2:45**

And King Solomon is blessed, and the throne of David will be prepared before the Lord forever.

**1 Kings 2:46**

And King Solomon commanded Banaias son of Iodae, and he went out and struck him and he died. And King Solomon was very understanding and wise, and Iouda and Israel were exceedingly many, like the sand on the sea in multitude, eating and drinking and rejoicing. And Solomon was ruler over all the kingdoms, and they were bringing gifts and serving Solomon all the days of his life. And Solomon began opening the domains of Lebanon. And he built Thermai in the wilderness. And this was Solomon's provision: thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of beaten flour, ten choice calves and twenty pasture-fed cattle and one hundred sheep, besides deer and gazelles and choice fatted birds. For he was ruler over everything beyond the river, from Raphi to Gaza, over all the kings beyond the river. And he had peace from all his sides all around, and Iouda and Israel lived trusting, each under his vine and under his fig tree, eating and drinking, from Dan to Bersabee, all the days of Solomon. And these were the chiefs of Solomon: Azariou son of Sadok the priest, and Orniou son of Nathan, chief of the overseers, and Edram over his house, and Souba secretary, and Basa son of Achithalam recorder, and Abi son of Ioab commander in chief, and Achire son of Edrai over the levies, and Banaia son of Iodae over the court guard and over the brickwork, and Zachour son of Nathan the counselor. And Solomon had forty thousand brood mares for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen. And he was ruler in all the kingdoms from the river to the land of the foreigners and to the borders of Egypt. Solomon son of David reigned over Israel and Iouda in Ierousalem.

### Chapter 3

**1 Kings 3:2**

Yet the people were burning incense on the high places, because a house was not yet built for the name of the Lord until now.

**1 Kings 3:3**

And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the ordinances of David his father, except that on the high places he was sacrificing and burning incense.

**1 Kings 3:4**

And he rose and went to Gabaon to sacrifice there, because that was the highest and greatest high place. Solomon offered one thousand whole burnt offerings on the altar in Gabaon.

**1 Kings 3:5**

And the Lord appeared to Solomon in sleep by night, and the Lord said to Solomon, Ask what request for yourself.

**1 Kings 3:6**

And Solomon said, You did great mercy with your servant David my father, just as he walked before you in truth and in righteousness and in uprightness of heart with you, and you kept for him this great mercy, to give his son upon his throne, as on this day.

**1 Kings 3:7**

And now, Lord my God, you gave your servant instead of David my father, and I am a small child and do not know my going out and my coming in.

**1 Kings 3:8**

And your servant is in the midst of your people whom you chose, a numerous people who will not be numbered.

**1 Kings 3:9**

And you will give your servant a heart that hears and discerns your people in righteousness, to understand between good and evil. For who will be able to judge this heavy people of yours?

**1 Kings 3:10**

And it was pleasing before the Lord that Solomon asked this word.

**1 Kings 3:11**

And the Lord said to him, Because you asked from me this word and did not ask for yourself many days and did not ask riches and did not ask the lives of your enemies, but asked for yourself understanding to hear judgment,

**1 Kings 3:12**

behold, I have done according to your word. Behold, I have given you a wise and understanding heart. One like you did not come to be before you, and after you none like you will arise.

**1 Kings 3:13**

And what you did not ask I have given you too, both riches and glory, so that no man like you has come to be among kings.

**1 Kings 3:14**

And if you walk in my way, keeping my commandments and my ordinances as David your father walked, I will multiply your days.

**1 Kings 3:15**

And Solomon awoke, and behold, it was a dream. And he rose and comes to Ierousalem and stood before the altar that was before the ark of the covenant of the Lord in Sion and offered whole burnt offerings and made peace offerings and made a great drinking-feast for himself and for all his servants.

**1 Kings 3:16**

Then two prostitute women appeared to the king and stood before him.

**1 Kings 3:17**

And the one woman said, In me, my lord, I and this woman live in one house, and we gave birth in the house.

**1 Kings 3:18**

And it came to be on the third day after I gave birth, that this woman also gave birth, and we were together, and there was no one with us except the two of us in the house.

**1 Kings 3:19**

And the son of this woman died in the night, because she lay on him.

**1 Kings 3:20**

And she rose in the middle of the night and took my son from my embrace while your servant was sleeping and laid him in her bosom, and her dead son she laid in my bosom.

**1 Kings 3:21**

And I rose in the morning to nurse my son, and he was dead. And behold, I considered him in the morning, and behold, he was not my son whom I bore.

**1 Kings 3:22**

And the other woman said, No, but my son is the living one, and your son is the dead one. And they were speaking before the king.

**1 Kings 3:23**

And the king said to them, You say, This is my living son, and this one's son is the dead one. And you say, No, but my son is the living one, and your son is the dead one.

**1 Kings 3:24**

And the king said, Bring me a sword. And they brought the sword before the king.

**1 Kings 3:25**

And the king said, Divide the living nursing child into two, and give half of him to this one and half of him to this one.

**1 Kings 3:26**

And the woman whose son was the living one answered and said to the king, because her womb was troubled over her son, In me, my lord, give her the child, and by death do not put him to death. But the other said, Let him be neither mine nor hers. Divide him.

**1 Kings 3:27**

And the king answered and said, Give the child to the one who said, Give him to her, and by death do not put him to death. She is his mother.

**1 Kings 3:28**

And all Israel heard this judgment that the king judged, and they feared before the king, because they saw that understanding of God was in him for doing justice.

### Chapter 5

**1 Kings 5:1**

And the appointed officers were thus providing for King Solomon and all the charges upon the table of the king, each in his month. They did not alter a word. And they were bringing the barley and the straw for the horses and the chariots to the place where the king might be, each according to his arrangement.

**1 Kings 5:2**

And these were the needs for Solomon in one day: thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of beaten flour,

**1 Kings 5:3**

and ten choice calves and twenty pasture-fed cattle and one hundred sheep, besides deer and gazelles and choice fatted birds.

**1 Kings 5:4**

For he was ruler beyond the river, and he had peace from all sides all around.

**1 Kings 5:9**

And the Lord gave understanding to Solomon and very great wisdom and breadth of heart like the sand that is beside the sea.

**1 Kings 5:10**

And Solomon was greatly multiplied in understanding beyond the understanding of all the ancient men and beyond all the wise of Egypt.

**1 Kings 5:11**

**1 Kings 5:12**

And Solomon spoke three thousand parables, and his songs were five thousand.

**1 Kings 5:14**

And Solomon took the daughter of Pharao for himself as wife and brought her into the City of David until he finished the house of the Lord and his own house and the wall of Ierousalem. Then Pharao king of Egypt went up and took Gazer beforehand and burned it, and the Chananite who lived in Mergab, and Pharao gave them as gifts to his daughter, wife of Solomon, and Solomon built Gazer.

**1 Kings 5:15**

And Chiram king of Tyre sent his servants to anoint Solomon in place of David his father, because Chiram loved David all his days.

**1 Kings 5:16**

And Solomon sent to Chiram, saying,

**1 Kings 5:17**

You know David my father, that he was not able to build a house for the name of the Lord my God because of the wars that encircled him, until the Lord gave them under the soles of his feet.

**1 Kings 5:18**

And now the Lord my God has given me rest all around. There is no adversary, and there is no evil encounter.

**1 Kings 5:19**

And behold, I say that I will build a house for the name of the Lord my God, just as the Lord God spoke to David my father, saying, Your son, whom I will give instead of you upon your throne, he will build the house for my name.

And now command, and let them cut wood for me from Lebanon. And behold, my servants are with your servants, and I will give you the wage of your service according to all that you say, because you know that there is no one among us knowing how to cut wood like the Sidonians.

**1 Kings 5:21**

And it came to be when Chiram heard the words of Solomon, he rejoiced greatly and said, Blessed is God today, who gave to David a wise son over this many people.

**1 Kings 5:22**

**1 Kings 5:23**

**1 Kings 5:24**

And Chiram was giving cedars to Solomon and all his desire.

**1 Kings 5:25**

And Solomon gave to Chiram twenty thousand cors of wheat and provision for his house and twenty thousand baths of beaten oil. According to this Solomon was giving to Chiram year by year.

**1 Kings 5:26**

And the Lord gave wisdom to Solomon just as he spoke to him, and there was peace between Chiram and between Solomon, and they cut a covenant between themselves.

**1 Kings 5:27**

And King Solomon raised a levy from all Israel, and the levy was thirty thousand men.

**1 Kings 5:28**

And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand in the month by turns. One month they were in Lebanon and two months in their houses, and Adoniram was over the levy.

**1 Kings 5:29**

And Solomon had seventy thousand carrying burdens and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain,

**1 Kings 5:30**

except for the chiefs appointed over the works of Solomon, three thousand six hundred overseers doing the works.

**1 Kings 5:32**

And they prepared the stones and the timbers for three years.

### Chapter 6

**1 Kings 6:1**

And it came to be in the four hundred and fortieth year of the coming out of the sons of Israel from Egypt, in the fourth year, in the second month, of King Solomon reigning over Israel. And the king commanded, and they took great costly stones for the foundation of the house, and unhewn stones. And the sons of Solomon and the sons of Chiram dressed them and laid them. In the fourth year he founded the house of the Lord in the month Niso, the second month. In the eleventh year, in the month Baal, this is the eighth month, the house was completed in every word of it and in every arrangement of it.

**1 Kings 6:2**

And the house that King Solomon built to the Lord: forty cubits was its length and twenty cubits in breadth and twenty-five cubits in height.

**1 Kings 6:3**

And the porch before the nave was twenty cubits in length, according to the breadth of the house, and its breadth before the house was ten cubits. And he built the house and finished it.

**1 Kings 6:4**

And he made to the house windows looking out, concealed.

**1 Kings 6:5**

And he set beam-structures upon the wall of the house all around, for the nave and for the debir, and he made side chambers all around.

**1 Kings 6:6**

The lower side chamber had a width of five cubits, and the middle six, and the third seven cubits in width, because he gave offsets to the house all around outside the house, so that they would not seize the walls of the house.

**1 Kings 6:7**

**1 Kings 6:8**

And the doorway of the lower side chamber was under the shoulder of the house on the right side, and a winding ascent led to the middle and from the middle to the third stories.

**1 Kings 6:9**

And he built the house and finished it and paneled the house with cedars.

**1 Kings 6:10**

And he built the bonds across the whole house, five cubits its height, and he fastened the bond with cedar woods.

**1 Kings 6:15**

And he built the walls of the house with cedar woods, from the floor of the house to the rafters and to the walls, and he paneled them continuously with woods inside, and he encircled the inside of the house with pine boards.

**1 Kings 6:16**

And he built the twenty cubits from the end of the house, the one side from the floor to the rafters, and he made the debir from it as the holy of holies.

**1 Kings 6:17**

And the nave in front was forty cubits.

**1 Kings 6:19**

The debir was in the middle of the house within, to place there the ark of the covenant of the Lord.

**1 Kings 6:20**

**1 Kings 6:21**

**1 Kings 6:22**

And the whole house he encircled with gold until the completion of the whole house.

**1 Kings 6:23**

**1 Kings 6:26**

And the height of the one cheroub was ten cubits, and so the second cheroub.

**1 Kings 6:28**

And he encircled the cheroubin with gold.

**1 Kings 6:29**

And all the walls of the house all around he engraved with a stylus, cheroubin and palms, the inner and the outer.

**1 Kings 6:30**

And the floor of the house he encircled with gold, of the innermost and of the outermost.

**1 Kings 6:31**

And for the doorway of the debir he made doors of juniper wood, and the doorposts were fivefold.

**1 Kings 6:32**

**1 Kings 6:33**

And thus he made for the gateway of the nave doorposts of juniper wood, four-sided porches.

**1 Kings 6:34**

And on both doors were pine woods, two folds on the one door and their turnings, and two folds on the second door turning.

**1 Kings 6:35**

**1 Kings 6:36**

And he built the innermost court, three rows of hewn stone and a row of worked cedar all around. And he built a curtain for the court of the porch of the house that was before the nave.

### Chapter 7

**1 Kings 7:1**

son of a widow woman, and he was from the tribe of Nephthali, and his father was a Tyrian man, a craftsman in bronze, and he was filled with skill and understanding and knowledge to do every work in bronze. And he was brought to King Solomon and did all the works.

the four hundred pomegranates for both networks, two rows of pomegranates for the one network, to cover both twisted works upon both pillars,
