**1 Kings 7:31**

and the pots and the shovels and the bowls and all the vessels that Chiram made for King Solomon for the house of the Lord, and the forty-eight pillars of the house of the king and of the house of the Lord, all the works of the king that Chiram made, all entirely of bronze.

**1 Kings 7:32**

There was no weight for the bronze from which he made all these works because of the very great abundance. There was no end to the weighing of the bronze.

**1 Kings 7:33**

In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the thickness of the earth, between Sokchoth and between Sira.

**1 Kings 7:34**

And King Solomon gave the vessels that he made in the house of the Lord: the golden altar, and the golden table on which were the loaves of offering,

**1 Kings 7:35**

and the lampstands, five at the right and five at the left before the debir, of closed gold, and the lamps and the wicks and the libation-bowls of gold,

**1 Kings 7:36**

and the doorposts and the nails and the bowls and the pans and the censers of closed gold, and the hinges of the doors of the innermost house, holy of holies, and the doors of the house of the nave, of gold.

**1 Kings 7:37**

And all the work that Solomon made for the house of the Lord was completed, and Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father and all the holy things of Solomon, the silver and the gold and the vessels, and he put them into the treasuries of the house of the Lord.

**1 Kings 7:38**

And Solomon built his own house in thirteen years.

**1 Kings 7:39**

And he built the House of the Forest of Lebanon, one hundred cubits its length and fifty cubits its breadth and thirty cubits its height, with three rows of cedar pillars and cedar shoulders upon the pillars.

**1 Kings 7:40**

And he roofed the house above upon the sides of the pillars, and the number of the pillars was forty-five, fifteen in a row.

**1 Kings 7:41**

And three beam-frames, and opening facing opening, threefold.

**1 Kings 7:42**

And all the doors and the openings were squared with beam-work, and from door to door, threefold.

**1 Kings 7:43**

And the Porch of the Pillars was fifty cubits in length and thirty in breadth, fitted in balance, a porch before them, and pillars and a thickness before it for the porches.

**1 Kings 7:44**

And the Porch of the Throne, where he would judge there, the Porch of Judgment.

**1 Kings 7:45**

And his house where he would sit there, one court winding around these, according to this work, and a house for the daughter of Pharao whom Solomon took, according to this porch.

**1 Kings 7:46**

All these were of costly stones, dressed according to interval, inside and from the foundation to the coping and outside to the great court,

**1 Kings 7:47**

founded with costly stones, great stones, ten-cubit stones and eight-cubit stones,

**1 Kings 7:48**

and above with costly stones according to the measure of hewn stones and cedars,

**1 Kings 7:49**

the great court all around, three rows of hewn stones and a row of dressed cedar,

**1 Kings 7:50**

and Solomon completed his whole house.

### Chapter 8

**1 Kings 8:1**

And it came to be when Solomon finished building the house of the Lord and his own house, after twenty years, then King Solomon assembled all the elders of Israel in Sion, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the City of David, this is Sion.

**1 Kings 8:2**

In the month Athanin.

**1 Kings 8:3**

And the priests lifted the ark,

**1 Kings 8:4**

and the tent of witness and all the holy vessels that were in the tent of witness,

**1 Kings 8:5**

and the king and all Israel before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle beyond number.

**1 Kings 8:6**

And the priests bring the ark to its place, into the debir of the house, into the holy of holies, under the wings of the cheroubin,

**1 Kings 8:7**

because the cheroubin had their wings spread over the place of the ark, and the cheroubin were covering the ark and its holy things from above.

**1 Kings 8:8**

And the holy poles projected, and the heads of the holy poles were seen from the holy place before the debir, but they were not visible outside.

**1 Kings 8:9**

There was nothing in the ark except two stone tablets, tablets of the covenant, which Moyses put there in Choreb, which the Lord covenanted with the sons of Israel when they came out from the land of Egypt.

**1 Kings 8:10**

And it came to be, as the priests came out from the holy place, that the cloud filled the house,

**1 Kings 8:11**

and the priests were not able to stand to minister because of the cloud, because the glory of the Lord filled the house.

**1 Kings 8:14**

And the king turned his face and the king blessed all Israel, and all the assembly of Israel was standing.

**1 Kings 8:15**

And he said, Blessed is the Lord God of Israel today, who spoke with his mouth concerning David my father and with his hands fulfilled it, saying,

**1 Kings 8:16**

From the day I brought out my people Israel from Egypt, I did not choose a city in one scepter of Israel to build a house for my name to be there, but I chose Ierousalem for my name to be there, and I chose David to be over my people Israel.

**1 Kings 8:17**

And it came to be upon the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.

**1 Kings 8:18**

And the Lord said to David my father, Because it came upon your heart to build a house for my name, you did well, because it came upon your heart.

**1 Kings 8:19**

Yet you shall not build the house, but only your son, the one coming out from your sides, he will build the house for my name.

**1 Kings 8:20**

And the Lord raised up his word that he spoke, and I rose in place of David my father and sat upon the throne of Israel just as the Lord spoke, and I built the house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.

**1 Kings 8:21**

And I placed there a place for the ark, in which is there the covenant of the Lord, which the Lord covenanted with our fathers when he brought them out from the land of Egypt.

**1 Kings 8:22**

And Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord in the sight of all the assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward heaven,

**1 Kings 8:23**

and said, O Lord God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above and upon the earth below, keeping covenant and mercy for your servant who walks before you with all his heart,

**1 Kings 8:24**

the things which you kept for your servant David my father, and you spoke with your mouth and fulfilled with your hands, as on this day.

**1 Kings 8:25**

And now, Lord God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father the things you spoke to him, saying, A man for you will not be lifted away from before me, sitting upon the throne of Israel, if only your children keep their ways to walk before me as you walked before me.

**1 Kings 8:26**

And now, Lord God of Israel, let your word be made firm for David my father.

**1 Kings 8:27**

For will God truly dwell with humans upon the earth? If heaven and heaven of heaven will not suffice for you, much less this house that I built for your name.

**1 Kings 8:28**

And yet look upon my petition, Lord God of Israel, to hear the delight with which your servant prays before you today,

**1 Kings 8:29**

for your eyes to be opened toward this house day and night, toward the place of which you said, My name will be there, to hear the prayer that your servant prays toward this place day and night,

**1 Kings 8:30**

and you will hear the petition of your servant and of your people Israel, whatever they pray toward this place. And you will hear in the place of your dwelling in heaven, and you will act and be gracious.

**1 Kings 8:31**

Whatever each person sins against his neighbor, and if he takes upon himself a curse to curse him, and comes and declares openly before your altar in this house,

**1 Kings 8:32**

then you will hear from heaven and act and judge your people Israel, to condemn the lawless by giving his way upon his own head, and to justify the righteous by giving to him according to his righteousness.

**1 Kings 8:33**

When your people Israel stumble before enemies because they sinned against you, and they turn back and confess to your name and pray and entreat in this house,

**1 Kings 8:34**

then you will hear from heaven and be gracious to the sins of your people Israel and return them to the land that you gave to their fathers.

**1 Kings 8:35**

When heaven is shut and rain does not come because they sinned against you, and they pray toward this place and confess to your name and turn back from their sins when you humble them,

**1 Kings 8:36**

then you will hear from heaven and be gracious to the sins of your servant and of your people Israel, because you will show them the good way to walk in it, and you will give rain upon the land that you gave to your people for an inheritance.

**1 Kings 8:37**

If famine happens, if death happens, if blight happens, mildew, locust, rust, if his enemy afflicts him in one of his cities, every encounter, every pain,

**1 Kings 8:38**

every prayer, every petition, whatever happens to any person, as each knows the touch of his own heart and spreads out his hands toward this house,

**1 Kings 8:39**

then you will hear from heaven from your ready dwelling place and be gracious and act and give to each man according to his ways, as you know his heart, because you alone know the heart of all the sons of humans,

**1 Kings 8:40**

so that they may fear you all the days they live upon the land that you gave to our fathers.

**1 Kings 8:41**

And also for the foreigner who is not from this people of yours,

**1 Kings 8:42**

and they will come and pray toward this place,

**1 Kings 8:43**

then you will hear from heaven from your ready dwelling place and do according to all that the foreigner calls on you for, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you as your people Israel do, and may know that your name is called upon this house that I built.

**1 Kings 8:44**

When your people go out to war against their enemies by the way that you send them, and they pray in the name of the Lord in the direction of the city that I chose in it and of the house that I built for your name,

**1 Kings 8:45**

then you will hear from heaven their petition and their prayer and do justice for them.

**1 Kings 8:46**

Because they will sin against you, for there is no human who will not sin, and you will bring against them and deliver them before enemies, and those who capture them will carry them captive to a far land or near,

**1 Kings 8:47**

and they will turn their hearts back in the land where they were carried there and turn and entreat you in the land of their migration, saying, We sinned, we acted lawlessly, we did wrong,

**1 Kings 8:48**

and turn to you with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their enemies where you carried them away, and they pray toward you in the direction of their land that you gave to their fathers, the city that I chose and the house that I built for your name,

**1 Kings 8:49**

then you will hear from heaven from your ready dwelling place

**1 Kings 8:50**

and be gracious to their wrongs by which they sinned against you and to all their rebellions with which they rebelled against you, and you will give them into compassions before those taking them captive, and they will pity them,

**1 Kings 8:51**

because they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out from the land of Egypt, from the midst of the iron furnace.

**1 Kings 8:52**

And let your eyes and your ears be opened toward the petition of your servant and toward the petition of your people Israel, to hear them in all things whatsoever they call on you for,

**1 Kings 8:53**

because you set them apart to yourself for an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, just as you spoke by the hand of your servant Moyses, when you brought out our fathers from the land of Egypt, O Lord, Lord. Then Solomon spoke concerning the house, as he finished building it: The sun the Lord made known in heaven. He said he would dwell in gloom. Build my house, a splendid house for yourself, for dwelling in newness. Behold, is not this written in the Book of the Song?

**1 Kings 8:54**

And it came to be when Solomon finished praying to the Lord all this prayer and petition, he rose from before the altar of the Lord, kneeling upon his knees and his hands spread out toward heaven,

**1 Kings 8:55**

and stood and blessed all the assembly of Israel with a loud voice, saying,

**1 Kings 8:56**

Blessed is the Lord today, who gave rest to his people Israel according to all that he spoke. Not one word failed from all his good words that he spoke by the hand of Moyses his servant.

**1 Kings 8:57**

May the Lord our God be with us just as he was with our fathers. May he not leave us nor turn away from us,

**1 Kings 8:58**

to incline our hearts toward him, to walk in all his ways and keep all his commandments and his ordinances, which he commanded our fathers.

**1 Kings 8:59**

And let these words, which I have entreated before the Lord our God, be near to the Lord our God day and night, to do the justice of your servant and the justice of his people Israel, the matter of each day in its day,

**1 Kings 8:60**

so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord, he is God, and there is no other.

**1 Kings 8:61**

And let our hearts be perfect toward the Lord our God and holy in walking in his ordinances and keeping his commandments, as on this day.

**1 Kings 8:62**

And the king and all the sons of Israel sacrificed a sacrifice before the Lord.

**1 Kings 8:63**

And King Solomon sacrificed the sacrifices of peace offerings that he sacrificed to the Lord, twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred twenty thousand sheep. And the king and all the sons of Israel dedicated the house of the Lord.

**1 Kings 8:64**

On that day the king consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of the Lord, because there he made the whole burnt offering and the sacrifices and the fats of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that was before the Lord was too small to carry the whole burnt offering and the sacrifices of the peace offerings.

**1 Kings 8:65**

And Solomon kept the feast on that day, and all Israel with him, a great assembly, from the entrance of Emath to the river of Egypt, before the Lord our God, in the house that he built, eating and drinking and rejoicing before the Lord our God for seven days.

**1 Kings 8:66**

And on the eighth day he sent away the people and blessed them, and they went each to his tents, rejoicing and good of heart over the good things that the Lord did for David his servant and for Israel his people.

### Chapter 9

**1 Kings 9:1**

And it came to be, when Solomon finished building the house of the Lord and the house of the king and all the workmanship of Solomon, whatever he desired to do,

**1 Kings 9:2**

that the Lord appeared to Solomon a second time, just as he appeared at Gabaon.

**1 Kings 9:3**

And the Lord said to him, I have heard the voice of your prayer and your petition with which you petitioned before me. I have done for you according to all your prayer. I have made this house holy that you built, to put my name there forever, and my eyes and my heart will be there all the days.

**1 Kings 9:4**

And you, if you walk before me just as David your father walked, in holiness of heart and in uprightness, doing according to all that I commanded him, and if you keep my ordinances and my commandments,

**1 Kings 9:5**

**1 Kings 9:6**

But if by turning away you turn away, you and your children, from me and do not keep my commandments and my ordinances that Moyses gave before you, and you go and serve other gods and bow to them,

**1 Kings 9:7**

**1 Kings 9:8**

And this house, exalted as it is, everyone passing through it will be astonished and will hiss, and they will say, For what cause did the Lord do thus to this land and to this house?

**1 Kings 9:9**

And they will say, Because they forsook the Lord their God who brought their fathers out of Egypt, from the house of slavery, and they held fast to foreign gods and bowed to them and served them. Therefore the Lord brought upon them this evil. Then Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharao from the City of David to his house that he built for himself in those days.

**1 Kings 9:10**

Twenty years in which Solomon built the two houses, the house of the Lord and the house of the king,

**1 Kings 9:11**

Chiram king of Tyre had supported Solomon with cedar woods and pine woods and with gold and with all his desire. Then the king gave to Chiram twenty cities in the land of Galilaia.

**1 Kings 9:12**

And Chiram went out from Tyre and went to Galilaia to see the cities that Solomon gave him, and they were not pleasing to him.

**1 Kings 9:13**

And he said, What are these cities that you gave me, brother? And he called them Border until this day.

**1 Kings 9:14**

And Chiram brought to Solomon one hundred and twenty talents of gold.

**1 Kings 9:26**

And the king Solomon made a ship at Gasiongaber, which is near Ailath on the shore of the last sea, in the land of Edom.

**1 Kings 9:27**

And Chiram sent in the ship his servants, seafaring men skilled to drive the sea, with the servants of Solomon.

**1 Kings 9:28**

And they came to Sopheira and took from there one hundred and twenty talents of gold and brought them to King Solomon.

### Chapter 10

**1 Kings 10:1**

And the queen of Saba heard Solomon's name and the name of the Lord and came to test him with riddles.

**1 Kings 10:2**

And she came to Ierousalem with a very heavy force and camels carrying spices and very much gold and costly stone, and she entered to Solomon and spoke to him all that was in her heart.

**1 Kings 10:3**

And Solomon reported to her all her words. There was not a word hidden from the king that he did not report to her.

**1 Kings 10:4**

And the queen of Saba saw all the understanding of Solomon and the house that he built,

**1 Kings 10:5**

and the foods of Solomon and the seating of his servants and the standing of his ministers and his clothing and his cupbearers and his whole burnt offering that he offered up in the house of the Lord, and she was beside herself.

**1 Kings 10:6**

And she said to King Solomon, True is the word that I heard in my land concerning your words and concerning your understanding.

**1 Kings 10:7**

And I did not believe those speaking to me until I came and my eyes saw. And behold, it is not even half according to what they reported to me. You have added goodness to all the report that I heard in my land.

**1 Kings 10:8**

Blessed are your women. Blessed are these servants of yours who stand before you continually, hearing all your understanding.

**1 Kings 10:9**

May the Lord your God be blessed, who delighted in you to give you upon the throne of Israel, because the Lord loved Israel to establish it forever, and he set you as king over them to do judgment in righteousness and in their judgments.

**1 Kings 10:10**

And she gave to Solomon one hundred and twenty talents of gold and very many spices and costly stone. Such a multitude of spices as those that the queen of Saba gave to King Solomon had not come again.

**1 Kings 10:11**

And the ship of Chiram, carrying the gold from Souphir, brought very many worked timbers and costly stone.

**1 Kings 10:12**

And the king made the worked timbers into supports for the house of the Lord and for the house of the king and lyres and harps for the singers. Such worked timbers had not come upon the earth nor been seen anywhere until this day.

**1 Kings 10:13**

And King Solomon gave to the queen of Saba all that she desired, whatever she asked, besides all that he had given her by the hand of King Solomon. And she turned and went to her land, she and all her servants.

**1 Kings 10:14**

And the weight of the gold coming to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,

**1 Kings 10:15**

besides the levies of the subjects and the merchants and all the kings from beyond and the satraps of the land.

**1 Kings 10:16**

And Solomon made three hundred beaten-gold spears. Three hundred gold pieces were upon each spear.

**1 Kings 10:17**

And three hundred beaten-gold shields, three minas of gold were in each shield, and he put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

**1 Kings 10:18**

And the king made a great ivory throne and covered it around with refined gold.

**1 Kings 10:19**

Six steps belonged to the throne, and backs of calves belonged to the throne behind it, and hands on this side and on that side of the seat, and two lions standing beside the hands.

**1 Kings 10:20**

And twelve lions standing upon the six steps on this side and on that. Thus it was not made for any kingdom.

**1 Kings 10:21**

And all the drinking vessels of Solomon were golden, and the wash-basins were golden, all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon, of closed gold. There was no silver, because it was not reckoned in the days of Solomon.

**1 Kings 10:22**

For the king had a ship of Tharsis in the sea with the ships of Chiram. Once every three years a ship from Tharsis would come to the king, bringing gold and silver and carved and hewn stones. This was the undertaking of the spoil that King Solomon brought up, to build the house of the Lord and the house of the king and the wall of Ierousalem and the citadel, to fence the enclosure of the City of David, and Assour and Magdan and Gazer and upper Baithoron and Iethermath and all the chariot-cities and all the horse-cities and the enterprise of Solomon that he undertook to build in Ierousalem and in all the land from the beginning of his rule. All the people remaining from the Chettite and the Amorraite and the Pherezzaite and the Chananite and the Heuite and the Iebousaite and the Gergesaean, who were not from the sons of Israel, whose children remained after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel were not able to destroy utterly, Solomon brought them up into levy until this day. But from the sons of Israel Solomon did not assign any to forced work, because they were the warrior men and his servants and his rulers of his chariots and his horsemen.

**1 Kings 10:23**

And Solomon was made greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and understanding.

**1 Kings 10:24**

And all the kings of the earth were seeking the face of Solomon to hear his understanding that the Lord put in his heart.

**1 Kings 10:25**

And they were bringing each his gifts: golden vessels and clothing and myrrh and spices and horses and mules, according to year by year.

**1 Kings 10:26**

And Solomon had four thousand brood mares for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he placed them in the cities of the chariots and with the king in Ierousalem. And he was ruling all the kings from the river even to the land of the foreigners and to the borders of Egypt.

**1 Kings 10:27**

And the king made the gold and the silver in Ierousalem like stones, and the cedars he made like the sycamores in the plain in multitude.

**1 Kings 10:28**

And the export of the horses of Solomon was from Egypt and from Thekoue. The merchants of the king were receiving them from Thekoue by exchange.

**1 Kings 10:29**

And an export chariot would come up from Egypt for one hundred silver pieces and a horse for fifty silver pieces, and so they would go out by sea for all the kings of the Chettiin and the kings of Syria.

### Chapter 11

**1 Kings 11:1**

And King Solomon was a lover of women, and he had seven hundred wives who were rulers and three hundred concubines, and he took foreign wives, and the daughter of Pharao, Moabites, Ammonites, Syrians, Idumeans, Chettites, and Amorrites,

**1 Kings 11:2**

from the nations of which the Lord said to the sons of Israel, You shall not go in to them, and they shall not go in to you, lest they turn your hearts aside after their idols. To these Solomon clung, to love.

**1 Kings 11:4**

And it came to be in the time of Solomon's old age, and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God like the heart of David his father, and the foreign women turned aside his heart after their gods.

**1 Kings 11:5**

Then Solomon built a high place for Chamos, idol of Moab, and for their king, idol of the sons of Ammon,

**1 Kings 11:6**

and for Astarte, abomination of the Sidonians.

**1 Kings 11:7**

And thus he did for all his foreign wives, burning incense and sacrificing to their idols.

**1 Kings 11:8**

And Solomon did evil before the Lord. He did not walk after the Lord as David his father did.

**1 Kings 11:9**

And the Lord was angered against Solomon because he turned his heart away from the Lord God of Israel, who appeared to him twice,

**1 Kings 11:10**

and who had commanded him concerning this matter, not at all to go after other gods, and to keep and do what the Lord God commanded him.

**1 Kings 11:11**

And the Lord said to Solomon, Because these things came to be with you and you did not keep my commandments and my ordinances that I commanded you, in tearing I will tear your kingdom out of your hand and give it to your servant.

**1 Kings 11:12**

Yet in your days I will not do it, for the sake of David your father. From the hand of your son I will take it.

**1 Kings 11:13**

Yet I will not take the whole kingdom. I will give one scepter to your son for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Ierousalem, the city that I chose.

**1 Kings 11:14**

And the Lord raised up an adversary against Solomon, Ader the Idumean, and Esrom son of Eliadae, who was in Raemmath, of Adrazar king of Souba his lord. And men were gathered to him, and he was chief of a band, and he took Damascus beforehand, and they were an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon. And Ader the Idumean was from the seed of the kingdom in Idumea.

**1 Kings 11:15**

And it happened when David was destroying Edom, when Ioab commander of the army went to bury the wounded, they cut down every male in Idumea.

**1 Kings 11:16**

For six months Ioab and all Israel sat there in Idumea until he destroyed every male from Idumea.

**1 Kings 11:17**

And Ader fled, he and all the Idumean men from the servants of his father with him, and they entered into Egypt, and Ader was a small boy.

**1 Kings 11:18**

And men rose from the city of Madiam and came to Pharan and took men with them and came to Pharao king of Egypt. And Ader entered to Pharao, and he gave him a house and appointed bread for him.

**1 Kings 11:19**

And Ader found favor before Pharao greatly, and he gave him as wife the sister of his own wife, sister of Thekeminas the elder.

**1 Kings 11:20**

And the sister of Thekeminas bore to Ader Ganebath her son, and Thekemina brought him up in the midst of the sons of Pharao, and Ganebath was in the midst of the sons of Pharao.

**1 Kings 11:21**

And Ader heard in Egypt that David had slept with his fathers and that Ioab the commander of the army had died, and Ader said to Pharao, Send me away, and I will return to my land.

**1 Kings 11:22**

And Pharao said to Ader, In what are you lacking with me? And behold, you seek to go away to your land. And Ader said to him, In sending away, send me away. And Ader returned to his land.

**1 Kings 11:25**

This was the evil that Ader did, and he was disgusted with Israel, and he reigned in the land of Edom.

**1 Kings 11:26**

And Ieroboam son of Nabat, the Ephrathite from Sarira, son of a widow woman, a servant of Solomon,

**1 Kings 11:27**

and this was the matter in which he lifted his hands against King Solomon: he built the citadel; he closed up the breach of the City of David his father.

**1 Kings 11:28**

And the man Ieroboam was strong in power, and Solomon saw the young man that he was a man of works, and he appointed him over the burdens of the house of Ioseph.

**1 Kings 11:29**

And it came to be at that time that Ieroboam went out from Ierousalem, and Achias the Selonite the prophet found him on the road, and he pulled him off the road. And Achias was clothed with a new garment, and both were in the open country.

**1 Kings 11:30**

And Achias took hold of his new garment that was upon him and tore it into twelve pieces.

**1 Kings 11:31**

And he said to Ieroboam, Take for yourself ten pieces, because thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I am tearing the kingdom from the hand of Solomon, and I will give you ten scepters.

**1 Kings 11:32**

And two scepters will belong to him for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Ierousalem, the city that I chose in it from all the tribes of Israel,

**1 Kings 11:33**

because he forsook me and did to Astarte, abomination of the Sidonians, and to Chamos and to the idols of Moab and to their king, provocation of the sons of Ammon, and he did not walk in my ways to do what is right before me, as David his father did.

**1 Kings 11:34**

And I will not take the whole kingdom from his hand, because in resisting I will resist him all the days of his life for the sake of David my servant, whom I chose.

**1 Kings 11:35**

And I will take the kingdom from the hand of his son and give you the ten scepters.

**1 Kings 11:36**

And to his son I will give the two scepters, so that there may be a setting for my servant David all the days before me in Ierousalem, the city that I chose for myself to put my name there.

**1 Kings 11:37**

And I will take you, and you will reign over whatever your soul desires, and you will be king over Israel.

**1 Kings 11:38**

And it will be, if you keep all that I command you and walk in my ways and do what is right before me, to keep my commandments and my ordinances just as David my servant did, then I will be with you and build for you a faithful house just as I built for David.

**1 Kings 11:40**

And Solomon sought to put Ieroboam to death, and he rose and fled into Egypt to Sousakim king of Egypt and was in Egypt until Solomon died.

**1 Kings 11:41**

And the rest of the matters of Solomon and all that he did and all his understanding, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of Solomon?

**1 Kings 11:42**

And King Solomon slept with his fathers, and Roboam his son reigned in place of him.

**1 Kings 12:1**

**1 Kings 12:14**

**1 Kings 12:22**

**1 Kings 12:23**

Speak to Roboam son of Solomon, king of Iouda, and to all the house of Iouda and Benjamin and to the remnant of the people, saying,

**1 Kings 12:24**

Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up nor fight with your brothers, sons of Israel. Let each return to his own house, because this word has happened from me. And they heard the word of the Lord and stopped from going according to the word of the Lord. And King Solomon sleeps with his fathers and is buried with his fathers in the City of David, and Roboam his son reigned in place of him in Ierousalem, being sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twelve years in Ierousalem, and the name of his mother was Naanan daughter of Anan son of Naas king of the sons of Ammon, and he did evil before the Lord and did not walk in the way of David his father. And there was a man from the hill country of Ephraim, servant to Solomon, and his name was Ieroboam, and his mother's name was Sarira, a prostitute woman, and Solomon gave him as chief officer of the staff over the burdens of the house of Ioseph, and he built for Solomon Sarira in the hill country of Ephraim, and he had three hundred chariots of horses. This one built the citadel among the burdens of the house of Ephraim. This one closed up the City of David and was being lifted up against the kingdom. And Solomon sought to put him to death, and he feared and fled to Sousakim king of Egypt and was with him until Solomon died. And Ieroboam heard in Egypt that Solomon died, and he spoke into the ears of Sousakim king of Egypt, saying, Send me away, and I will depart to my land. And Sousakim said to him, Ask what request and I will give it to you. And Sousakim gave to Ieroboam the elder sister of Thekemina, his own wife, for a wife. She was great among the daughters of the king and bore to Ieroboam Abia his son. And Ieroboam said to Sousakim, Truly send me away, and I will depart. And Ieroboam went out from Egypt and came to the land of Sarira in the hill country of Ephraim and gathered there all the scepter of Ephraim and built a fort there. And his young child became very sick with a very severe sickness, and Ieroboam went to inquire concerning the child, and he said to Ano his wife, Rise and go inquire of God concerning the child, whether he will live from his sickness. And there was a man in Selom, and his name was Achias, and he was sixty years old, and the word of the Lord was with him. And Ieroboam said to his wife, Rise and take in your hand to the man of God loaves and cakes for his children and grapes and a jar of honey. And the woman rose and took in her hand loaves and two cakes and grapes and a jar of honey for Achias, and the man was old and his eyes were dim from seeing. And she rose from Sarira and went. And it came to be when she entered the city to Achias the Selonite, Achias said to his young servant, Go out now to meet Ano wife of Ieroboam and say to her, Come in and do not stand still, because thus says the Lord: Hard things I am sending upon you. And Ano entered to the man of God, and Achias said to her, Why have you brought me loaves and grapes and cakes and a jar of honey? Thus says the Lord: Behold, you will depart from me, and it will be when you enter the gate into Sarira and your maidens come out to meet you and say to you, The child has died, because thus says the Lord: Behold, I will destroy from Ieroboam one urinating against a wall, and those dying of Ieroboam in the city dogs will devour, and the one dying in the field the birds of heaven will devour, and for the child they will mourn. Alas, Lord, because a good word concerning the Lord was found in him. And the woman departed when she heard, and it came to be when she entered into Sarira, the child died and the cry went out to meet her. And Ieroboam went to Sikima in the hill country of Ephraim and gathered there the tribes of Israel, and Roboam son of Solomon went up there. And the word of the Lord came to Samaias the Elamite, saying, Take for yourself a new garment not yet entered into water and tear it into twelve pieces, and give them to Ieroboam and say to him, Thus says the Lord: Take for yourself ten pieces to put on, and Ieroboam took them, and Samaias said, Thus says the Lord concerning the ten tribes of Israel. And the people said to Roboam son of Solomon, Your father made his yoke heavy upon us and made the foods of his table heavy. And now, if you lighten things upon us, we will serve you. And Roboam said to the people, In three days I will answer you a word. And he said, Bring in to me the elders and I will take counsel with them what word I should answer the people on the third day. And Roboam spoke into their ears, just as the people sent to him, and the elders said, Thus the people spoke to you. And Roboam scattered their counsel, and it was not pleasing before him, and he sent and brought in his companions and spoke these same things to them: Thus the people sent to me. And his companions said, Thus you will speak to the people, saying, My littleness is thicker than my father's loin. My father whipped you with whips, but I will rule you with scorpions. And the word was pleasing before Roboam, and he answered the people just as his companions, the young men, counseled him. And all the people cried out as one man, each to his neighbor, and they all cried aloud, saying, There is no share for us in David and no inheritance in the son of Iessai. To your tents, Israel, because this man is not for ruler nor for leader. And all the people were scattered from Sikim and each went to his tent, and Roboam prevailed and went and mounted his chariot and entered into Ierousalem, and all the scepter of Iouda and all the scepter of Benjamin went after him. And it came to be at the turn of the year, and Roboam gathered all the men of Iouda and Benjamin and went up to war against Ieroboam at Sikima. And the word of the Lord came to Samaias the man of God, saying, Speak to Roboam king of Iouda and to all the house of Iouda and Benjamin and to the remnant of the people, saying, Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up nor fight against your brothers the sons of Israel. Return each to his house, because this word has happened from me. And they heard the word of the Lord and held back from going according to the word of the Lord.

**1 Kings 16:28**

And Ambri slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and Achaab his son reigned in place of him. And in the eleventh year of Ambri, Iosaphat son of Asa reigned, thirty-five years old in his reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Ierousalem, and his mother's name was Gazouba daughter of Selei. And he walked in the way of Asa his father and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right before the Lord, except the high places they did not remove; they sacrificed on the high places and burned incense. And the rest of the alliances that Iosaphat made and all the dominion that he exercised and those against whom he fought, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Iouda? And the rest of the entanglements that were imposed in the days of Asa his father he removed from the land. And there was no king in Syria, only a deputy. And King Iosaphat made a ship for Tharsis to go to Sophir for gold, and it did not go because the ship was broken at Gasiongaber. Then the king of Israel said to Iosaphat, I will send your servants and my servants in the ship, and Iosaphat was not willing. And Iosaphat slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and Ioram his son reigned in place of him.

**1 Kings 16:29**

In the second year of Iosaphat, Achaab son of Ambri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.

**1 Kings 16:30**

And Achaab did evil before the Lord. He did worse than all those before him.

**1 Kings 16:31**

And it was not enough for him to walk in the sins of Ieroboam son of Nabat, and he took Iezabel daughter of Iethebaal king of the Sidonians for a wife and went and served Baal and bowed down to him.

**1 Kings 16:32**

And he set up an altar to Baal in the house of his abominations, which he built in Samaria.

**1 Kings 16:33**

And Achaab made a grove, and Achaab added by making provocations, provoking his own soul toward destruction. He did evil beyond all the kings of Israel who came before him.

**1 Kings 16:34**

In his days Achiēl the Baithēlite built Iericho. In Abirōn his firstborn he founded it, and in Segoub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word of the Lord that he spoke by the hand of Iēsous son of Nauē.

### Chapter 17

**1 Kings 17:1**

And Elijah the prophet, the Thesbite from Thesbon of Galaad, said to Achaab, As the Lord God of hosts, God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, these years there shall be no dew and rain except by the word of my mouth.

**1 Kings 17:2**

And word of the Lord came to Elijah,

**1 Kings 17:3**

Go from here eastward and hide yourself by the wadi Chorrath, the one before the Jordan.

**1 Kings 17:4**

And it shall be, you will drink water from the wadi, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.

**1 Kings 17:5**

And Elijah did according to the word of the Lord and sat by the wadi Chorrath before the Jordan.

**1 Kings 17:6**

And the ravens brought him breads in the morning and meat in the evening, and he drank water from the wadi.

**1 Kings 17:7**

And it came to be after days, the wadi dried up because no rain came upon the land.

**1 Kings 17:8**

And word of the Lord came to Elijah,

**1 Kings 17:9**

Rise and go to Sarepta of Sidonia. Behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to feed you.

**1 Kings 17:10**

And he rose and went to Sarepta, to the gate of the city, and behold, there a widow woman was gathering sticks. And Elijah cried after her and said to her, Please fetch me a little water in a vessel and I will drink.

**1 Kings 17:11**

And as she went to fetch it, Elijah cried after her and said, Please take for me a morsel of bread in your hand.

**1 Kings 17:12**

And the woman said, As the Lord your God lives, I have no cake except as much as a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the jug, and behold, I am gathering two little sticks and will go in and make it for myself and my children, and we will eat and die.

**1 Kings 17:13**

And Elijah said to her, Take courage. Go in and do according to your word, but first make for me from there a little cake and bring it out to me, and for yourself and your children you will make it afterward.

**1 Kings 17:14**

For thus says the Lord: the jar of flour will not fail and the jug of oil will not lessen until the day the Lord gives rain upon the land.

**1 Kings 17:15**

And the woman went and did, and she and he and her children were eating.

**1 Kings 17:16**

And the jar of flour did not fail, and the jug of oil did not lessen, according to the word of the Lord that he spoke by the hand of Elijah.

**1 Kings 17:17**

And it came to be after these things, the son of the woman, mistress of the house, became sick, and his sickness was very severe until no breath was left in him.

**1 Kings 17:18**

And she said to Elijah, What is to me and to you, man of God? You entered to me to bring my injustices to remembrance and to put my son to death.

**1 Kings 17:19**

And Elijah said to the woman, Give me your son. And he took him from her bosom and brought him up into the upper room where he himself sat there and laid him upon his bed.

**1 Kings 17:20**

And Elijah cried out and said, Alas, Lord, witness of the widow with whom I dwell, with her you have done evil, by putting her son to death?

**1 Kings 17:21**

And he breathed on the child three times and called upon the Lord and said, Lord my God, let the soul of this child now return into him.

**1 Kings 17:22**

And it came to be so, and the child cried out.

**1 Kings 17:23**

And he brought him down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother, and Elijah said, Look, your son lives.

**1 Kings 17:24**

And the woman said to Elijah, Behold, I now know that you are a man of God and the word of the Lord in your mouth is true.

### Chapter 18

**1 Kings 18:1**

And it came to be after many days, the word of the Lord came to Elijah in the third year, saying, Go and appear to Achaab, and I will give rain upon the face of the earth.

**1 Kings 18:2**

And Elijah went to appear to Achaab, and the famine was severe in Samaria.

**1 Kings 18:3**

And Achaab called Abdiou the steward, and Abdiou was fearing the Lord greatly.

**1 Kings 18:4**

And it came to be when Iezabel was striking the prophets of the Lord, Abdiou took one hundred prophet-men and hid them by fifty in a cave and fed them with bread and water.

**1 Kings 18:5**

And Achaab said to Abdiou, Come, let us pass through the land, to the springs of the waters and to the wadis, if somehow we may find grass and preserve horses and mules, and they will not be destroyed from among the livestock.

**1 Kings 18:6**

And they divided for themselves the road to pass through it. Achaab went one road alone, and Abdiou went another road alone.

**1 Kings 18:7**

And Abdiou was on the road alone, and Elijah came to meet him alone, and Abdiou hurried and fell upon his face and said, Are you really my lord Elijah?

**1 Kings 18:8**

And Elijah said to him, I am. Go, tell your lord, Behold, Elijah.

**1 Kings 18:9**

And Abdiou said, What have I sinned, that you are giving your servant into the hand of Achaab to kill me?

**1 Kings 18:10**

As the Lord your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you, and they said, He is not here, and he bound the kingdom and its regions by oath that it had not found you.

**1 Kings 18:11**

And now you say, Go, announce to your lord, Behold, Elijah.

**1 Kings 18:12**

And it will be, if I go away from you, the Spirit of the Lord will carry you to a land that I do not know, and I will go in to report to Achaab, and he will kill me. Yet your servant has been fearing the Lord from his youth.

**1 Kings 18:13**

Was it not reported to you, my lord, what I did when Iezabel was killing the prophets of the Lord, that I hid one hundred men of the prophets of the Lord, fifty by fifty in a cave, and fed them with breads and water?

**1 Kings 18:14**

And now you say to me, Go, tell your lord, Behold, Elijah, and he will kill me.

**1 Kings 18:15**

And Elijah said, As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand, today I will appear to him.

**1 Kings 18:16**

And Abdiou went to meet Achaab and reported to him, and Achaab ran out and went to meet Elijah.

**1 Kings 18:17**

And it came to be when Achaab saw Elijah, Achaab said to Elijah, Are you really the one disturbing Israel?

**1 Kings 18:18**

And Elijah said, I am not disturbing Israel, but you and your father's house, in that you forsook the Lord your God and went after the Baalim.

**1 Kings 18:19**

And now send, gather to me all Israel at Mount Carmel and the prophets of the Shame, four hundred fifty, and the prophets of the groves, four hundred, eating Iezabel's table.

**1 Kings 18:20**

And Achaab sent to all Israel and gathered all the prophets at Mount Carmel.

**1 Kings 18:21**

And Elijah came near to all and said to them, How long will you limp on both knees? If the Lord is God, go after him; but if Baal is, go after him. And the people did not answer a word.

**1 Kings 18:22**

And Elijah said to the people, I alone am left as prophet of the Lord, utterly alone, and the prophets of Baal are four hundred fifty men and the prophets of the grove four hundred.

**1 Kings 18:23**

Let them give us two calves, and let them choose one for themselves and butcher it and place it upon the woods, and put no fire. And I will prepare the other bull, and I will certainly place no fire.

**1 Kings 18:24**

And call in the name of your gods, and I will call in the name of the Lord my God, and the god who answers by fire, he is God. And all the people answered and said, Good is the word that you spoke.

**1 Kings 18:25**

And Elijah said to the prophets of the Shame, Choose for yourselves the one calf and prepare it first, because you are many, and call in the name of your god, but put no fire.

**1 Kings 18:26**

And they took the calf and prepared it, and they kept calling in the name of Baal from morning until midday and said, Answer us, O Baal, answer us. And there was no voice, and there was no hearing, and they ran about on the altar that they made.

**1 Kings 18:27**

And it came to be at midday, Elijah the Thesbite mocked them and said, Call with a loud voice, because he is god. Surely he has talk on his mind, or perhaps he is occupied, or perhaps he sleeps and will awaken.

**1 Kings 18:28**

And they called with a loud voice and cut themselves according to their custom with swords and lances until blood poured out upon them.

**1 Kings 18:29**

And they prophesied until the evening passed, and it came to be at the time for the sacrifice to go up, and there was no voice. And Elijah the Thesbite spoke to the prophets of the abominations, saying, Stand aside now, and I will make my whole burnt offering. And they stood aside and went away.

**1 Kings 18:30**

And Elijah said to the people, Come near to me. And all the people came near to him.

**1 Kings 18:31**

And Elijah took twelve stones according to the number of the tribes of Israel, as the Lord spoke to him, saying, Israel shall be your name.

**1 Kings 18:32**

And he built the stones in the name of the Lord and healed the torn-down altar and made a trench around the altar, able to hold two measures of seed.

**1 Kings 18:33**

And he stacked the split wood upon the altar that he made and cut up the whole burnt offering and placed it upon the wood and stacked it upon the altar.

**1 Kings 18:34**

And he said, Take for me four jars of water and pour it upon the whole burnt offering and upon the wood. And they did so. And he said, Do it a second time, and they did it a second time. And he said, Do it a third time, and they did it a third time.

**1 Kings 18:35**

And the water kept going around the altar, and they filled the trench with water.

**1 Kings 18:36**

And Elijah cried out to heaven and said, Lord God of Abraam and Isaak and Israel, answer me, Lord, answer me today by fire, and let all this people know that you are Lord, God of Israel, and I am your servant, and because of you I have done these works.

**1 Kings 18:37**

Answer me, Lord, answer me by fire, and let this people know that you are the Lord, God, and you have turned back the heart of this people.

**1 Kings 18:38**

And fire from the Lord fell from heaven and devoured the whole burnt offering and the split wood and the water in the trench, and the fire licked up the stones and the dust.

**1 Kings 18:39**

And all the people fell on their faces and said, Truly the Lord, he is God, he is God.

**1 Kings 18:40**

And Elijah said to the people, Seize the prophets of Baal. Let not one of them be saved. And they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the wadi Kisōn and slaughtered them there.

**1 Kings 18:41**

And Elijah said to Achaab, Go up, eat and drink, because there is a sound of the feet of rain.

**1 Kings 18:42**

And Achaab went up to eat and drink, and Elijah went up upon Carmel and bent to the ground and put his face between his knees.

**1 Kings 18:43**

And he said to his servant-boy, Go up and look in the direction of the sea. And the servant-boy looked and said, There is nothing. And Elijah said, Then return seven times, and the servant-boy returned seven times.

**1 Kings 18:44**

And it came to be at the seventh time, behold, a little cloud like a man's footprint bringing up water, and he said, Go up and tell Achaab, Harness your chariot and go down, lest the rain overtake you.

**1 Kings 18:45**

And it came to be here and there, and the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and a great rain came, and Achaab wept and went to Iezrael.

**1 Kings 18:46**

And the hand of the Lord was upon Elijah, and he girded up his waist and ran before Achaab as far as Iezrael.

### Chapter 19

**1 Kings 19:1**

And Achaab reported to Iezabel his wife all that Elijah did and how he killed the prophets with the sword.

**1 Kings 19:2**

And Iezabel sent to Elijah and said, If you are Elijah and I am Iezabel, may God do thus to me and add thus, because by this time tomorrow I will make your life like the life of one of them.

**1 Kings 19:3**

And Elijah feared and rose and went for his own life, and he came to Bērsabee of Iouda and left his servant-boy there.

**1 Kings 19:4**

And he himself went in the wilderness a day's road and came and sat under one broom plant, and he asked for his life to die and said, Let it be enough now. Take away my life from me, Lord, because I am no better than my fathers.

**1 Kings 19:5**

And he lay down and slept there under a plant, and behold, someone touched him and said to him, Rise and eat.

**1 Kings 19:6**

And Elijah looked, and behold, at his head was a barley cake and a jug of water. And he rose and ate and drank and turned back and slept.

**1 Kings 19:7**

And the angel of the Lord returned a second time and touched him and said to him, Rise, eat, because the road is too much for you.

**1 Kings 19:8**

And he rose and ate and drank and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights as far as Mount Chōrēb.

**1 Kings 19:9**

And he entered there into the cave and lodged there. And behold, word of the Lord came to him and said, What are you doing here, Elijah?

**1 Kings 19:10**

And Elijah said, In zeal I have been very zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the sons of Israel forsook you, they tore down your altars, and they killed your prophets with the sword, and I alone am left, utterly alone, and they seek my life to take it.

**1 Kings 19:11**

And he said, You will go out tomorrow and stand before the Lord on the mountain. Behold, the Lord will pass by, and a great strong wind, dissolving mountains and crushing rocks before the Lord. The Lord was not in the wind. And after the wind, an earthquake. The Lord was not in the earthquake.

**1 Kings 19:12**

And after the earthquake, fire. The Lord was not in the fire. And after the fire, a voice of a thin breeze, and there the Lord.

**1 Kings 19:13**

And it came to be as Elijah heard, he covered his face with his sheepskin cloak and went out and stood under the cave. And behold, a voice came to him and said, What are you doing here, Elijah?

**1 Kings 19:14**

And Elijah said, In zeal I have been very zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the sons of Israel forsook your covenant, they pulled down your altars, and they killed your prophets with the sword, and I alone am left, utterly alone, and they seek my life to take it.

**1 Kings 19:15**

And the Lord said to him, Go, return on your way, and you will come to the wilderness road of Damascus, and you will anoint Azaēl king of Syria.

**1 Kings 19:16**

And Ieou son of Namessi you will anoint king over Israel, and Elisaie son of Saphat from Abelmaoula you will anoint prophet in your place.

**1 Kings 19:17**

And it shall be, the one escaping from the sword of Azaēl, Ieou will put to death, and the one escaping from the sword of Ieou, Elisaie will put to death.

**1 Kings 19:18**

And you will leave in Israel seven thousand men, every knee that did not bend knee to Baal and every mouth that did not bow to him.

**1 Kings 19:19**

And he went away from there and found Elisaie son of Saphat, and he was plowing with twelve pairs of oxen before him, and he himself was with the twelve, and Elijah came upon him and threw his sheepskin cloak upon him.

**1 Kings 19:20**

And Elisaie left the oxen and ran after Elijah and said, Let me kiss my father, and I will follow after you. And Elijah said, Return, because what have I done to you?

**1 Kings 19:21**

And he turned back from after him and took the pairs of oxen and sacrificed and boiled them with the gear of the oxen and gave them to the people, and they ate. And he rose and went after Elijah and ministered to him.

### Chapter 20

**1 Kings 20:1**

And one vineyard belonged to Nabouthai the Iezraēlite beside the threshing floor of Achaab king of Samaria.

**1 Kings 20:2**

And Achaab spoke to Nabouthai, saying, Give me your vineyard, and it shall be for me as a garden of vegetables because it is near to my house, and I will give you another vineyard, better than it. But if it pleases before you, I will give you silver, the exchange-price of this vineyard, and it shall be for me as a garden of vegetables.

**1 Kings 20:3**

And Nabouthai said to Achaab, May it not be for me from my God to give the inheritance of my fathers to you.

**1 Kings 20:4**

And Achaab's spirit became troubled, and he lay upon his bed and covered his face and did not eat bread.

**1 Kings 20:5**

And Iezabel his wife came in to him and spoke to him, Why is your spirit troubled and you are not eating bread?

**1 Kings 20:6**

And he said to her, Because I spoke to Nabouthai the Iezraēlite, saying, Give me your vineyard for silver, and if you wish, I will give you another vineyard in place of it, and he said, I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers.

**1 Kings 20:7**

And Iezabel his wife said to him, Do you now act as king over Israel? Rise, eat bread, and become your own man. I will give you the vineyard of Nabouthai the Iezraēlite.

**1 Kings 20:8**

And she wrote a letter in the name of Achaab and sealed it with his seal and sent the letter to the elders and the free men living with Nabouthai.

**1 Kings 20:9**

And it was written in the letters, saying, Proclaim a fast and seat Nabouthai at the head of the people.

**1 Kings 20:10**

And seat two men, sons of lawlessness, opposite him, and let them testify against him, saying, He blessed God and king. And let them bring him out and stone him, and let him die.

**1 Kings 20:11**

And the men of his city, the elders and the free men dwelling in his city, did just as Iezabel sent to them, just as it was written in the letters that she sent to them.

**1 Kings 20:12**

They proclaimed a fast and seated Nabouthai at the head of the people.

**1 Kings 20:13**

And two men, sons of lawlessness, came and sat opposite him and testified against him, saying, You blessed God and king. And they brought him out outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.

**1 Kings 20:14**

And they sent to Iezabel, saying, Nabouthai has been stoned and is dead.

**1 Kings 20:15**

And it came to be when Iezabel heard, she said to Achaab, Rise, inherit the vineyard of Nabouthai the Iezraēlite, who did not give it to you for silver, because Nabouthai is not alive; he is dead.

**1 Kings 20:16**

And it came to be when Achaab heard that Nabouthai the Iezraēlite was dead, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth, and after these things Achaab rose and went down into the vineyard of Nabouthai the Iezraēlite to inherit it.

**1 Kings 20:17**

And the Lord said to Elijah the Thesbite, saying,

**1 Kings 20:18**

Rise and go down to meet Achaab king of Israel, the one in Samaria. Behold, he is in the vineyard of Nabouthai because he has gone down there to inherit it.

**1 Kings 20:19**

And you will speak to him, saying, Thus says the Lord: As you murdered and inherited, because of this thus says the Lord: In every place where the sows and the dogs licked the blood of Nabouthai, there the dogs will lick your blood, and the prostitutes will wash in your blood.

**1 Kings 20:20**

And Achaab said to Elijah, Have you found me, my enemy? And he said, I have found you, because you have vainly sold yourself to do evil before the Lord, provoking him.

**1 Kings 20:21**

Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing evils upon you and will burn after you and destroy from Achaab one pissing against a wall, hemmed in and forsaken in Israel.

**1 Kings 20:22**

And I will make your house like the house of Ieroboam son of Nabat and like the house of Baasa son of Achia, because of the provocations by which you provoked and made Israel sin.

**1 Kings 20:23**

And concerning Iezabel the Lord spoke, saying, Dogs will eat her in the forewall of Iezrael.

**1 Kings 20:24**

The dead one of Achaab in the city, dogs will eat, and the dead one of his in the field, the birds of the sky will eat.

**1 Kings 20:25**

Yet vainly Achaab sold himself to do evil before the Lord, because Iezabel his wife turned him aside.

**1 Kings 20:26**

And he was greatly abominated by going after abominations, according to all that the Amorrite did, whom the Lord destroyed from before the sons of Israel.

**1 Kings 20:27**

And because of the word, as Achaab was pierced to the heart from before the Lord and went weeping, he tore his tunic and girded sackcloth upon his body and fasted and put on sackcloth on the day when he struck Nabouthai the Iezraēlite.

**1 Kings 20:28**

And word of the Lord came by the hand of his servant Elijah concerning Achaab, and the Lord said,

**1 Kings 20:29**

Have you seen how Achaab was pierced to the heart from before me? I will not bring the evil in his days, but in the days of his son I will bring the evil.

### Chapter 21

**1 Kings 21:1**

And son of Ader gathered all his force and went up and besieged Samaria, and thirty-two kings with him and all horse and chariot, and they went up and besieged Samaria and fought against it.

**1 Kings 21:2**

And he sent to Achaab king of Israel into the city.

**1 Kings 21:3**

And he said to him, Thus says son of Ader: Your silver and your gold are mine, and your wives and your children are mine.

**1 Kings 21:4**

And the king of Israel answered and said, According as you spoke, my lord king, I am yours and all that is mine.

**1 Kings 21:5**

And the messengers returned and said, Thus says son of Ader: I sent to you, saying, Your silver and your gold and your wives and your children you will give to me.

**1 Kings 21:6**

For by this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you, and they will search your house and the houses of your servants, and whatever is the desire of their eyes, upon it they will lay their hands and take it.

**1 Kings 21:7**

And the king of Israel called all the elders and said, Know now and see that this one is seeking evil, because he sent to me concerning my wives and my sons and my daughters. My silver and my gold I did not withhold from him.

**1 Kings 21:8**

And the elders and all the people said to him, Do not listen and do not be willing.

**1 Kings 21:9**

And he said to the messengers of son of Ader, Tell your lord, All that you sent to your servant at first I will do, but this thing I cannot do. And the men departed and returned a word to him.

**1 Kings 21:10**

And son of Ader sent back to him, saying, Thus may God do to me and thus add, if the dust of Samaria will be enough for foxes, for all my footmen.

**1 Kings 21:11**

And the king of Israel answered and said, Let it be enough. Let not the bent one boast like the upright one.

**1 Kings 21:12**

And it came to be when he answered him this word, he himself was drinking, and all the kings with him, in tents, and he said to his servants, Build a palisade, and they set a palisade against the city.

**1 Kings 21:13**

And behold, one prophet came near to the king of Israel and said, Thus says the Lord: Have you seen all this great crowd? Behold, I am giving it today into your hands, and you will know that I am the Lord.

**1 Kings 21:14**

And Achaab said, By whom? And he said, Thus says the Lord: By the servant-boys of the rulers of the regions. And Achaab said, Who will join the battle? And he said, You.

**1 Kings 21:15**

And Achaab reviewed the servant-boys of the rulers of the regions, and they were two hundred thirty, and after these he reviewed the people, every son of strength, sixty thousand.

**1 Kings 21:16**

And they went out at midday, and son of Ader was drinking himself drunk in Sokchōth, he and the thirty-two kings, helpers with him.

**1 Kings 21:17**

And the servant-boys of the rulers of the regions went out first, and they sent and reported to the king of Syria, saying, Men have come out from Samaria.

**1 Kings 21:18**

And he said to them, If these come out for peace, seize them alive, and if they come out for war, seize them alive.

**1 Kings 21:19**

And these came out from the city, the servant-boys of the rulers of the regions, and the force behind them.

**1 Kings 21:20**

Each struck the one by him, and each struck again the one by him, and Syria fled, and Israel pursued them, and son of Ader king of Syria escaped on horse with horseman.

**1 Kings 21:21**

And the king of Israel went out and took all the horses and the chariots and struck a great blow in Syria.

**1 Kings 21:22**

And the prophet came near to the king of Israel and said, Be strong, and know and see what you will do, because at the turn of the year son of Ader king of Syria comes up against you.

**1 Kings 21:23**

And the servants of the king of Syria said, The God of Israel is a god of mountains and not a god of valleys, because of this he prevailed over us. But if we fight them on the plain, will we not prevail over them?

**1 Kings 21:24**

And do this thing: remove the kings, each from his place, and put satraps in place of them.

**1 Kings 21:25**

And we will replace for you a force according to the force that fell from you, and horse for horse and chariots for chariots, and we will fight them on the plain and prevail over them. And he listened to their voice and did so.

**1 Kings 21:26**

And it came to be at the turn of the year, son of Ader reviewed Syria and went up to Apheka to war against Israel.

**1 Kings 21:27**

And the sons of Israel were reviewed and came to meet them, and Israel camped opposite them like two flocks of goats, and Syria filled the land.

**1 Kings 21:28**

And the man of God came near and said to the king of Israel, Thus says the Lord: Because Syria said, The Lord God of Israel is a god of mountains and not a god of valleys, I will give all this great force into your hand, and you will know that I am the Lord.

**1 Kings 21:29**

And they encamped opposite these seven days, and it came to be on the seventh day the battle drew near, and Israel struck Syria, one hundred thousand footmen in one day.

**1 Kings 21:30**

And the rest fled to Apheka into the city, and the wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand men of the rest. And son of Ader fled and entered into the bedchamber, into the inner room.

**1 Kings 21:31**

And he said to his servants, I know that the kings of Israel are kings of mercy. Let us put sackcloth on our loins and ropes on our heads and go out to the king of Israel, if perhaps he will keep our lives alive.

**1 Kings 21:32**

And they tied sackcloth on their loins and set ropes on their heads and said to the king of Israel, Your servant son of Ader says, Let my life now live. And he said, If he still lives, he is my brother.

**1 Kings 21:33**

And the men took it as an omen and hurried and caught the word from his mouth and said, Your brother, son of Ader. And he said, Go in and fetch him. And son of Ader came out to him, and they brought him up to him on the chariot.

**1 Kings 21:34**

And he said to him, The cities that my father took from your father I will give back to you, and you will set streets for yourself in Damascus, just as my father set them in Samaria. And I, in covenant, will send you away. And he made a covenant with him and sent him away.

**1 Kings 21:35**

And one man from the sons of the prophets said to his neighbor by the word of the Lord, Strike me now. And the man was not willing to strike him.

**1 Kings 21:36**

And he said to him, Because you did not hear the voice of the Lord, behold, you are running away from me, and a lion will strike you. And he went away from him, and a lion found him and struck him.

**1 Kings 21:37**

And he found another man and said, Strike me now. And the man struck him, striking and shattering him.

**1 Kings 21:38**

And the prophet went and stood for the king of Israel by the road and bound his eyes with a band.

**1 Kings 21:39**

And it came to be as the king passed by, this one cried to the king and said, Your servant went out into the army of battle, and behold, a man brought to me a man and said to me, Guard this man. If by escaping he escapes, your life will be for his life, or you will weigh out a talent of silver.

**1 Kings 21:40**

And it came to be, your servant looked here and there, and he was not there. And the king of Israel said to him, Behold, you have also destroyed the snares set for me.

**1 Kings 21:41**

And he hurried and removed the band from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him, that he was one of the prophets.

**1 Kings 21:42**

And he said to him, Thus says the Lord: Because you brought out from your hand a man appointed to destruction, your life shall be for his life and your people for his people.

**1 Kings 21:43**

And the king of Israel went away confounded and discouraged and came into Samaria.

### Chapter 22

**1 Kings 22:1**

And they sat three years, and there was no war between Syria and Israel.

**1 Kings 22:2**

And it came to be in the third year, Iosaphat king of Iouda went down to the king of Israel.

**1 Kings 22:3**

And the king of Israel said to his servants, Do you know that Remmath Galaad belongs to us, and we are silent to take it from the hand of the king of Syria?

**1 Kings 22:4**

And the king of Israel said to Iosaphat, Will you come up with us to Remmath Galaad for war? And Iosaphat said, As I am, so are you; as my people, so your people; as my horses, so your horses.

**1 Kings 22:5**

And Iosaphat king of Iouda said to the king of Israel, Ask the Lord today.

**1 Kings 22:6**

And the king of Israel gathered all the prophets, about four hundred men, and the king said to them, Shall I go to Remmath Galaad for war, or shall I hold back? And they said, Go up, and in giving, the Lord will give into the hands of the king.

**1 Kings 22:7**

And Iosaphat said to the king of Israel, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord, and shall we ask the Lord through him?

**1 Kings 22:8**

And the king of Israel said to Iosaphat, There is still one man by whom we may ask the Lord, and I hate him because he does not speak good concerning me, only evil: Michaias son of Iemla. And Iosaphat king of Iouda said, Let not the king speak so.

**1 Kings 22:9**

And the king of Israel called one eunuch and said, Quickly, Michaias son of Iemla.

**1 Kings 22:10**

And the king of Israel and Iosaphat king of Iouda were sitting, each upon his throne, armed, in the gates of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.

**1 Kings 22:11**

And Sedekias son of Chanana made iron horns for himself and said, Thus says the Lord: With these you will gore Syria until it is finished.

**1 Kings 22:12**

And all the prophets prophesied thus, saying, Go up to Remmath Galaad and prosper, and the Lord will give into your hands, and the king of Syria.

**1 Kings 22:13**

And the messenger who went to call Michaias spoke to him, saying, Behold now, all the prophets speak with one mouth good things concerning the king. Be now also in your words like the words of one of these and speak good things.

**1 Kings 22:14**

And Michaias said, As the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to me, these things I will speak.

**1 Kings 22:15**

And he came to the king, and the king said to him, Michaias, shall I go up to Remmath Galaad for war, or shall I hold back? And he said, Go up and prosper, and the Lord will give into the hand of the king.

**1 Kings 22:16**

And the king said to him, How many times do I put you under oath, that you speak truth to me in the name of the Lord?

**1 Kings 22:17**

And Michaias said, Not so. I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like a flock that has no shepherd, and the Lord said, There is no lord for these. Let each return to his own house in peace.

**1 Kings 22:18**

And the king of Israel said to Iosaphat king of Iouda, Did I not tell you that this one does not prophesy good things to me, only evils?

**1 Kings 22:19**

And Michaias said, Not so. Hear the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord God of Israel sitting upon his throne, and all the army of heaven stood around him, at his right hand and at his left.

**1 Kings 22:20**

And the Lord said, Who will deceive Achaab king of Israel, and he will go up and fall in Remmath Galaad? And one said this and another said this.

**1 Kings 22:21**

And a spirit went out and stood before the Lord and said, I will deceive him. And the Lord said to him, By what?

**1 Kings 22:22**

And he said, I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, You will deceive and indeed you will prevail. Go out and do so.

**1 Kings 22:23**

And now, behold, the Lord has given a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken evils against you.

**1 Kings 22:24**

And Sedekiou son of Chanana came near and struck Michaias on the jaw and said, What spirit of the Lord was this that spoke in you?

**1 Kings 22:25**

And Michaias said, Behold, you will see on that day when you enter chamber within chamber to hide yourself.

**1 Kings 22:26**

And the king of Israel said, Take Michaias and return him to Emēr the ruler of the city and to Iōas son of the king.

**1 Kings 22:27**

Say to put this one in prison and to feed him bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace.

**1 Kings 22:28**

And Michaias said, If returning you return in peace, the Lord has not spoken in me.

**1 Kings 22:29**

And the king of Israel and Iosaphat king of Iouda went up with him to Remmath Galaad.

**1 Kings 22:30**

And the king of Israel said to Iosaphat king of Iouda, I will disguise myself and enter into the battle, and you put on my clothing. And the king of Israel disguised himself and entered into the battle.

**1 Kings 22:31**

And the king of Syria commanded the rulers of his chariots, thirty-two, saying, Fight neither small nor great, only the king of Israel, utterly alone.

**1 Kings 22:32**

And it came to be when the rulers of the chariots saw Iosaphat king of Iouda, they said, This one appears to be the king of Israel, and they surrounded him to fight, and Iosaphat cried out.

**1 Kings 22:33**

And it came to be when the rulers of the chariots saw that this one was not the king of Israel, they turned away from him.

**1 Kings 22:34**

And one stretched the bow accurately and struck the king of Israel between the lung and between the breastplate, and he said to his charioteer, Turn your hands and bring me out from the battle, because I am wounded.

**1 Kings 22:35**

And the battle turned in that day, and the king was standing on the chariot opposite Syria from morning until evening, and the blood from the wound kept pouring into the bosom of the chariot, and he died at evening, and the blood of the stroke kept going out as far as the bosom of the chariot.

**1 Kings 22:36**

And the herald stood at sunset, saying, Each to his own city and to his own land.

**1 Kings 22:37**

Because the king is dead. And they came to Samaria and buried the king in Samaria.

**1 Kings 22:38**

And they washed the chariot at the spring of Samaria, and the sows and the dogs licked the blood, and the prostitutes bathed in the blood, according to the word of the Lord that he spoke.

**1 Kings 22:39**

And the rest of the matters of Achaab and all that he did and the ivory house that he built and all the cities that he made, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Israel?

**1 Kings 22:40**

And Achaab slept with his fathers, and Ochozias his son reigned in place of him.

**1 Kings 22:41**

And Iosaphat son of Asa reigned over Iouda. In the fourth year of Achaab king of Israel he reigned.

**1 Kings 22:42**

Iosaphat was a son of thirty-five years when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Ierousalem, and his mother's name was Azouba daughter of Selei.

**1 Kings 22:43**

And he walked in every way of Asa his father, and he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the Lord.

**1 Kings 22:44**

Yet he did not remove the high places. The people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.

**1 Kings 22:45**

And Iosaphat made peace with the king of Israel.

**1 Kings 22:46**

And the rest of the matters of Iosaphat and his acts of power, what he did, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Iouda?

**1 Kings 22:51**

And Iosaphat slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David his father, and Iōram his son reigned in place of him.

**1 Kings 22:52**

And Ochozias son of Achaab reigned over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Iosaphat king of Iouda, and he reigned over Israel two years.

**1 Kings 22:53**

And he did evil before the Lord and walked in the way of Achaab his father and in the way of Iezabel his mother and in the sins of the house of Ieroboam son of Nabat, who made Israel sin.

**1 Kings 22:54**

And he served the Baals and bowed down to them and provoked the Lord God of Israel according to all the things that came before him.

## 2 Kings

### Chapter 1

**2 Kings 1:1**

And Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Achaab.

**2 Kings 1:2**

And Ochozias fell through the lattice in his upper room in Samaria and became sick, and he sent messengers and said to them, Come and seek in Baal of flies, god of Akkarōn, whether I will live from this sickness. And they went to inquire through him.

**2 Kings 1:3**

And angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah the Thesbite, saying, Rise, come to meet the messengers of Ochozias king of Samaria, and you will speak to them, Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to seek in Baal of flies, god of Akkarōn?

**2 Kings 1:4**

And not so, because thus says the Lord: The bed on which you went up there, you shall not come down from it, because by death you will die. And Elijah went and spoke to them.

**2 Kings 1:5**

And the messengers returned to him, and he said to them, Why is it that you returned?

**2 Kings 1:6**

And they said to him, A man came up to meet us and said to us, Come, return to the king who sent you, and speak to him, Thus says the Lord: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to seek in Baal of flies, god of Akkarōn? And not so, the bed on which you went up there, you shall not come down from it, because by death you will die.

**2 Kings 1:7**

And he spoke to them, saying, What was the appearance of the man who came up to meet you and spoke to you these words?

**2 Kings 1:8**

And they said to him, A hairy man, with a leather belt girded around his waist. And he said, This is Elijah the Thesbite.

**2 Kings 1:9**

And he sent to him a captain of fifty and his fifty, and he went up and came to him. And behold, Elijah was sitting on the top of the mountain, and the captain of fifty spoke to him and said, Man of God, the king has called you. Come down.

**2 Kings 1:10**

And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, If I am a man of God, fire will come down from heaven and eat you and your fifty. And fire came down from heaven and ate him and his fifty.

**2 Kings 1:11**

And the king added and sent to him another captain of fifty and his fifty, and he went up and the captain of fifty spoke to him and said, Man of God, thus says the king: Quickly, come down.

**2 Kings 1:12**

And Elijah answered and spoke to him and said, If I am a man of God, fire will come down from heaven and eat you and your fifty. And fire came down from heaven and ate him and his fifty.

**2 Kings 1:13**

And the king added yet to send a third captain of fifty and his fifty, and the third captain of fifty came to him and bent upon his knees before Elijah and begged him and spoke to him and said, Man of God, let my life now be precious, and the life of these fifty servants of yours, in your eyes.

**2 Kings 1:14**

Behold, fire came down from heaven and ate the first two captains of fifty and their fifties. And now let the life of your servants be precious in your eyes.

**2 Kings 1:15**

And angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah and said, Go down with him. Do not fear from before them. And Elijah rose and went down with him to the king.

**2 Kings 1:16**

And Elijah spoke to him and said, Thus says the Lord: Why is it that you sent messengers to seek in Baal of flies, god of Akkarōn? And not so, the bed on which you went up there, you shall not come down from it, because by death you will die.

**2 Kings 1:17**

And he died according to the word of the Lord that Elijah spoke.

**2 Kings 1:18**

And the rest of the matters of Ochozias, what he did, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Israel? And Iōram son of Achaab reigned over Israel in Samaria twelve years, in the eighteenth year of Iosaphat king of Iouda. And he did evil before the Lord, yet not like his brothers nor like his mother.
