And he removed the pillars of Baal that his father made and shattered them. Yet in the sins of the house of Ieroboam, who made Israel sin, he clung and did not depart from them. And the anger of the Lord was enraged against the house of Achaab.

### Chapter 2

**2 Kings 2:1**

And it came to be when the Lord was taking Elijah up in a storm as into heaven, Elijah and Elisaie went from Galgala.

**2 Kings 2:2**

And Elijah said to Elisaie, Stay here now, because the Lord has sent me as far as Baithēl. And Elisaie said, As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. And they went to Baithēl.

**2 Kings 2:3**

And the sons of the prophets in Baithēl came to Elisaie and said to him, Do you know that today the Lord is taking your lord away from over your head? And he said, I also know. Be silent.

**2 Kings 2:4**

And Elijah said to Elisaie, Stay here now, because the Lord has sent me to Ierichō. And Elisaie said, As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. And they came to Ierichō.

**2 Kings 2:5**

And the sons of the prophets in Ierichō came near to Elisaie and said to him, Do you know that today the Lord is taking your lord away from over your head? And he said, I too know. Be silent.

**2 Kings 2:6**

And Elijah said to him, Stay here now, because the Lord has sent me as far as the Jordan. And Elisaie said, As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. And both went on.

**2 Kings 2:7**

And fifty men from the sons of the prophets stood opposite at a distance, and both stood by the Jordan.

**2 Kings 2:8**

And Elijah took his sheepskin cloak and rolled it up and struck the water, and the water divided here and there, and both crossed in dry land.

**2 Kings 2:9**

And it came to be when they crossed over, Elijah said to Elisaie, Ask what I should do for you before I am taken up from you. And Elisaie said, Let double things of your spirit now be upon me.

**2 Kings 2:10**

And Elijah said, You made the asking hard. If you see me being taken up from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it shall certainly not happen.

**2 Kings 2:11**

And it came to be as they were going on and talking, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire, and they separated between the two of them, and Elijah was taken up in a storm as into heaven.

**2 Kings 2:12**

And Elisaie was watching and crying out, Father, father, chariot of Israel and its horseman. And he did not see him anymore, and he seized his garments and tore them into two tearings.

**2 Kings 2:13**

And he lifted up Elijah's sheepskin cloak that fell from above upon Elisaie, and Elisaie returned and stood on the lip of the Jordan.

**2 Kings 2:14**

And he took Elijah's sheepskin cloak that fell from above him and struck the water, and it did not divide, and he said, Where is the God of Elijah, indeed? And he struck the waters, and they split here and there, and Elisaie crossed over.

**2 Kings 2:15**

And the sons of the prophets in Ierichō saw him from opposite them and said, The spirit of Elijah has come to rest upon Elisaie. And they came to meet him and bowed to him to the ground.

**2 Kings 2:16**

And they said to him, Behold now, with your servants are fifty men, sons of strength. Let them go now and seek your lord, lest the Spirit of the Lord lifted him and cast him into the Jordan or onto one of the mountains or onto one of the hills. And Elisaie said, You shall not send.

**2 Kings 2:17**

And they pressed him until he was ashamed, and he said, Send them. And they sent fifty men, and they sought three days and did not find him.

**2 Kings 2:18**

And they returned to him, and he was sitting in Ierichō, and Elisaie said, Did I not tell you, Do not go?

**2 Kings 2:19**

And the men of the city said to Elisaie, Behold, the dwelling of the city is good, as my lord sees, but the waters are bad and the land barren.

**2 Kings 2:20**

And Elisaie said, Take for me a new little jar and put salt there. And they brought it to him.

**2 Kings 2:21**

And Elisaie went out to the outflow of the waters and threw salt there and said, Thus says the Lord: I have healed these waters. There shall no longer be from there death and barrenness.

**2 Kings 2:22**

And the waters were healed until this day, according to the word Elisaie spoke.

**2 Kings 2:23**

And he went up from there to Baithēl, and as he was going up on the road, little boys came out from the city and mocked him and said to him, Go up, baldhead, go up.

**2 Kings 2:24**

And he turned after them and saw them and cursed them in the name of the Lord, and behold, two bears came out of the woodland and tore apart forty-two boys from among them.

**2 Kings 2:25**

And he went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

### Chapter 3

**2 Kings 3:1**

And Iōram son of Achaab reigned in Israel in the eighteenth year of Iosaphat king of Iouda, and he reigned twelve years.

**2 Kings 3:2**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, yet not like his father and not like his mother, and he removed the pillars of Baal that his father made.

**2 Kings 3:3**

Yet he clung to the sin of Ieroboam son of Nabat, who made Israel sin. He did not depart from it.

**2 Kings 3:4**

And Mosa king of Moab was a sheep-breeder, and in the revolt he paid back to the king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs and one hundred thousand rams in wool.

**2 Kings 3:5**

And it came to be after Achaab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the kingdom of Israel.

**2 Kings 3:6**

And King Iōram went out on that day from Samaria and reviewed Israel.

**2 Kings 3:7**

And he went and sent to Iosaphat king of Iouda, saying, The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to Moab for war? And he said, I will go up. As I am, so you; as my people, so your people; as my horses, so your horses.

**2 Kings 3:8**

And he said, By what road shall I go up? And he said, By the wilderness road of Edom.

**2 Kings 3:9**

And the king of Israel and the king of Iouda and the king of Edom went, and they went around by a seven-days road, and there was no water for the camp and for the cattle at their feet.

**2 Kings 3:10**

And the king of Israel said, Alas, because the Lord has called these three passing kings to give them into the hand of Moab.

**2 Kings 3:11**

And Iosaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord, and shall we seek the Lord from him? And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, Elisaie son of Saphat is here, who poured water on the hands of Elijah.

**2 Kings 3:12**

And Iosaphat said, Word of the Lord is with him. And the king of Israel and Iosaphat king of Iouda and the king of Edom went down to him.

**2 Kings 3:13**

And Elisaie said to the king of Israel, What is to me and to you? Go to the prophets of your father. And the king of Israel said to him, No, because the Lord has called these three kings to hand them over into the hands of Moab.

**2 Kings 3:14**

And Elisaie said, As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand, unless I regarded the face of Iosaphat king of Iouda, I would not look toward you or see you.

**2 Kings 3:15**

And now bring me a musician. And it came to be, as the musician played, the hand of the Lord came upon him.

**2 Kings 3:16**

And he said, Thus says the Lord: Make this wadi pits, pits.

**2 Kings 3:17**

For thus says the Lord: You will not see wind and you will not see rain, and this wadi will be filled with water, and you will drink, you and your possessions and your cattle.

**2 Kings 3:18**

And this is light in the eyes of the Lord, and I will hand Moab over into your hand.

**2 Kings 3:19**

And you will strike every fortified city, and you will bring down every good tree, and you will stop up all springs of water, and every good tract you will spoil with stones.

**2 Kings 3:20**

And it came to be in the morning, as the sacrifice was going up, behold, waters were coming by the road of Edom, and the land was filled with water.

**2 Kings 3:21**

And all Moab heard that the kings had gone up to fight them, and they cried out from everyone girding on a belt and upward, and they stood at the border.

**2 Kings 3:22**

And they rose early in the morning, and the sun rose upon the waters, and Moab saw opposite them the waters red like blood.

**2 Kings 3:23**

And they said, This is blood of the sword. The kings fought and struck each man his neighbor. And now, Moab, to the spoils!

**2 Kings 3:24**

And they entered into the camp of Israel, and Israel rose and struck Moab, and they fled from before them, and they entered, going in and striking Moab.

**2 Kings 3:25**

And they tore down the cities, and on every good tract each man threw his stone and filled it, and they stopped up every spring of water and brought down every good tree until they left only the wall-stones of Kir-hareseth torn down. And the slingers encircled it and struck it.

**2 Kings 3:26**

And the king of Moab saw that the battle had grown too strong against him, and he took with himself seven hundred men drawing sword to break through to the king of Edom, and they were not able.

**2 Kings 3:27**

And he took his firstborn son, who would reign in place of him, and offered him as a whole burnt offering upon the wall, and great regret came upon Israel, and they withdrew from him and returned to the land.

### Chapter 4

**2 Kings 4:1**

And one woman from the sons of the prophets cried to Elisaie, saying, Your servant, my husband, has died, and you knew that your servant was fearing the Lord, and the creditor has come to take my two sons for himself as slaves.

**2 Kings 4:2**

And Elisaie said, What shall I do for you? Tell me what there is for you in the house. And she said, There is nothing for your servant in the house except oil for anointing.

**2 Kings 4:3**

And he said to her, Go, ask for yourself vessels from outside, from all your neighbors, empty vessels. Do not make them few.

**2 Kings 4:4**

And you will go in and shut the door on yourself and on your sons, and you will pour into these vessels, and the filled one you will lift away.

**2 Kings 4:5**

And she went from him and did so, and she shut the door on herself and on her sons. They kept bringing the vessels near to her, and she kept pouring.

**2 Kings 4:6**

Until the vessels were filled, and she said to her sons, Bring another vessel near to me. And they said to her, There is no more vessel. And the oil stood still.

**2 Kings 4:7**

And she came and reported to the man of God, and Elisaie said, Go and sell the oil and pay your interest, and you and your sons will live on the remaining oil.

**2 Kings 4:8**

And it came to be one day Elisaie passed through to Sōman, and there was a great woman there, and she constrained him to eat bread. And it came to be, as often as he went in, he turned aside there to eat.

**2 Kings 4:9**

And the woman said to her husband, Behold now, I know that this one who continually passes over us is a holy man of God.

**2 Kings 4:10**

Let us make for him a little upper-room place, and let us put there for him a bed and a table and a chair and a lampstand, and it shall be, when he comes in to us, he will turn in there.

**2 Kings 4:11**

And it came to be one day, he went in there and turned in to the upper room and slept there.

**2 Kings 4:12**

And he said to Giezi his servant-boy, Call this Sōmanite for me. And he called her, and she stood before him.

**2 Kings 4:13**

And he said to him, Say now to her, Behold, you have stirred up for us all this concern. What needs to be done for you? Is there a word for you to the king or to the commander of the force? And she said, I dwell in the midst of my people.

**2 Kings 4:14**

And he said, What needs to be done for her? And Giezi his servant-boy said, Truly she has no son, and her husband is old.

**2 Kings 4:15**

And he called her, and she stood by the door.

**2 Kings 4:16**

And Elisaie said to her, At this time, as the living season returns, you will be embracing a son. And she said, No, my lord, do not lie to your servant.

**2 Kings 4:17**

And the woman conceived and bore a son at this time, as the living season returned, just as Elisaie spoke to her.

**2 Kings 4:18**

And the boy grew strong, and it came to be when the boy went out to his father, to the reapers.

**2 Kings 4:19**

And he said to his father, My head, my head. And he said to the servant-boy, Carry him to his mother.

**2 Kings 4:20**

And he carried him to his mother, and he lay on her knees until midday and died.

**2 Kings 4:21**

And she brought him up and laid him on the bed of the man of God and shut the door upon him and went out.

**2 Kings 4:22**

And she called her husband and said, Send me now one of the servant-boys and one of the donkeys, and I will run as far as the man of God and return.

**2 Kings 4:23**

And he said, Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath. And she said, Peace.

**2 Kings 4:24**

And she saddled the donkey and said to her servant-boy, Lead on. Do not slow my riding unless I tell you.

**2 Kings 4:25**

So she went and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. And it came to be when Elisaie saw her coming, he said to Giezi his servant-boy, Behold now, that Sōmanite.

**2 Kings 4:26**

Now run to meet her and say, Is there peace for you? Is there peace for your husband? Is there peace for the boy? And she said, Peace.

**2 Kings 4:27**

And she came to Elisaie at the mountain and seized his feet, and Giezi came near to push her away, and Elisaie said, Leave her, because her soul is bitter within her, and the Lord hid it from me and did not tell me.

**2 Kings 4:28**

And she said, Did I ask for a son from my lord? Did I not say, Do not mislead me?

**2 Kings 4:29**

And Elisaie said to Giezi, Gird your waist and take my staff in your hand and go, because if you meet a man you shall not bless him, and if a man blesses you, you shall not answer him, and you shall put my staff on the face of the boy.

**2 Kings 4:30**

And the mother of the boy said, As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. And Elisaie rose and went after her.

**2 Kings 4:31**

And Giezi passed before her and placed the staff on the face of the boy, but there was no voice and there was no hearing, and he returned to meet him and reported to him, saying, The boy did not wake up.

**2 Kings 4:32**

And Elisaie entered into the house, and behold, the boy was dead, laid on his bed.

**2 Kings 4:33**

And Elisaie went into the house and shut the door upon the two of them and prayed to the Lord.

**2 Kings 4:34**

And he went up and lay upon the boy and put his mouth on his mouth and his eyes on his eyes and his hands on his hands and bent himself over him, and the flesh of the boy grew warm.

**2 Kings 4:35**

And he turned and walked in the house here and there and went up and bent himself over the boy until seven times, and the boy opened his eyes.

**2 Kings 4:36**

And Elisaie cried out to Giezi and said, Call this Sōmanite. And he called her, and she came in to him, and Elisaie said, Take your son.

**2 Kings 4:37**

And the woman came in and fell at his feet and bowed to the ground, and she took her son and went out.

**2 Kings 4:38**

And Elisaie returned to Galgala, and famine was in the land, and the sons of the prophets sat before him, and Elisaie said to his servant-boy, Set on the great pot and boil stew for the sons of the prophets.

**2 Kings 4:39**

And one went out into the field to gather herbs and found a vine in the field and gathered from it wild gourds, his garment full, and put them into the pot of stew, because they did not know them.

**2 Kings 4:40**

And they poured it out for the men to eat, and it came to be while they were eating from the stew, behold, they cried out and said, Death in the pot, man of God, and they were not able to eat.

**2 Kings 4:41**

And he said, Take flour and throw it into the pot. And Elisaie said to Giezi the servant-boy, Pour out to the people and let them eat. And there was no longer any evil thing in the pot.

**2 Kings 4:42**

And a man came from Baithsarisa and brought to the man of God firstfruits, twenty barley loaves and fresh ears in a sack, and he said, Give to the people and let them eat.

**2 Kings 4:43**

And his attendant said, What shall I give this before one hundred men? And he said, Give to the people and let them eat, because thus says the Lord: They will eat and leave some.

**2 Kings 4:44**

And they ate and left some, according to the word of the Lord.

### Chapter 5

**2 Kings 5:1**

And Naiman, commander of the force of Syria, was a great man before his lord and honored in face, because through him the Lord gave salvation to Syria; and the man was mighty in strength, afflicted with skin-disease.

**2 Kings 5:2**

And Syria had gone out in raiding bands and taken captive from the land of Israel a small young girl, and she was before the wife of Naiman.

**2 Kings 5:3**

And she said to her mistress, If only my lord were before the prophet of God in Samaria. Then he would remove him from his skin-disease.

**2 Kings 5:4**

And he went in and reported to his lord, saying, Thus and thus spoke the young girl from the land of Israel.

**2 Kings 5:5**

And the king of Syria said to Naiman, Come, go in, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel. And he went and took in his hand ten talents of silver and six thousand pieces of gold and ten changes of garments.

**2 Kings 5:6**

And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, And now, when this letter comes to you, behold, I have sent to you Naiman my servant, and you shall remove him from his skin-disease.

**2 Kings 5:7**

And it came to be, when the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his garments and said, Am I God, to kill and make alive, that this man sends to me to remove a man from his skin-disease? Only recognize now and see that he is seeking a pretext against me.

**2 Kings 5:8**

And it came to be, when Elisaie heard that the king of Israel tore his garments, he sent to the king of Israel, saying, Why have you torn your garments? Let Naiman now come to me, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel.

**2 Kings 5:9**

And Naiman came with horse and chariot and stood at the door of the house of Elisaie.

**2 Kings 5:10**

And Elisaie sent a messenger to him, saying, Go, wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will return to you, and you will be cleansed.

**2 Kings 5:11**

And Naiman grew angry and went away and said, Behold, I said to myself that he would surely come out to me and stand and call on the name of his God and put his hand on the place and remove the skin-diseased part.

**2 Kings 5:12**

Are not Abana and Pharphar, rivers of Damascus, better than the Jordan and all the waters of Israel? If I go and wash in them, will I not be cleansed? And he turned aside and went away in anger.

**2 Kings 5:13**

And his servants came near and spoke to him, saying, Father, if the prophet had spoken a great word to you, would you not do it? How much more when he said to you, Wash and be cleansed.

**2 Kings 5:14**

And Naiman went down and immersed himself in the Jordan seven times according to the word of Elisaie, and his flesh returned like the flesh of a small boy, and he was cleansed.

**2 Kings 5:15**

And he returned to Elisaie, he and all his camp, and came and stood and said, Behold now, I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. And now take a blessing from your servant.

**2 Kings 5:16**

And Elisaie said, As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will not take it. And he pressed him to take it, but he refused.

**2 Kings 5:17**

And Naiman said, If not, then let there be given to your servant a load of red earth, as much as a pair of mules can carry, for your servant will no longer make whole-burnt-offering or sacrifice to other gods, but only to the Lord.

**2 Kings 5:18**

In this matter may the Lord be merciful to your servant: when my lord enters the house of Remman to bow there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow in the house of Remman, when I bow in the house of Remman, may the Lord be merciful to your servant in this matter.

**2 Kings 5:19**

And Elisaie said to Naiman, Go in peace. And he went away from him a short stretch of land.

**2 Kings 5:20**

And Giezi, the servant-boy of Elisaie, said, Behold, my lord spared this Naiman the Syrian by not taking from his hand what he brought. As the Lord lives, unless I run after him and take something from him.

**2 Kings 5:21**

And Giezi pursued after Naiman, and Naiman saw him running after him and turned back from the chariot to meet him.

**2 Kings 5:22**

And he said, Peace. My lord has sent me, saying, Behold, now two servant-boys have come to me from the hill-country of Ephraim, from the sons of the prophets. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of garments.

**2 Kings 5:23**

And Naiman said, Take two talents of silver. And he bound them in two bags, with two changes of garments, and gave them to two of his servant-boys, and they carried them before him.

**2 Kings 5:24**

And they came to the hidden place, and he took them from their hands and stored them in the house and sent the men away.

**2 Kings 5:25**

And he himself went in and stood by his lord. And Elisaie said to him, Where have you come from, Giezi? And Giezi said, Your servant did not go here or there.

**2 Kings 5:26**

And Elisaie said to him, Did not my heart go with you when the man turned back from his chariot to meet you? Is now the time to take silver and to take garments and olive-groves and vineyards and sheep and cattle and male servants and female servants?

**2 Kings 5:27**

And the skin-disease of Naiman will cling to you and to your seed forever. And he went out from before him afflicted with skin-disease like snow.

### Chapter 6

**2 Kings 6:1**

And the sons of the prophets said to Elisaie, Behold now, the place where we dwell before you is too narrow for us.

**2 Kings 6:2**

Let us go now as far as the Jordan, and let each man take from there one beam, and let us make for ourselves there a place to dwell there. And he said, Go.

**2 Kings 6:3**

And one said, Please come with your servants. And he said, I will go.

**2 Kings 6:4**

And he went with them. And they came to the Jordan and were cutting the wood.

**2 Kings 6:5**

And behold, one was felling the beam, and the iron fell into the water, and he cried out, Alas, master, and it was borrowed.

**2 Kings 6:6**

And the man of God said, Where did it fall? And he showed him the place, and he cut off a stick and threw it there, and the iron floated.

**2 Kings 6:7**

And he said, Lift it up for yourself. And he stretched out his hand and took it.

**2 Kings 6:8**

And the king of Syria was warring against Israel and consulted with his servants, saying, At such and such a place I will encamp.

**2 Kings 6:9**

And Elisaie sent to the king of Israel, saying, Beware of passing by this place, because Syria is hidden there.

**2 Kings 6:10**

And the king of Israel sent to the place of which Elisaie spoke to him and was on guard there, not once nor twice.

**2 Kings 6:11**

And the soul of the king of Syria was thrown into confusion over this matter, and he called his servants and said to them, Will you not tell me who is betraying me to the king of Israel?

**2 Kings 6:12**

And one of his servants said, No, my lord king. Rather Elisaie the prophet in Israel tells the king of Israel all the words that you speak in the chamber of your bed.

**2 Kings 6:13**

And he said, Come, see where this man is, and I will send and take him. And they reported to him, saying, Behold, he is in Dothaim.

**2 Kings 6:14**

And he sent there horse and chariot and a heavy force, and they came by night and surrounded the city.

**2 Kings 6:15**

And the servant of Elisaie rose early and went out, and behold, a force was surrounding the city, with horse and chariot. And the servant-boy said to him, Alas, master, what shall we do?

**2 Kings 6:16**

And Elisaie said, Do not fear, because those with us are more than those with them.

**2 Kings 6:17**

And Elisaie prayed and said, Lord, open the eyes of the servant-boy and let him see. And the Lord opened his eyes, and he saw, and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisaie.

**2 Kings 6:18**

And they came down toward him, and Elisaie prayed to the Lord and said, Strike this nation with blindness now. And he struck them with blindness according to the word of Elisaie.

**2 Kings 6:19**

And Elisaie said to them, This is not the city, and this is not the way. Come after me, and I will lead you to the man whom you seek. And he led them into Samaria.

**2 Kings 6:20**

And it came to be, when they entered Samaria, Elisaie said, Lord, open now their eyes and let them see. And the Lord opened their eyes and they saw, and behold, they were in the midst of Samaria.

**2 Kings 6:21**

And the king of Israel said, when he saw them, Shall I strike them down, father? Shall I strike them down?

**2 Kings 6:22**

And he said, You shall not strike them down. Would you strike down those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow? Set bread and water before them, and let them eat and drink and go to their lord.

**2 Kings 6:23**

And he set before them a great feast, and they ate and drank, and he sent them away, and they went to their lord. And raiding bands of Syria did not continue to come into the land of Israel.

**2 Kings 6:24**

And it came to be after this that Ben-hadad king of Syria gathered all his camp and went up and besieged Samaria.

**2 Kings 6:25**

And there was a great famine in Samaria, and behold, they besieged it until a donkey's head was fifty shekels of silver and a quarter of a kab of dove's dung was five shekels of silver.

**2 Kings 6:26**

And the king of Israel was passing over the wall, and a woman cried to him, saying, Save, my lord king.

**2 Kings 6:27**

And he said to her, If the Lord does not save you, from where shall I save you? From the threshing floor or from the winepress?

**2 Kings 6:28**

And the king said to her, What troubles you? And the woman said, This woman said to me, Give your son, and let us eat him today, and my son we will eat tomorrow.

**2 Kings 6:29**

And we boiled my son and ate him, and I said to her on the second day, Give your son and let us eat him, and she hid her son.

**2 Kings 6:30**

And it came to be, when the king heard the words of the woman, he tore his garments. And he was passing over the wall, and the people saw the sackcloth on his flesh within.

**2 Kings 6:31**

And he said, Thus may God do to me and thus may he add, if the head of Elisaie son of Shaphat remains on him today.

**2 Kings 6:32**

And Elisaie was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him, and the king sent a man from before him. Before the messenger came to him, Elisaie said to the elders, Do you see that this son of a murderer has sent to take away my head? See, when the messenger comes, shut the door and press him at the door. Is not the sound of the feet of his lord behind him?

**2 Kings 6:33**

While he was still speaking with them, behold, the messenger came down to him and said, Behold, this evil is from the Lord. Why should I wait for the Lord any longer?

### Chapter 7

**2 Kings 7:1**

And Elisaie said, Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord: At this time tomorrow a measure of fine flour will be a shekel, and two measures of barley a shekel, at the gates of Samaria.

**2 Kings 7:2**

And the officer on whose hand the king leaned answered Elisaie and said, Behold, if the Lord makes floodgates in heaven, can this thing be? And Elisaie said, Behold, you will see with your eyes, but from there you will not eat.

**2 Kings 7:3**

And four men afflicted with skin-disease were beside the gate of the city. And one man said to his neighbor, Why do we sit here until we die?

**2 Kings 7:4**

If we say, Let us enter the city, the famine is in the city, and we will die there. And if we sit here, we will die. And now come, let us fall into the camp of Syria. If they keep us alive, we will live; and if they put us to death, we will die.

**2 Kings 7:5**

And they rose in the dark to enter the camp of Syria and came to the edge of the camp of Syria, and behold, no man was there.

**2 Kings 7:6**

For the Lord had made the camp of Syria hear a sound of chariot and a sound of horse and a sound of great force, and one man said to his brother, Behold now, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us.

**2 Kings 7:7**

And they rose and fled in the dark and abandoned their tents and their horses and their donkeys, the camp just as it was, and fled for their own life.

**2 Kings 7:8**

And these men afflicted with skin-disease came to the edge of the camp and entered one tent and ate and drank and took from there silver and gold and clothing and went and hid them. And they returned and entered another tent and took from there and went and hid them.

**2 Kings 7:9**

And one man said to his neighbor, We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until the morning light, lawlessness will find us. And now come, let us go in and report to the house of the king.

**2 Kings 7:10**

And they went in and cried out to the gate of the city and reported to them, saying, We entered the camp of Syria, and behold, no man was there and no human voice, only horses tied and donkeys and the tents just as they were.

**2 Kings 7:11**

And the gatekeepers cried out and reported it inside the house of the king.

**2 Kings 7:12**

And the king rose by night and said to his servants, Let me now tell you what Syria has done to us. They know that we are hungry, and they went out from the camp and hid themselves in the field, saying, When they come out from the city, we will seize them alive and enter the city.

**2 Kings 7:13**

And one of his servants answered and said, Let them take now five of the horses left, which were left here. Behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel that has come to an end. Let us send and see.

**2 Kings 7:14**

And they took two mounted horsemen, and the king of Israel sent them after the king of Syria, saying, Go and see.

**2 Kings 7:15**

And they went after them as far as the Jordan, and behold, all the road was full of garments and vessels which Syria threw away in their panic. And the messengers returned and reported to the king.

**2 Kings 7:16**

And the people went out and plundered the camp of Syria. And a measure of fine flour became a shekel, and two measures of barley a shekel, according to the word of the Lord.

**2 Kings 7:17**

And the king had appointed the officer on whose hand he leaned over the gate, and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died, just as the man of God spoke when the king came down to him.

**2 Kings 7:18**

And it came to be just as Elisaie had spoken to the king, saying, Two measures of barley a shekel and a measure of fine flour a shekel will be at this time tomorrow in the gate of Samaria.

**2 Kings 7:19**

And the officer answered Elisaie and said, Behold, if the Lord makes floodgates in heaven, can this thing be? And Elisaie said, Behold, you will see with your eyes, but from there you will not eat.

**2 Kings 7:20**

And so it happened to him, and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

### Chapter 8

**2 Kings 8:1**

And Elisaie spoke to the woman whose son he restored to life, saying, Rise and go, you and your house, and sojourn where you may sojourn, because the Lord has called for famine upon the land, and it has come upon the land seven years.

**2 Kings 8:2**

And the woman rose and did according to the word of Elisaie, and she and her house went and sojourned in the land of the Philistines seven years.

**2 Kings 8:3**

And it came to be at the end of seven years that the woman returned from the land of the Philistines to the city, and she came to cry to the king concerning her house and concerning her fields.

**2 Kings 8:4**

And the king was speaking to Giezi the servant-boy of Elisaie, the man of God, saying, Tell me now all the great things Elisaie did.

**2 Kings 8:5**

And it came to be, while he was recounting to the king how Elisaie restored a dead son to life, behold, the woman whose son Elisaie restored to life cried to the king concerning her house and her fields. And Giezi said, My lord king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisaie restored to life.

**2 Kings 8:6**

And the king asked the woman, and she recounted it to him. And the king gave her one eunuch, saying, Restore all that was hers and all the produce of her field from the day she left the land until now.

**2 Kings 8:7**

And Elisaie came to Damascus, and Ben-hadad king of Syria was sick. And they reported to him, saying, The man of God has come here.

**2 Kings 8:8**

And the king said to Hazael, Take in your hand a gift, and go to meet the man of God, and inquire of the Lord through him, saying, Shall I live from this sickness of mine?

**2 Kings 8:9**

And Hazael went to meet him and took in his hand a gift, even every good thing of Damascus, a load of forty camels, and came and stood before him and said to Elisaie, Your son Ben-hadad king of Syria has sent me to you, saying, Shall I live from this sickness?

**2 Kings 8:10**

And Elisaie said, Go, say to him, You will surely live, yet the Lord has shown me that he will surely die.

**2 Kings 8:11**

And he fixed his face and held it until shame, and the man of God wept.

**2 Kings 8:12**

And Hazael said, Why does my lord weep? And he said, Because I know what evils you will do to the sons of Israel. You will send their strongholds into fire, and their chosen men you will kill with the sword, and their infants you will dash, and their pregnant women you will rip open.

**2 Kings 8:13**

And Hazael said, What is your servant, this dead dog, that he should do this great thing? And Elisaie said, The Lord has shown me you as king over Syria.

**2 Kings 8:14**

And he went from Elisaie and entered to his lord, and he said to him, What did Elisaie say to you? And he said, He said to me, You will surely live.

**2 Kings 8:15**

And it came to be on the next day that he took a coverlet and dipped it in water and spread it over his face, and he died. And Hazael reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 8:16**

In the fifth year of Joram son of Achaab, king of Israel, Jehoram son of Josaphat became king, king of Judah.

**2 Kings 8:17**

He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 8:18**

And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Achaab had done, because the daughter of Achaab was his wife, and he did evil before the Lord.

**2 Kings 8:19**

Yet the Lord did not wish to destroy Judah because of Dauid his servant, as he said to give him a lamp and to his sons all the days.

**2 Kings 8:20**

In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah and made a king reign over themselves.

**2 Kings 8:21**

And Joram went over to Sior, and all the chariots with him. And it came to be, when he rose by night, he struck Edom that had encircled him and the commanders of the chariots, and the people fled to their tents.

**2 Kings 8:22**

And Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah until this day. Then Lobena rebelled at that time.

**2 Kings 8:23**

And the rest of the words of Joram and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 8:24**

And Joram slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of Dauid his father, and Ochozias his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 8:25**

In the twelfth year of Joram son of Achaab king of Israel, Ochozias son of Joram became king.

**2 Kings 8:26**

Ochozias was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Gotholia, daughter of Ambrie king of Israel.

**2 Kings 8:27**

And he walked in the way of the house of Achaab and did evil before the Lord, like the house of Achaab.

**2 Kings 8:28**

And he went with Joram son of Achaab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Remmoth Galaad, and the Syrians struck Joram.

**2 Kings 8:29**

And king Joram returned to be healed in Jezrael from the wounds which they struck him at Remmoth when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. And Ochozias son of Joram went down to see Joram son of Achaab in Jezrael, because he was ill.

### Chapter 9

**2 Kings 9:1**

And Elisaie the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, Gird your loins and take this flask of oil in your hand and go to Remmoth Galaad.

**2 Kings 9:2**

And you will enter there and see there Iou son of Iosaphat son of Namessi, and you will go in and raise him up from the midst of his brothers and bring him into an inner room within a room.

**2 Kings 9:3**

Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head and say, Thus says the Lord, I have anointed you as king over Israel. And you will open the door and flee and not stay.

**2 Kings 9:4**

And the servant-boy, the prophet, went to Remmoth Galaad.

**2 Kings 9:5**

And he entered, and behold, the commanders of the force were sitting, and he said, I have a word for you, commander. And Iou said, For which one among all of us? And he said, For you, commander.

**2 Kings 9:6**

And he rose and entered the house, and he poured the oil on his head and said to him, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, I have anointed you as king over the people of the Lord, over Israel.

**2 Kings 9:7**

And you shall destroy the house of Achaab your lord, and I will avenge the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the Lord from the hand of Jezabel.

**2 Kings 9:8**

And I will cut off from the house of Achaab everyone who urinates against a wall, and one held fast and left behind in Israel.

**2 Kings 9:9**

And I will make the house of Achaab like the house of Ieroboam son of Nabat and like the house of Baasa son of Achia.

**2 Kings 9:10**

And the dogs shall eat Jezabel in the portion of Jezrael, and there is none who buries. And he opened the door and fled.

**2 Kings 9:11**

And Iou went out to the servants of his lord, and they said to him, Is all well? Why did this madman come to you? And he said to them, You know the man and his rambling.

**2 Kings 9:12**

And they said, It is false. Tell us now. And he said to them, Thus and thus he spoke to me, saying, Thus says the Lord, I have anointed you as king over Israel.

**2 Kings 9:13**

And hearing, they hurried, and each took his garment and put it under him on the bare steps, and they blew on a horn and said, Iou reigns.

**2 Kings 9:14**

And Iou son of Iosaphat son of Namessi conspired against Ioram. And Ioram himself had been guarding Remmoth Galaad, he and all Israel, because of Hazael king of Syria.

**2 Kings 9:15**

And Ioram the king returned to be healed in Jezrael from the wounds with which the Syrians struck him when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. And Iou said, If your soul is with me, let none escape from the city to go and report in Jezrael.

**2 Kings 9:16**

And Iou mounted and went to Jezrael, because Ioram was being healed there, and Ochozias king of Judah had gone down to see Ioram.

**2 Kings 9:17**

And the watchman stood on the tower in Jezrael and saw the dust of Iou as he came and said, I see dust. And Ioram said, Take a rider and send him before them, and let him say, Is it peace?

**2 Kings 9:18**

And a horseman went to meet them and said, Thus says the king, Is it peace? And Iou said, What is peace to you? Turn behind me. And the watchman reported, saying, The messenger came to them and did not return.

**2 Kings 9:19**

And he sent a second horseman, and he came to him and said, Thus says the king, Is it peace? And Iou said, What is peace to you? Turn behind me.

**2 Kings 9:20**

And the watchman reported, saying, He came to them and did not return, and the driving is like the driving of Iou son of Namessi, because he drives furiously.

**2 Kings 9:21**

And Ioram said, Harness. And they harnessed his chariot, and Ioram king of Israel and Ochozias king of Judah went out, each in his chariot, to meet Iou, and they found him in the portion of Nabouthai the Jezraelite.

**2 Kings 9:22**

And it came to be, when Ioram saw Iou, he said, Is it peace, Iou? And Iou said, What peace, while the whoredoms of Jezabel your mother and her many sorceries remain?

**2 Kings 9:23**

And Ioram turned his hands to flee and said to Ochozias, Treachery, Ochozias!

**2 Kings 9:24**

And Iou filled his hand with the bow and struck Ioram between his arms, and the arrow went out through his heart, and he bent upon his knees.

**2 Kings 9:25**

And Iou said to Badekar his officer, Lift him and throw him into the portion of the field of Nabouthai the Jezraelite, because I remember, I and you riding on pairs behind Achaab his father, and the Lord took up this burden against him, saying,

**2 Kings 9:26**

Surely the blood of Nabouthai and the blood of his sons I saw yesterday, says the Lord, and I will repay him in this portion, says the Lord. And now lift him and throw him into the portion according to the word of the Lord.

**2 Kings 9:27**

And Ochozias king of Judah saw and fled by way of Baithaggan, and Iou pursued after him and said, Strike him too. And they struck him in the chariot at the ascent of Gai, which is Ieblaam, and he fled to Mageddo and died there.

**2 Kings 9:28**

And his servants set him on the chariot and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb in the city of Dauid.

**2 Kings 10:1**

### Chapter 11

**2 Kings 11:1**

**2 Kings 11:7**

**2 Kings 15:26**

And the rest of the words of Phakeias and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel.

**2 Kings 15:27**

**2 Kings 15:28**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord. He did not depart from all the sins of Ieroboam son of Nabat, who made Israel sin.

**2 Kings 15:29**

In the days of Phakee king of Israel, Thaglathphellasar king of the Assyrians came and took Aiin and Abelbaithmaacha and Ianōch and Kenez and Asōr and Galaad and Galilaia, all the land of Nephthali, and deported them to the Assyrians.

**2 Kings 15:30**

And Ōsēe son of Ela made a conspiracy against Phakee son of Romeliou and struck him and killed him and reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Iōatham son of Azarias.

**2 Kings 15:31**

And the rest of the words of Phakee and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel.

**2 Kings 15:32**

In the second year of Phakee son of Romeliou king of Israel, Iōatham son of Azarias king of Judah reigned.

**2 Kings 15:33**

He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Ierousa daughter of Sadōk.

**2 Kings 15:34**

**2 Kings 15:35**

**2 Kings 15:36**

And the rest of the words of Iōatham and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 15:37**

In those days the Lord began to send into Judah Raassōn king of Syria and Phakee son of Romeliou.

**2 Kings 15:38**

And Iōatham slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of Dauid his father, and Achaz his son reigned in his place.

### Chapter 16

**2 Kings 16:1**

In the seventeenth year of Phakee son of Romeliou, Achaz son of Iōatham king of Judah reigned.

**2 Kings 16:2**

Achaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem, and he did not do what was right in the eyes of the Lord his God faithfully, as Dauid his father.

**2 Kings 16:3**

And he walked in the way of Ieroboam son of Nabat king of Israel, and even his son he caused to pass through fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord drove out from before the sons of Israel.

**2 Kings 16:4**

And he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places and on the hills and under every leafy tree.

**2 Kings 16:5**

**2 Kings 16:6**

**2 Kings 16:7**

And Achaz sent messengers to Thaglathphellasar king of the Assyrians, saying, I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Syria and from the hand of the king of Israel, those rising against me.

**2 Kings 16:8**

And Achaz took the silver and the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of the king's house and sent gifts to the king.

**2 Kings 16:9**

**2 Kings 16:11**

And Ourias the priest built the altar according to all that king Achaz sent from Damascus.

**2 Kings 16:12**

And the king saw the altar and went up upon it.

**2 Kings 16:13**

And he burned his whole-burnt-offering and his sacrifice and his drink-offering and poured out the blood of his peace-offerings upon the altar.

**2 Kings 16:14**

**2 Kings 16:15**

**2 Kings 16:16**

And Ourias the priest did according to all that king Achaz commanded him.

**2 Kings 16:18**

**2 Kings 16:19**

### Chapter 17

**2 Kings 17:1**

In the twelfth year of Achaz king of Judah, Ōsēe son of Ela reigned in Samaria over Israel nine years.

**2 Kings 17:2**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, yet not like the kings of Israel who were before him.

**2 Kings 17:3**

**2 Kings 17:4**

**2 Kings 17:5**

And the king of the Assyrians came up in all the land and came up to Samaria and besieged it three years.

**2 Kings 17:6**

**2 Kings 17:7**

And it came to be because the sons of Israel sinned against the Lord their God who brought them up from the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.

**2 Kings 17:8**

And they walked in the statutes of the nations whom the Lord drove out from before the sons of Israel, and in those of the kings of Israel, as many as they made.

**2 Kings 17:9**

And the sons of Israel secretly did matters not so against the Lord their God, and they built for themselves high places in all their cities, from tower of watchmen to fortified city.

**2 Kings 17:10**

And they set up for themselves pillars and groves on every high hill and under every leafy tree.

**2 Kings 17:11**

And there they burned incense on all the high places, as the nations whom the Lord deported from before them, and they made companions and engraved things to provoke the Lord.

**2 Kings 17:12**

And they served idols, of which the Lord said to them, You shall not do this thing to the Lord.

**2 Kings 17:13**

And the Lord testified in Israel and in Judah by the hand of all his prophets, every seer, saying, Turn from your evil ways and keep my commandments and my ordinances and all the law.

**2 Kings 17:14**

And they did not listen and hardened their neck beyond the neck of their fathers.

**2 Kings 17:15**

And his testimonies, which he testified to them, they did not keep, and they went after vanities and became vain, and after the nations around them, concerning whom he commanded them not to do according to these.

**2 Kings 17:16**

They abandoned the commandments of the Lord their God and made for themselves cast images, two calves, and made groves and bowed down to all the force of heaven and served Baal.

**2 Kings 17:17**

And they made their sons and their daughters pass through fire and practiced divinations and omens and sold themselves to do evil in the eyes of the Lord, to provoke him.

**2 Kings 17:18**

And the Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them from before his face, and none was left except the tribe of Judah alone.

**2 Kings 17:19**

Yet Judah also did not keep the commandments of the Lord their God, and they walked in the statutes of Israel which they made.

**2 Kings 17:20**

And the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel and shook them and gave them into the hand of those plundering them until he cast them from before his face.

**2 Kings 17:21**

**2 Kings 17:22**

And the sons of Israel walked in every sin of Ieroboam which he did. They did not depart from it,

**2 Kings 17:23**

**2 Kings 17:24**

And the king of the Assyrians brought from Babylon and from Choutha and from Aia and from Aimath and Seppharouain and settled them in the cities of Samaria instead of the sons of Israel. And they inherited Samaria and dwelt in its cities.

**2 Kings 17:25**

And it came to be at the beginning of their dwelling there, they did not fear the Lord, and the Lord sent lions among them, and they were killing among them.

**2 Kings 17:26**

And they said to the king of the Assyrians, The nations whom you deported and settled in the cities of Samaria did not know the judgment of the god of the land, and he sent the lions among them, and behold, they are putting them to death because they do not know the judgment of the god of the land.

**2 Kings 17:27**

And the king of the Assyrians commanded, saying, Take there one of the priests whom you deported from there, and let him go and dwell there and enlighten them about the judgment of the god of the land.

**2 Kings 17:28**

And they brought one of the priests whom they deported from Samaria, and he dwelt in Baithēl and was enlightening them how they should fear the Lord.

**2 Kings 17:29**

And nation by nation was making its own gods and putting them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans made, nation in the cities in which they were dwelling.

**2 Kings 17:30**

And the men of Babylon made Sokkōthbainith, and the men of Chouth made Nērigel, and the men of Aimath made Asimath,

**2 Kings 17:31**

**2 Kings 17:32**

And they were fearing the Lord and appointing for themselves priests of the high places from among themselves, and they were making for them in the houses of the high places.

**2 Kings 17:33**

They feared the Lord and served their gods according to the custom of the nations from which he deported them there.

**2 Kings 17:34**

Until this day they act according to their custom. They do not fear, and they do not act according to their ordinances and according to their judgment and according to the law and according to the commandment which the Lord commanded the sons of Iakōb, whom he named Israel.

**2 Kings 17:35**

And the Lord made a covenant with them and commanded them, saying, You shall not fear other gods, and you shall not bow down to them, and you shall not serve them, and you shall not sacrifice to them,

**2 Kings 17:36**

**2 Kings 17:37**

And the ordinances and the judgments and the law and the commandments which he wrote for you, you shall keep to do all the days, and you shall not fear other gods.

**2 Kings 17:38**

And the covenant which he made with you, you shall not forget, and you shall not fear other gods,

**2 Kings 17:39**

**2 Kings 17:40**

And you will not listen according to their judgment, which they do.

**2 Kings 17:41**

And these nations were fearing the Lord and were serving their carved images, and indeed their sons and the sons of their sons, just as their fathers did, they do until this day.

### Chapter 18

**2 Kings 18:1**

And it came to be in the third year of Ōsēe son of Ela, king of Israel, Ezekias son of Achaz king of Judah reigned.

**2 Kings 18:2**

**2 Kings 18:3**

And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Dauid his father did.

**2 Kings 18:4**

**2 Kings 18:5**

**2 Kings 18:6**

**2 Kings 18:7**

And the Lord was with him. In all that he did, he prospered. And he rebelled against the king of the Assyrians and did not serve him.

**2 Kings 18:8**

**2 Kings 18:9**

And it came to be in the fourth year of king Ezekias, which was the seventh year of Ōsēe son of Ela king of Israel, Salamanassar king of the Assyrians came up against Samaria and was besieging it.

**2 Kings 18:10**

And he captured it at the end of three years, in the sixth year of Ezekias, which was the ninth year of Ōsēe king of Israel, and Samaria was captured.

**2 Kings 18:11**

And the king of the Assyrians deported Samaria to the Assyrians and set them in Alae and in Abōr, river of Gōzan, and mountains of the Medes,

**2 Kings 18:12**
