**2 Kings 18:13**

And in the fourteenth year of king Ezekias, Sennachērim king of the Assyrians came up against the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

**2 Kings 18:14**

And Ezekias king of Judah sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians to Lachis, saying, I have sinned. Turn away from me. Whatever you impose on me I will bear. And the king of the Assyrians imposed on Ezekias king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.

**2 Kings 18:15**

And Ezekias gave all the silver found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king's house.

**2 Kings 18:16**

At that time Ezekias cut off the doors of the temple of the Lord and the supports which Ezekias king of Judah overlaid, and he gave them to the king of the Assyrians.

**2 Kings 18:17**

And the king of the Assyrians sent Tharthan and Raphis and Rapsakēs from Lachis to king Ezekias with a heavy force against Jerusalem, and they came up and came to Jerusalem and stood by the conduit of the upper pool on the way of the fuller's field.

**2 Kings 18:18**

And they called to Ezekias, and Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward and Somnas the scribe and Iōas son of Asaph the recorder came out to them.

**2 Kings 18:19**

And Rapsakēs said to them, Say now to Ezekias, Thus says the great king, king of the Assyrians: What is this confidence in which you have trusted?

**2 Kings 18:20**

You said, Only words of lips are counsel and strength for war. Now then, in whom have you trusted that you rebelled against me?

**2 Kings 18:21**

Now behold, you have trusted for yourself on this broken reed staff, on Egypt, on which if a man leans it will go into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.

**2 Kings 18:22**

And if you say to me, We have trusted in the Lord our God, is not this the one whose high places and altars Ezekias removed and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Before this altar in Jerusalem you shall bow?

**2 Kings 18:23**

And now make a bargain now with my lord king of the Assyrians, and I will give you two thousand horses if you are able to give riders for them.

**2 Kings 18:24**

And how will you turn away the face of one governor from the least of the servants of my lord? And you trusted for yourself in Egypt for chariots and horsemen.

**2 Kings 18:25**

And now, was it without the Lord that we came up against this place to destroy it? The Lord said to me, Go up against this land and destroy it.

**2 Kings 18:26**

And Eliakim son of Chelkias and Somnas and Iōas said to Rapsakēs, Speak now to your servants in Syrian, because we understand, and do not speak with us in Judean. Why do you speak in the ears of the people upon the wall?

**2 Kings 18:27**

And Rapsakēs said to them, Was it to your lord and to you that my lord sent me to speak these words? Was it not to the men sitting on the wall, to eat their dung and drink their urine with you?

**2 Kings 18:28**

And Rapsakēs stood and cried with a great voice in Judean and spoke and said, Hear the words of the great king, king of the Assyrians.

**2 Kings 18:29**

Thus says the king: Let not Ezekias lift you up with words, because he will not be able to deliver you from my hand.

**2 Kings 18:30**

And let not Ezekias make you hope in the Lord, saying, In delivering the Lord will deliver us. This city will not be given into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.

**2 Kings 18:31**

Do not listen to Ezekias, because thus says the king of the Assyrians: Make a blessing with me and come out to me, and each man will eat of his vine and each man will eat of his fig tree and each man will drink water from his cistern,

**2 Kings 18:32**

until I come and take you to a land like your land, a land of grain and wine and bread and vineyards, a land of olive oil and honey, and you will live and not die. And do not listen to Ezekias, because he deceives you, saying, The Lord will rescue us.

**2 Kings 18:33**

Have the gods of the nations, in delivering, delivered each his own land from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?

**2 Kings 18:34**

Where is the god of Aimath and Arphad? Where is the god of Seppharouain? And have they delivered Samaria from my hand?

**2 Kings 18:35**

Who among all the gods of the lands delivered their lands from my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?

**2 Kings 18:36**

And they kept silent and did not answer him a word, because it was the king's command, saying, You shall not answer him.

**2 Kings 18:37**

And Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward and Somnas the scribe and Iōas son of Asaph the recorder came to Ezekias with torn garments and reported to him the words of Rapsakēs.

### Chapter 19

**2 Kings 19:1**

And it came to be, when king Ezekias heard, he tore his garments and wrapped himself in sackcloth and entered into the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 19:2**

And he sent Eliakim the steward and Somnas the scribe and the elders of the priests clothed in sackcloth to Esaias the prophet son of Amōs.

**2 Kings 19:3**

And they said to him, Thus says Ezekias: This day is a day of affliction and rebuke and provocation, because sons came as far as birth pains and there is no strength for the woman giving birth.

**2 Kings 19:4**

If perhaps the Lord your God will hear all the words of Rapsakēs, whom the king of the Assyrians his lord sent to reproach the living God and to blaspheme in words which the Lord your God heard, then you shall take up prayer for the remnant that is found.

**2 Kings 19:5**

And the servants of king Ezekias came to Esaias.

**2 Kings 19:6**

And Esaias said to them, Thus you shall say to your lord: Thus says the Lord, Do not fear from the words which you heard, with which the servant-boys of the king of the Assyrians blasphemed.

**2 Kings 19:7**

Behold, I am putting a spirit in him, and he will hear a report and return to his land, and I will bring him down by the sword in his land.

**2 Kings 19:8**

And Rapsakēs returned and found the king of the Assyrians warring against Lobna, because he heard that he departed from Lachis.

**2 Kings 19:9**

And he heard concerning Tharaka king of the Ethiopians, saying, Behold, he came out to war with you. And he turned and sent messengers to Ezekias, saying,

**2 Kings 19:10**

Let not your God on whom you trust lift you up, saying, Jerusalem will not be given into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.

**2 Kings 19:11**

Behold, you heard all that the kings of the Assyrians did to all lands, to devote them. And will you be rescued?

**2 Kings 19:12**

Did the gods of the nations rescue them, those whom my fathers destroyed, both Gōzan and Charran and Raphes and sons of Edem in Thaesthen?

**2 Kings 19:13**

Where is the king of Aimath and the king of Arphad, and where is Seppharouain, Ana, and Aua?

**2 Kings 19:14**

And Ezekias took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them, and he went up to the house of the Lord, and Ezekias spread them out before the Lord.

**2 Kings 19:15**

And he said, Lord God of Israel, the one sitting upon the cherubim, you are God alone in all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.

**2 Kings 19:16**

Incline, Lord, your ear and hear. Open, Lord, your eyes and see. And hear the words of Sennachērim which he sent to reproach the living God.

**2 Kings 19:17**

Because truly, Lord, the kings of the Assyrians laid waste the nations

**2 Kings 19:18**

and gave their gods into the fire, because they are not gods but works of human hands, wood and stone, and they destroyed them.

**2 Kings 19:19**

And now, Lord our God, save us from his hand, and all the kingdoms of the earth will know that you alone, Lord, are God.

**2 Kings 19:20**

And Esaias son of Amōs sent to Ezekias, saying, Thus says the Lord God of the forces, the God of Israel: I heard what you prayed to me concerning Sennachērim king of the Assyrians.

**2 Kings 19:21**

This is the word which the Lord spoke against him: Virgin daughter of Siōn despised you and mocked you. Daughter Jerusalem shook her head over you.

**2 Kings 19:22**

Whom did you reproach and blaspheme? Against whom did you raise your voice and lift your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel.

**2 Kings 19:23**

By the hand of your messengers you reproached the Lord and said, By the multitude of my chariots I will go up to the heights of mountains, the sides of Lebanon, and I cut down the greatness of its cedar, its choice cypresses, and I came to the farthest part of its border, the forest of its Carmel.

**2 Kings 19:24**

I cooled and drank foreign waters, and with the sole of my foot I laid waste all rivers of a besieged land.

**2 Kings 19:25**

I formed it. Now I brought it, and it came to be for elevations of desolated settlements, fortified cities.

**2 Kings 19:26**

And those dwelling in them were weak of hand. They were dismayed and put to shame. They became grass of field and green herb, grass of rooftops and trampling before standing grain.

**2 Kings 19:27**

And your sitting and your going out and your going in I knew, and your rage against me.

**2 Kings 19:28**

Because you raged against me and your insolence went up in my ears, I will put my hooks in your nostrils and my bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back on the way by which you came.

**2 Kings 19:29**

And this to you is the sign: Eat this year what grows of itself, and in the second year the springing growth, and in the third sow and reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

**2 Kings 19:30**

And the remnant of the house of Judah that escaped and was left will again take root downward and make fruit upward.

**2 Kings 19:31**

Because from Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and one preserved from Mount Siōn. The zeal of the Lord of forces will do this.

**2 Kings 19:32**

Not so. Thus says the Lord to the king of the Assyrians: He will not enter into this city and will not shoot there an arrow and will not come before it with shield and will certainly not cast up against it a mound.

**2 Kings 19:33**

By the way that he came, by it he will return, and into this city he will not enter, says the Lord.

**2 Kings 19:34**

And I will shield this city for my own sake and for Dauid my servant.

**2 Kings 19:35**

And it came to be by night, and an angel of the Lord went out and struck in the camp of the Assyrians one hundred eighty-five thousand. And they rose early in the morning, and behold, all were dead bodies.

**2 Kings 19:36**

And Sennachērim king of the Assyrians departed and went and returned and dwelt in Nineuē.

**2 Kings 19:37**

And it came to be, while he was bowing in the house of Neserach his god, Adramelech and Sarasar his sons struck him with the sword, and they escaped into the land of Ararat, and Asordan his son reigned in his place.

### Chapter 20

**2 Kings 20:1**

In those days Ezekias became sick unto death, and Esaias son of Amōs the prophet entered to him and said to him, Thus says the Lord: Give command to your house, because you are dying and will not live.

**2 Kings 20:2**

And Ezekias turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord, saying,

**2 Kings 20:3**

O Lord, remember now how I walked before you in truth and with a full heart and did what was good in your eyes. And Ezekias wept with great weeping.

**2 Kings 20:4**

And Esaias was in the middle court, and word of the Lord came to him, saying,

**2 Kings 20:5**

Turn back and say to Ezekias the leader of my people, Thus says the Lord God of Dauid your father: I heard your prayer, I saw your tears. Behold, I will heal you. On the third day you will go up into the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 20:6**

And I will add fifteen years to your days, and from the hand of the king of the Assyrians I will save you and this city, and I will shield this city for my own sake and for Dauid my servant.

**2 Kings 20:7**

And he said, Let them take a cake of figs and let them put it upon the sore, and he will recover.

**2 Kings 20:8**

And Ezekias said to Esaias, What is the sign that the Lord will heal me and I will go up into the house of the Lord on the third day?

**2 Kings 20:9**

And Esaias said, This is the sign from the Lord that the Lord will do the word which he spoke. Shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or shall it turn back ten steps?

**2 Kings 20:10**

And Ezekias said, It is a light thing for the shadow to slope ten steps. No, but let the shadow turn back ten steps.

**2 Kings 20:11**

And Esaias the prophet cried to the Lord, and the shadow turned back on the steps ten steps backward.

**2 Kings 20:12**

At that time Marōdachbaladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and a gift to Ezekias, because he heard that Ezekias was sick.

**2 Kings 20:13**

And Ezekias rejoiced over them and showed them his whole treasure-house, the silver and the gold, the spices and the good oil and the house of the vessels and all that was found in his treasuries. There was not a thing which Ezekias did not show them in his house and in all his dominion.

**2 Kings 20:14**

And Esaias the prophet entered to king Ezekias and said to him, What did these men say, and from where did they come to you? And Ezekias said, They came to me from a far land, from Babylon.

**2 Kings 20:15**

And he said, What did they see in your house? And he said, They saw all that is in my house. There was not a thing in my house or in my treasuries that I did not show them.

**2 Kings 20:16**

And Esaias said to Ezekias, Hear word of the Lord.

**2 Kings 20:17**

Behold, days are coming, and everything in your house and whatever your fathers stored up to this day will be taken to Babylon, and not a thing will be left, which the Lord said.

**2 Kings 20:18**

And from your sons who will come out from you, whom you will beget, they will take, and they will be eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon.

**2 Kings 20:19**

And Ezekias said to Esaias, Good is the word of the Lord which you spoke. Let there be peace in my days.

**2 Kings 20:20**

And the rest of the words of Ezekias and all his might and what he did, the spring and the conduit, and how he brought the water into the city, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 20:21**

And Ezekias slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of Dauid, and Manassēs his son reigned in his place.

### Chapter 21

**2 Kings 21:1**

Manassēs was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Opsiaba.

**2 Kings 21:2**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord drove out from before the sons of Israel.

**2 Kings 21:3**

And he turned back and rebuilt the high places which Ezekias his father tore down and raised up an altar to Baal and made groves, as Achaab king of Israel did, and bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.

**2 Kings 21:4**

And he built altars in the house of the Lord, of which he said, In Jerusalem I will put my name.

**2 Kings 21:5**

And he built altars to all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 21:6**

And he made his sons pass through fire and practiced divination and omens and made spirit-mediums and knowers. He multiplied to do evil in the eyes of the Lord, to provoke him.

**2 Kings 21:7**

And he set the carved image of the grove in the house, of which the Lord said to Dauid and to Salōmōn his son, In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name there forever.

**2 Kings 21:8**

And I will not again add to shake the foot of Israel from the land which I gave to their fathers, if only they keep all that I commanded, according to all the commandment which my servant Moses commanded them.

**2 Kings 21:9**

And they did not listen, and Manassēs led them astray to do evil in the eyes of the Lord beyond the nations which the Lord destroyed from before the sons of Israel.

**2 Kings 21:10**

And the Lord spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets, saying,

**2 Kings 21:11**

Because Manassēs king of Judah did these evil abominations, beyond all that the Amorrite who was before him did, and even caused Judah to sin with their idols,

**2 Kings 21:12**

not so. Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing evils on Jerusalem and on Judah, so that whoever hears, both his ears will ring.

**2 Kings 21:13**

And I will stretch over Jerusalem the measure of Samaria and the plummet of the house of Achaab, and I will wipe Jerusalem as an alabaster vessel is wiped, being wiped and turned on its face.

**2 Kings 21:14**

And I will push away the remnant of my inheritance and give them into the hands of their enemies, and they will become plunder and spoil to all their enemies,

**2 Kings 21:15**

because they did evil in my eyes and were provoking me from the day I brought out their fathers from Egypt until this day.

**2 Kings 21:16**

And Manassēs also poured out very much innocent blood until he filled Jerusalem from mouth to mouth, besides his sins with which he made Judah sin by doing evil in the eyes of the Lord.

**2 Kings 21:17**

And the rest of the words of Manassēs and all that he did and the sin which he sinned, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 21:18**

And Manassēs slept with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Oza, and Amōn his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 21:19**

Amōn was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Mesollam daughter of Arōs from Ieteba.

**2 Kings 21:20**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, as Manassēs his father did.

**2 Kings 21:21**

And he walked in every way in which his father walked and served the idols which his father served and bowed down to them.

**2 Kings 21:22**

And he abandoned the Lord God of his fathers and did not walk in the way of the Lord.

**2 Kings 21:23**

And the servants of Amōn conspired against him and put the king to death in his house.

**2 Kings 21:24**

And all the people of the land struck down all those conspiring against king Amōn, and the people of the land made Iōsias his son king in his place.

**2 Kings 21:25**

And the rest of the words of Amōn, what he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 21:26**

And they buried him in his tomb in the garden of Oza, and Iōsias his son reigned in his place.

### Chapter 22

**2 Kings 22:1**

Iōsias was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Iedida daughter of Edeia from Basourōth.

**2 Kings 22:2**

And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord and walked in every way of Dauid his father. He did not turn aside to the right or to the left.

**2 Kings 22:3**

And it came to be in the eighteenth year of king Iōsias, in the eighth month, the king sent Saphphan son of Eseliou son of Mesollam, the scribe of the house of the Lord, saying,

**2 Kings 22:4**

Go up to Chelkias the high priest and seal the silver brought into the house of the Lord, which the keepers of the threshold gathered from the people.

**2 Kings 22:5**

And let them give it into the hand of those doing the works, those appointed in the house of the Lord. And he gave it to those doing the works, those in the house of the Lord, to strengthen the breach of the house,

**2 Kings 22:6**

to the carpenters and the builders and the masons, and to buy timber and quarried stones to strengthen the breach of the house.

**2 Kings 22:7**

Only, they did not reckon with them the silver being given to them, because they act in faithfulness.

**2 Kings 22:8**

And Chelkias the high priest said to Saphphan the scribe, I found a book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Chelkias gave the book to Saphphan, and he read it.

**2 Kings 22:9**

And Saphphan brought it to king Iōsias and brought word back to the king and said, Your servants poured out the silver found in the house of the Lord and gave it into the hand of those doing the works, those appointed in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 22:10**

And Saphphan the scribe said to the king, saying, Chelkias the priest gave me a book. And Saphphan read it before the king.

**2 Kings 22:11**

And it came to be, when the king heard the words of the book of the law, he tore his garments.

**2 Kings 22:12**

And the king commanded Chelkias the priest and Achikam son of Saphphan and Achobōr son of Micha and Saphphan the scribe and Asaia servant of the king, saying,

**2 Kings 22:13**

Go, seek the Lord concerning me and concerning all the people and concerning all Judah, concerning the words of this book that was found, because great is the anger of the Lord, which burns in us, because our fathers did not listen to all the words of this book to do according to all written for us.

**2 Kings 22:14**

And Chelkias the priest and Achikam and Achobōr and Saphphan and Asaia went to Oldan the prophetess, wife of Sellēm son of Thekoue son of Araas keeper of the wardrobe, and she dwelt in Jerusalem in the Maseña, and they spoke to her.

**2 Kings 22:15**

And she said to them, Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me,

**2 Kings 22:16**

Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing evils upon this place and upon those dwelling in it, all the words of the book which the king of Judah read,

**2 Kings 22:17**

because they abandoned me and burned incense to other gods, so as to provoke me in all the works of their hands, and my wrath will burn in this place and will not be quenched.

**2 Kings 22:18**

And to the king of Judah who sent you to seek the Lord, thus you shall say to him: Thus says the Lord God of Israel concerning the words which you heard:

**2 Kings 22:19**

Because your heart was softened and you were ashamed from before the Lord when you heard what I spoke against this place and against those dwelling in it, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and you tore your garments and wept before me, I also heard, says the Lord.

**2 Kings 22:20**

Not so. Behold, I am adding you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your tomb in peace, and your eyes will not see among all the evils that I am bringing upon this place. And they returned word to the king.

### Chapter 23

**2 Kings 23:1**

And the king sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 23:2**

And the king went up to the house of the Lord, and every man of Judah and all those dwelling in Jerusalem with him, and the priests and the prophets and all the people from small to great. And he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant found in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 23:3**

And the king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his ordinances with all heart and with all soul, to establish the words of this covenant written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant.

**2 Kings 23:4**

And the king commanded Chelkias the high priest and the priests of the second order and the keepers of the threshold to bring out from the temple of the Lord all the vessels made for Baal and for the grove and for all the force of heaven, and he burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kedrōn and carried their dust to Baithēl.

**2 Kings 23:5**

And he put an end to the idol-priests whom the kings of Judah appointed and who were burning incense in the high places and in the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, and those burning incense to Baal and to the sun and to the moon and to the Mazouroth and to all the force of heaven.

**2 Kings 23:6**

And he brought the grove out from the house of the Lord, outside Jerusalem to the wadi Kedrōn, and burned it in the wadi Kedrōn and beat it small to dust and threw its dust on the tombs of the sons of the people.

**2 Kings 23:7**

And he tore down the houses of the consecrated ones which were in the house of the Lord, where the women were weaving hangings for the grove.

**2 Kings 23:8**

And he brought all the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where the priests burned incense, from Gabaa to Bērsabee, and he tore down the house of the gates by the entrance of the gate of Iēsous governor of the city, those on the left at the gate of the city.

**2 Kings 23:9**

Only, the priests of the high places did not go up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, except they ate unleavened bread in the midst of their brothers.

**2 Kings 23:10**

And he defiled Topheth in the valley of the son of Ennom, so as not to make a man bring his son or a man bring his daughter through fire to Moloch.

**2 Kings 23:11**

And he put an end to the horses which the kings of Judah gave to the sun at the entrance of the house of the Lord, in the treasury of Nathan the king's eunuch in the suburbs, and the chariot of the sun he burned with fire.

**2 Kings 23:12**

And the altars on the roof of the upper room of Achaz, which the kings of Judah made, and the altars which Manassēs made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, the king tore down and broke up there and threw their dust into the wadi Kedrōn.

**2 Kings 23:13**

And the house that was before Jerusalem, to the right of the mount of Mosoath, which Salōmōn king of Israel built to Astartē, abomination of the Sidonians, and to Chamōs, abomination of Moab, and to Molochol, abomination of the sons of Ammon, the king defiled.

**2 Kings 23:14**

And he crushed the pillars and destroyed the groves and filled their places with human bones.

**2 Kings 23:15**

And indeed the altar in Baithēl, the high place which Ieroboam son of Nabat made, who made Israel sin, indeed that altar and the high place he tore down and crushed its stones and beat them small to dust and burned the grove.

**2 Kings 23:16**

And Iōsias turned and saw the tombs there in the city, and he sent and took the bones from the tombs and burned them upon the altar and defiled it, according to the word of the Lord which the man of God spoke.

**2 Kings 23:17**

And he said, What is that marker which I see? And the men of the city said to him, It is the man of God who came out from Judah and called out these words which he called out against the altar of Baithēl.

**2 Kings 23:18**

And he said, Leave him. Let no man move his bones. And they preserved his bones with the bones of the prophet who came out from Samaria.

**2 Kings 23:19**

And also all the houses of the high places which were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel made to provoke the Lord, Iōsias removed and did to them according to all the deeds that he did in Baithēl.

**2 Kings 23:20**

And he sacrificed all the priests of the high places who were there upon the altars and burned the bones of humans upon them and returned to Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 23:21**

And the king commanded all the people, saying, Keep the Passover to the Lord our God, as it is written in this book of the covenant.

**2 Kings 23:22**

Because this Passover was not held from the days of the judges who judged Israel and all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah,

**2 Kings 23:23**

except in the eighteenth year of king Iōsias this Passover was held to the Lord in Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 23:24**

And indeed the spirit-mediums and the knowers and the theraphin and the idols and all the abominations that had appeared in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem king Iōsias removed, to establish the words of the law written upon the book which Chelkias the priest found in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 23:25**

Like him there was no king before him who turned to the Lord with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength according to all the law of Moses, and after him none like him arose.

**2 Kings 23:26**

Only, the Lord did not turn away from the fury of his great anger, with which his anger burned in Judah, because of the provocations with which Manassēs provoked him.

**2 Kings 23:27**

And the Lord said, Also Judah I will remove from before my face, as I removed Israel, and I will reject this city which I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, My name will be there.

**2 Kings 23:28**

And the rest of the words of Iōsias and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 23:29**

And in his days Pharaoh Nechao king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians by the river Euphrates, and Iōsias went to meet him, and Nechao put him to death in Mageddō when he saw him.

**2 Kings 23:30**

And his servants set him on the chariot, dead from Mageddō, and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb in the city of Dauid. And the people of the land took Ioachas son of Iōsias and anointed him and made him king in place of his father.

**2 Kings 23:31**

Ioachas was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Amital daughter of Ieremiou from Lemna.

**2 Kings 23:32**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord according to all that his fathers did.

**2 Kings 23:33**

And Pharaoh Nechao removed him in Deblatha in the land of Emath so that he should not reign in Jerusalem, and he imposed a penalty on the land of a hundred talents of silver and a hundred talents of gold.

**2 Kings 23:34**

And Pharaoh Nechao made Eliakim son of Iōsias king of Judah king in place of Iōsias his father, and he changed his name to Ioakim, and he took Ioachas and brought him into Egypt, and he died there.

**2 Kings 23:35**

And Ioakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh, but he assessed the land to give the silver according to the mouth of Pharaoh. Each man according to his valuation they gave the silver and the gold with the people of the land, to give to Pharaoh Nechao.

**2 Kings 23:36**

Ioakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Ieldaph daughter of Phedeia from Rouma.

**2 Kings 23:37**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord according to all that his fathers did.

### Chapter 24

**2 Kings 24:1**

In his days Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon came up, and Ioakim became his servant three years, and he turned and rebelled against him.

**2 Kings 24:2**

And the Lord sent against him raiding bands of the Chaldeans and raiding bands of Syria and raiding bands of Moab and raiding bands of the sons of Ammon, and he sent them into the land of Judah to strengthen against it, according to the word of the Lord which he spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets.

**2 Kings 24:3**

Only, it was upon the anger of the Lord in Judah to remove him from before his face, because of the sins of Manassēs according to all that he did,

**2 Kings 24:4**

and indeed he poured out innocent blood and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the Lord did not wish to be propitiated.

**2 Kings 24:5**

And the rest of the words of Ioakim and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 24:6**

And Ioakim slept with his fathers, and Ioakim his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 24:7**

And the king of Egypt no longer added to go out from his land, because the king of Babylon took from the wadi of Egypt as far as the river Euphrates, all that belonged to the king of Egypt.

**2 Kings 24:8**

Ioakim was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Nestha daughter of Ellanathan from Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 24:9**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord according to all that his father did.

**2 Kings 24:10**

At that time Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.

**2 Kings 24:11**

And Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon entered into the city, and his servants were besieging it.

**2 Kings 24:12**

And Ioakim king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he and his servants and his mother and his rulers and his eunuchs, and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

**2 Kings 24:13**

And he carried out from there all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house and cut in pieces all the golden vessels which Salōmōn king of Israel made in the temple of the Lord, according to the word of the Lord.

**2 Kings 24:14**

And he deported Jerusalem and all the rulers and the mighty in strength, ten thousand in captivity, and every craftsman and every smith, and none was left except the poor of the land.

**2 Kings 24:15**

And he deported Ioakim to Babylon, and the king's mother and the king's wives and his eunuchs and the mighty of the land he led away in exile from Jerusalem into Babylon.

**2 Kings 24:16**

And all the men of force, seven thousand, and the craftsman and the smith, a thousand, all mighty ones making war, the king of Babylon brought them as exiles into Babylon.

**2 Kings 24:17**

And the king of Babylon made Maththania his kinsman king in his place and set his name Sedekia.

**2 Kings 24:18**

Sedekias was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Amital daughter of Ieremiou.

**2 Kings 24:19**

And he did evil before the Lord according to all that Ioakim did.

**2 Kings 24:20**

Because it was upon the anger of the Lord against Jerusalem and Judah until he cast them from before his face. And Sedekias rebelled against the kingdom of Babylon.

### Chapter 25

**2 Kings 25:1**

And it came to be in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon came, and all his force, against Jerusalem, and they encamped against it and built a siege-wall around it.

**2 Kings 25:2**

And the city came under siege until the eleventh year of king Sedekias.

**2 Kings 25:3**

On the ninth day of the month, famine became strong in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

**2 Kings 25:4**

And the city was breached, and all the men of war went out by night by way of the gate between the walls, which is by the king's garden, and the Chaldeans were around the city, and he went by way of the Arabah.

**2 Kings 25:5**

And the force of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Ierichō, and all his force was scattered from upon him.

**2 Kings 25:6**

And they captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Deblatha, and he spoke judgment with him.

**2 Kings 25:7**

And he slaughtered the sons of Sedekias before his eyes, and the eyes of Sedekias he blinded, and he bound him in fetters and brought him into Babylon.

**2 Kings 25:8**

And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon, Nabouzardan the chief guard, standing before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 25:9**

And he burned the house of the Lord and the king's house and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great house he burned.

**2 Kings 25:10**

And the force of the Chaldeans that was with the chief guard tore down the walls of Jerusalem all around.

**2 Kings 25:11**

And the rest of the people left in the city and those who had fallen away, who fell to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the support Nabouzardan the chief guard removed.

**2 Kings 25:12**

And from the poor of the land the chief guard left some for vinedressers and field-workers.

**2 Kings 25:13**

And the bronze pillars in the house of the Lord and the bases and the bronze sea in the house of the Lord the Chaldeans broke up and carried their bronze into Babylon.

**2 Kings 25:14**

And the pots and the shovels and the bowls and the censers and all the bronze vessels with which they ministered, he took.

**2 Kings 25:15**

And the firepans and the bowls, those of gold and those of silver, the chief guard took.

**2 Kings 25:16**

The two pillars, the one sea, and the bases which Salōmōn made for the house of the Lord, there was no weight to the bronze of all the vessels.

**2 Kings 25:17**

Eighteen cubits was the height of the one pillar, and the bronze capital was upon it, and the height of the capital was three cubits, with network and pomegranates upon the capital round about, all bronze. And the same for the second pillar with the network.

**2 Kings 25:18**

And the chief guard took Saraian the first priest and Sophonian of the second order and the three keeping the threshold.

**2 Kings 25:19**

And from the city he took one eunuch who was overseer over the men of war and five men of those seeing the king's face who were found in the city and the scribe of the ruler of the force, the one mustering the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land found in the city.

**2 Kings 25:20**

And Nabouzardan the chief guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Deblatha.

**2 Kings 25:21**

And the king of Babylon struck them and put them to death in Deblatha in the land of Aimath, and Judah was deported from its land.

**2 Kings 25:22**

And the people left in the land of Judah, whom Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon left, over them he appointed Godolias son of Achikam son of Saphphan.

**2 Kings 25:23**

And all the commanders of the force, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon appointed Godolias, and they came to Godolias at Massēphath, even Ismaēl son of Nathaniou and Iōanan son of Karēe and Saraias son of Thanemeth the Netophathite and Iezonias son of the Maachathite, they and their men.

**2 Kings 25:24**

And Godolias swore to them and to their men and said to them, Do not fear the servants of the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well for you.

**2 Kings 25:25**

And it came to be in the seventh month, Ismaēl son of Nathaniou son of Elisama from the seed of the kings, and ten men with him, came and struck Godolias, and he died, and also the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Massēphath.

**2 Kings 25:26**

And all the people rose, from small to great, and the commanders of the forces, and they entered into Egypt, because they feared from before the Chaldeans.

**2 Kings 25:27**

And it came to be in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Ioakim king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, Euilmarōdach king of Babylon, in the year of his reign, lifted up the head of Ioakim king of Judah from prison.

**2 Kings 25:28**

And he spoke good things with him and gave his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.

**2 Kings 25:29**

And he changed the garments of his prison, and he ate bread continually before him all the days of his life.

**2 Kings 25:30**

And his allowance, a continual allowance, was given to him from the king's house, a matter of a day in its day, all the days of his life.

## 1 Chronicles

### Chapter 1

**1 Chronicles 1:1**

Adam, Seth, Enos,

**1 Chronicles 1:2**

Kainan, Maleleel, Iared,

**1 Chronicles 1:3**

Enoch, Mathousala, Lamech,

**1 Chronicles 1:4**

Noe. Sons of Noe: Sem, Cham, Iapheth.

**1 Chronicles 1:5**

Sons of Iapheth: Gamer, Magog, Madai, Iouan, Elisa, Thobel, Mosoch, and Thiras.

**1 Chronicles 1:6**

Sons of Gamer: Aschanaz, Riphath, and Thorgama.

**1 Chronicles 1:7**

Sons of Iouan: Elisa, Tharsis, Kitioi, and Rhodioi.

**1 Chronicles 1:8**

Sons of Cham: Chous, Mestraim, Phoud, and Chanaan.

**1 Chronicles 1:9**

Sons of Chous: Saba, Euilat, Sabatha, Regma, and Sebekatha. Sons of Regma: Saba and Oudadan.

**1 Chronicles 1:10**

And Chous begot Nebrod. This one began to be a giant hunter upon the earth.

**1 Chronicles 1:17**

Sons of Sem: Ailam and Assour and Arphaxad.

**1 Chronicles 1:24**

Sala.

**1 Chronicles 1:25**

Eber, Phalek, Ragau,

**1 Chronicles 1:26**

Serouch, Nachor, Thara,

**1 Chronicles 1:27**

Abraam.

**1 Chronicles 1:28**

And sons of Abraam: Isaak and Ismael.

**1 Chronicles 1:29**

And these are their generations: Nabaioth the firstborn of Ismael, and Kedar, Nabdeel, Mabsan,

**1 Chronicles 1:30**

Masma, Idouma, Masse, Choddad, Thaiman,

**1 Chronicles 1:31**

Iettour, Naphes, and Kedma. These are sons of Ismael.

**1 Chronicles 1:32**

And sons of Chettoura, concubine of Abraam, and she bore to him Zembran, Iexan, Madan, Madiam, Sobak, Soe. And sons of Iexan: Saba and Daidan.

**1 Chronicles 1:33**

And sons of Madiam: Gaipha, Opher, Enoch, Abida, and Eldaa. All these were sons of Chettoura.

**1 Chronicles 1:34**

And Abraam begot Isaak. Sons of Isaak: Esau and Iakob.

**1 Chronicles 1:35**

Sons of Esau: Eliphas, Ragouel, Ieoul, Ieglom, and Kore.

**1 Chronicles 1:36**

Sons of Eliphas: Thaiman, Omar, Sophar, Gootham, Kenez, and from Thamna, Amalek.

**1 Chronicles 1:37**

And sons of Ragouel: Nacheth, Zare, Some, and Moze.

**1 Chronicles 1:38**

Sons of Seir: Lotan, Sobal, Sebegon, Ana, Deson, Osar, and Daison.

**1 Chronicles 1:39**

And sons of Lotan: Chorri and Aiman, and Ailath and Namna.

**1 Chronicles 1:40**

Sons of Sobal: Golam, Manachath, Gaibel, Sob, and Onam. And sons of Sebegon: Aia and Ana.

**1 Chronicles 1:41**

Sons of Ana: Daison. Sons of Daison: Emeron, Eseban, Iethran, and Charran.

**1 Chronicles 1:42**

And sons of Osar: Balaan, Zoukan, and Iokan. Sons of Daison also: Os and Arran.

**1 Chronicles 1:43**

And these were their kings: Balak son of Beor, and name of his city was Dennaba.

**1 Chronicles 1:44**

And Balak died, and Iobab son of Zara from Bosorra reigned in his place.

**1 Chronicles 1:45**

And Iobab died, and Asom from the land of the Thaimanites reigned in his place.

**1 Chronicles 1:46**

And Asom died, and Adad son of Barad, who struck Madiam in the plain of Moab, reigned in his place, and name of his city was Geththaim.

**1 Chronicles 1:47**

And Adad died, and Samaa from Masekka reigned in his place.

**1 Chronicles 1:48**

And Samaa died, and Saoul from Rooboth by the river reigned in his place.

**1 Chronicles 1:49**

And Saoul died, and Balaennon son of Achobor reigned in his place.

**1 Chronicles 1:50**

And Balaennon son of Achobor died, and Adad son of Barad reigned in his place, and name of his city was Phogor.

**1 Chronicles 1:51**

And Adad died, and the chiefs of Edom were: chief Thamana, chief Gola, chief Ietheth,

**1 Chronicles 1:52**

chief Elibamas, chief Elas, chief Phinons,

**1 Chronicles 1:53**

chief Kenez, chief Thaiman, chief Mabsar,

**1 Chronicles 1:54**

chief Megediel, chief Iram. These were chiefs of Edom.

### Chapter 2

**1 Chronicles 2:1**

These are names of the sons of Israel: Rouben, Symeon, Leui, Iouda, Issachar, Zaboulon,

**1 Chronicles 2:2**

Dan, Ioseph, Beniamin, Nephthali, Gad, Aser.

**1 Chronicles 2:3**

And Thamar his bride bore to him Phares and Zara. All sons of Iouda were five.

**1 Chronicles 2:5**

Sons of Phares: Arson and Iemouel.

**1 Chronicles 2:6**

And sons of Zara: Zambri, Aithan, Aiman, Chalchal, and Dara, all five.

**1 Chronicles 2:7**

**1 Chronicles 2:8**

**1 Chronicles 2:9**

**1 Chronicles 2:10**

**1 Chronicles 2:11**

**1 Chronicles 2:17**

**1 Chronicles 2:18**

**1 Chronicles 2:20**

**1 Chronicles 2:22**

**1 Chronicles 2:23**

**1 Chronicles 2:24**

**1 Chronicles 2:25**

**1 Chronicles 2:26**

**1 Chronicles 2:27**

And sons of Ram firstborn of Ieremeel were Maas, Iamin, and Akor.

**1 Chronicles 2:28**

And sons of Ozom were Samai and Iadae. And sons of Samai: Nadab and Abisour.

**1 Chronicles 2:29**

**1 Chronicles 2:30**

Sons of Nadab: Saled and Apphaim. And Saled died having no children.

**1 Chronicles 2:31**

**1 Chronicles 2:32**

And sons of Iadae: Achisamai, Iether, and Ionathan. And Iether died having no children.

**1 Chronicles 2:33**

And sons of Ionathan: Phaleth and Ozaza. These were sons of Ieremeel.

**1 Chronicles 2:34**

And Sosan had no sons, only daughters. And Sosan had an Egyptian servant, and his name was Iochel.

**1 Chronicles 2:35**

**1 Chronicles 2:36**

And Eththi begot Nathan, and Nathan begot Zabed.

**1 Chronicles 2:37**

And Zabed begot Aphalel, and Aphalel begot Obed.

**1 Chronicles 2:38**

And Obed begot Ieou, and Ieou begot Azarian.

**1 Chronicles 2:39**

And Azarias begot Chelles, and Chelles begot Eleasa.

**1 Chronicles 2:40**

And Eleasa begot Sosomei, and Sosomei begot Saloum.

**1 Chronicles 2:41**

And Saloum begot Iechemian, and Iechemias begot Elisama.

**1 Chronicles 2:42**

And sons of Chaleb brother of Ieremeel: Marisa his firstborn. This one was father of Ziph, and sons of Marisa father of Chebron.

**1 Chronicles 2:43**

And sons of Chebron: Kore, Thappous, Rekom, and Semaa.

**1 Chronicles 2:44**

And Semaa begot Raem father of Ierkaan, and Ierkaan begot Samai.

**1 Chronicles 2:45**

And his son was Maon, and Maon was father of Baithsour.

**1 Chronicles 2:46**

And Gaipha, concubine of Chaleb, bore Arran and Mosa and Gezoue, and Arran begot Gezoue.

**1 Chronicles 2:47**

And sons of Iadai: Ragem, Ioatham, Gerson, Phalet, Gaipha, and Sagaph.

**1 Chronicles 2:48**

And concubine of Chaleb, Mocha, bore Saber and Tharchna.

**1 Chronicles 2:49**

And Sagaph begot father of Marmena and Saou father of Machabena and father of Gaibaa. And daughter of Chaleb was Ascha.

**1 Chronicles 2:50**

These were sons of Chaleb, sons of Or firstborn of Ephratha: Sobal father of Kariathiarim,

**1 Chronicles 2:51**

Salomon father of Baithlaem, Arim father of Baithgedor.

**1 Chronicles 2:52**

And sons of Sobal father of Kariathiarim were Araa, Esi, and Ammanith.

**1 Chronicles 2:53**

Emospheos, city of Iair, Aithalim, Miphithim, and Esamathim and Amasaraim. From these came out the Sarathaians and the Esthaolaians.

**1 Chronicles 2:54**

Sons of Salomon: Baithlaem, Netophathi, Ataroth, house of Ioab, and half of the Manathi, Esarei.

**1 Chronicles 2:55**

Families of scribes dwelling in Iabes: Thargathiim, Samathiim, Sookathiim. These are the Kinaioi who came from Mesema, father of the house of Rechab.

### Chapter 3

**1 Chronicles 3:1**

and Nage and Naphag and Ianoue,

**1 Chronicles 3:21**

### Chapter 4

**1 Chronicles 4:1**

**1 Chronicles 4:4**

**1 Chronicles 4:5**

**1 Chronicles 4:6**

**1 Chronicles 4:7**

**1 Chronicles 4:8**

**1 Chronicles 4:9**

**1 Chronicles 4:10**

**1 Chronicles 4:11**

And Chaleb father of Ascha begot Machir. This one was father of Assathon.

**1 Chronicles 4:12**

**1 Chronicles 4:14**

**1 Chronicles 4:15**

And sons of Chaleb son of Iephonne: Era, Ala, and Noom. And sons of Ala: Kenez.

**1 Chronicles 4:16**

And his son: Geseel, Aemiachi, Zapha, Zaira, and Eserael.

**1 Chronicles 4:17**

And sons of Esri: Iether, Morad, Apher, and Ialon. And Iether begot Maron and Semai and Mareth father of Esthemon.

**1 Chronicles 4:18**

**1 Chronicles 4:19**

**1 Chronicles 4:20**

**1 Chronicles 4:21**

**1 Chronicles 4:22**

**1 Chronicles 4:23**

**1 Chronicles 4:24**

Sons of Symeon: Namouel and Iamin, Iarib, Zara, Saul,

**1 Chronicles 4:25**

Salem his son, Mabasam his son, Masma his son,

**1 Chronicles 4:26**

Amouel his son, Saboud his son, Zakchour his son, Semei his son.

**1 Chronicles 4:27**

And to Semei were sixteen sons and three daughters, and to their brothers there were not many sons, and all their families did not multiply like sons of Iouda.

**1 Chronicles 4:28**

And they dwelt in Bersabee and Samaa and Molada and Esersoual

**1 Chronicles 4:29**

**1 Chronicles 4:30**

and Bathouel and Erma and Seklag

**1 Chronicles 4:31**

**1 Chronicles 4:32**

**1 Chronicles 4:33**

**1 Chronicles 4:34**

And Mosobab and Iemoloch and Iosia son of Amasia

**1 Chronicles 4:35**

and Ioel, and this one was son of Isabia son of Saraia son of Asiel,

**1 Chronicles 4:36**

and Elioenai and Iakaba and Iasouia and Asaia and Ediel and Ismael and Banaia

**1 Chronicles 4:37**

and Zouza son of Sephei son of Allon son of Iedia son of Samari son of Samaiou.

**1 Chronicles 4:38**

These who came by names were rulers in their generations, and in houses of their fathers they were multiplied into a multitude.

**1 Chronicles 4:39**

And they went until coming to Gerara, to the east of the valley, to seek pasture for their cattle.

**1 Chronicles 4:40**

And they found rich and good pasture, and the land before them was wide, and peace and quiet, because from sons of Cham those dwelling there had been before.

**1 Chronicles 4:41**

And these who were written by name came in days of Ezekias king of Judah and struck their houses and the Minaeans whom they found there and devoted them until this day and dwelt in their place, because there was pasture there for their cattle.

**1 Chronicles 4:42**

And from them, from the sons of Symeon, five hundred men went to Mount Seir, and Phalettia and Noadia and Raphaia and Oziel, sons of Iesi, were their leaders.

**1 Chronicles 4:43**

And they struck the remaining survivors of Amalek and dwelt there until this day.

### Chapter 5

**1 Chronicles 5:1**

And sons of Rouben, firstborn of Israel, because he was the firstborn, but when he went up upon the bed of his father, his blessing was given to his son Ioseph son of Israel, and he was not enrolled for firstborn rights,

**1 Chronicles 5:2**

because Iouda was strong in power among his brothers, and from him came a ruler, but the blessing was Ioseph's.

**1 Chronicles 5:3**

Sons of Rouben firstborn of Israel: Enoch, Phallous, Arson, and Charmi.

**1 Chronicles 5:4**

**1 Chronicles 5:5**

his son Micha, his son Recha, his son Baal,

**1 Chronicles 5:6**

his son Beeera, whom Thaglathphalnasar king of Assour deported. He was ruler of the Roubenites.

**1 Chronicles 5:7**

**1 Chronicles 5:8**

and Balek son of Ozouz son of Sama son of Ioel. He dwelt in Aroer and upon Nabaub and Beelmaon,

**1 Chronicles 5:9**

**1 Chronicles 5:10**

**1 Chronicles 5:11**

**1 Chronicles 5:12**

**1 Chronicles 5:13**

**1 Chronicles 5:14**

**1 Chronicles 5:15**

son of Abdiēl son of Gouni, chief of house of fathers.

**1 Chronicles 5:16**

They dwelt in Galaad in Basan and in its towns and all the surrounding regions of Saron, to their extremity.

**1 Chronicles 5:17**

The enrollment of all of them was in the days of Iōatham king of Judah and in the days of Ieroboam king of Israel.

**1 Chronicles 5:18**

Sons of Rouben and Gad and half tribe of Manassē, from sons of power, men bearing shields and sword and drawing bow and taught in war, forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty, going out to war.

**1 Chronicles 5:19**

And they made war with the Hagarenes and Itoureans and Naphisaians and Nadabaians.

**1 Chronicles 5:20**

And they prevailed over them, and the Hagaraians and all their tents were given into their hands, because they cried to God in the war, and he heard them, because they hoped in him.

**1 Chronicles 5:21**

And they took captive their goods: five thousand camels, two hundred fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys, and one hundred thousand human lives.

**1 Chronicles 5:22**

**1 Chronicles 5:23**

And the half tribe of Manassē dwelt in the land from Basan to Baalermon and Sanir and Mount Aermon and in Lebanon. They multiplied.

**1 Chronicles 5:24**

And these were chiefs of houses of their fathers: Opher and Isei and Eliēl and Esdriēl and Iermia and Odouia and Iediēl, mighty men of power, men of name, chiefs of houses of their fathers.

**1 Chronicles 5:25**

And they transgressed against the God of their fathers and whored after gods of the peoples of the land, whom God drove out from before them.

**1 Chronicles 5:26**

And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Phaloch king of Assour and the spirit of Thaglathphalnasar king of Assour, and he deported Rouben and the Gaddi and the half tribe of Manassē, and brought them to Chalach and Chabor and Hara and to river Gozan, until this day.

**1 Chronicles 5:27**

Sons of Levi: Gedson, Kaath, and Merari.

**1 Chronicles 5:28**

And sons of Kaath: Ambram, Issaar, Chebron, and Oziēl.

**1 Chronicles 5:29**

**1 Chronicles 5:30**

Eleazar begot Phinees, Phinees begot Abisou,

**1 Chronicles 5:31**

Abisou begot Bokkai, Bokkai begot Ozi,

**1 Chronicles 5:32**

**1 Chronicles 5:33**

and Mariel begot Amaria, and Amaria begot Achitob,

**1 Chronicles 5:34**

and Achitob begot Sadok, and Sadok begot Achimaas,

**1 Chronicles 5:35**

and Achimaas begot Azaria, and Azarias begot Ioanan,

**1 Chronicles 5:36**

and Ioanas begot Azarian. This one served as priest in the house which Salomon built in Jerusalem.

**1 Chronicles 5:37**

And Azaria begot Amaria, and Amaria begot Achitob,

**1 Chronicles 5:38**

and Achitob begot Sadok, and Sadok begot Salom,

**1 Chronicles 5:39**

and Salom begot Chelkian, and Chelkias begot Azaria,

**1 Chronicles 5:40**

### Chapter 10

**1 Chronicles 10:1**

And Philistines fought against Israel, and Israel fled from before Philistines, and wounded men fell on Mount Gelboue.

**1 Chronicles 10:2**

And Philistines pursued after Saul and after his sons, and Philistines struck Ionathan and Aminadab and Melchisoue, sons of Saul.

**1 Chronicles 10:3**

And battle grew heavy against Saul, and archers found him with bows, and he was pained from arrows.

**1 Chronicles 10:4**

And Saul said to one carrying his weapons, Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest these uncircumcised come and mock me. But one carrying his weapons would not, because he feared greatly. And Saul took sword and fell upon it.

**1 Chronicles 10:5**

And one carrying his weapons saw that Saul had died, and he too fell upon his sword and died.

**1 Chronicles 10:6**

And Saul died, and his three sons died on that day, and all his house died together.

**1 Chronicles 10:7**

And every man of Israel in valley saw that Israel fled and that Saul and his sons had died, and they left their cities and fled, and Philistines came and lived in them.

**1 Chronicles 10:8**

**1 Chronicles 10:9**

And they stripped him and took his head and his weapons, and sent into land of Philistines all around to proclaim good news to their idols and to people.

**1 Chronicles 10:10**

And they put his weapons in house of their god, and they put his head in house of Dagon.

**1 Chronicles 10:11**

And all dwelling in Galaad heard all that Philistines had done to Saul and to Israel.

**1 Chronicles 10:12**

And every mighty man from Galaad rose and took body of Saul and bodies of his sons and brought them to Iabis, and they buried their bones under oak in Iabis and fasted seven days.

**1 Chronicles 10:13**

And Saul died in his lawless deeds which he committed lawlessly against Lord, against word of Lord, because he did not keep it, because Saul inquired through ventriloquist to seek, and Samuel prophet answered him.

**1 Chronicles 10:14**

And he did not seek Lord, and he put him to death and turned kingdom to Dauid son of Iessai.

### Chapter 11

**1 Chronicles 11:1**

**1 Chronicles 11:3**

Anan son of Moocha, and Iosaphat the Baithanite,

**1 Chronicles 11:44**

Ozia the Astarothite, Samma and Iiēl sons of Chothan the Hararite,

**1 Chronicles 11:45**

Iediēl son of Sameri and Ioazae his brother the Ieasite,

**1 Chronicles 11:46**

Eliēl the Mii, and Iaribi, and Iosia son of Elnaam, and Iethemas the Moabite,

**1 Chronicles 12:11**

**1 Chronicles 12:29**

**1 Chronicles 12:31**

**1 Chronicles 12:33**

**1 Chronicles 12:34**

**1 Chronicles 12:35**

**1 Chronicles 12:36**

**1 Chronicles 12:37**

**1 Chronicles 12:38**

**1 Chronicles 12:39**

**1 Chronicles 12:40**

**1 Chronicles 12:41**

### Chapter 13

**1 Chronicles 13:1**

And Dauid took counsel with commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with every leader.

**1 Chronicles 13:2**

And Dauid said to all assembly of Israel, If this seems good to you, and if it has been prospered from Lord our God, let us send to our brothers left behind in all land of Israel, and with them to priests and Levites in cities of their possession, and let them gather to us.

**1 Chronicles 13:3**

And let us bring ark of our God to us, because from days of Saul they did not seek it.

**1 Chronicles 13:4**

And all assembly said to do so, because word was upright in eyes of all people.

**1 Chronicles 13:5**

And Dauid assembled all Israel from borders of Egypt and as far as entrance of Hamath, to bring ark of God from city of Iarim.

**1 Chronicles 13:6**

**1 Chronicles 13:7**

And they placed ark of God on new wagon from house of Aminadab, and Oza and his brothers were leading wagon.

**1 Chronicles 13:8**

And Dauid and all Israel were playing before God with all strength, and with songs and lyres and harps and tambourines and cymbals and trumpets.

**1 Chronicles 13:9**

And they came as far as threshing floor, and Oza stretched out his hand to grasp ark, because calf turned it aside.

**1 Chronicles 13:10**

And Lord’s anger grew hot against Oza, and he struck him there because he stretched out his hand upon ark, and he died there before God.

**1 Chronicles 13:11**

And Dauid was troubled because Lord had broken out with breach against Oza, and he called that place Breach-of-Oza until this day.

**1 Chronicles 13:12**

And Dauid feared God on that day, saying, How shall I bring ark of God to myself?

**1 Chronicles 13:13**

And Dauid did not bring back ark to himself into City of Dauid, but turned it aside into house of Abeddara the Geththite.

**1 Chronicles 13:14**

And ark of God stayed in house of Abeddara three months, and God blessed Abeddaram and all his things.

### Chapter 14

**1 Chronicles 14:1**

**1 Chronicles 14:2**

**1 Chronicles 14:3**

**1 Chronicles 14:4**

**1 Chronicles 14:5**

**1 Chronicles 14:6**

and Nage and Naphag and Ianouou,

**1 Chronicles 14:7**

**1 Chronicles 14:8**

**1 Chronicles 14:9**

**1 Chronicles 14:10**

**1 Chronicles 14:11**

**1 Chronicles 14:12**

**1 Chronicles 14:13**

**1 Chronicles 14:14**

**1 Chronicles 14:15**

**1 Chronicles 14:16**

**1 Chronicles 14:17**

**1 Chronicles 15:1**

### Chapter 16

**1 Chronicles 16:1**

**1 Chronicles 16:3**

**1 Chronicles 16:5**

**1 Chronicles 16:6**

**1 Chronicles 16:7**

**1 Chronicles 16:8**

**1 Chronicles 16:9**

**1 Chronicles 16:10**

**1 Chronicles 16:11**

Seek Lord and grow strong; seek his face continually.

**1 Chronicles 16:12**

**1 Chronicles 16:13**

**1 Chronicles 16:14**

He is Lord our God; in all earth are his judgments.

**1 Chronicles 16:15**

Remembering forever his covenant, his word which he commanded for thousand generations,

**1 Chronicles 16:16**

**1 Chronicles 16:17**

**1 Chronicles 16:18**

**1 Chronicles 16:19**

**1 Chronicles 16:20**

**1 Chronicles 16:21**

**1 Chronicles 16:22**

Do not touch my anointed ones, and do not do evil among my prophets.

**1 Chronicles 16:23**

**1 Chronicles 16:25**

For Lord is great and greatly praised; he is fearful above all gods.

**1 Chronicles 16:26**

For all gods of nations are idols, but our God made heaven.

**1 Chronicles 16:27**

Glory and praise are before him; strength and boasting are in his place.

**1 Chronicles 16:28**

**1 Chronicles 16:29**

Give to Lord glory of his name; take gifts and bring them before him, and worship Lord in his holy courts.

**1 Chronicles 16:30**

Let all earth fear from before him; let earth be set right and not be shaken.

**1 Chronicles 16:31**

**1 Chronicles 16:32**

**1 Chronicles 16:33**

**1 Chronicles 16:34**

**1 Chronicles 16:35**

**1 Chronicles 16:36**

**1 Chronicles 16:37**

**1 Chronicles 16:38**

**1 Chronicles 16:39**

and Sadok the priest and his brothers the priests before tent of Lord at high place in Gabaon,

**1 Chronicles 16:40**

**1 Chronicles 16:41**

and with him Haiman and Idithon and rest of chosen ones named by name to praise Lord, because his mercy is forever,

**1 Chronicles 16:42**

and with them trumpets and cymbals for sounding aloud, and instruments of songs of God; sons of Idithon were at gate.

**1 Chronicles 16:43**

### Chapter 17

**1 Chronicles 17:1**

And it came to pass, as Dauid settled in his house, Dauid said to Nathan prophet, Behold, I dwell in cedar house, but ark of covenant of Lord is under curtains.

**1 Chronicles 17:2**

And Nathan said to Dauid, Do all that is in your soul, because God is with you.

**1 Chronicles 17:3**

And it came to pass in that night, word of Lord came to Nathan, saying,

**1 Chronicles 17:4**

Go and speak to Dauid my servant, Thus says Lord, You shall not build me house for me to dwell in it.

**1 Chronicles 17:5**

Because I have not dwelt in house from day when I brought up Israel until this day, but I have been in tent and in dwelling-place.

**1 Chronicles 17:6**

In all places where I went through among all Israel, did I ever speak to one tribe of Israel, to shepherd my people, saying, Why have you not built me cedar house?

**1 Chronicles 17:7**

And now thus you shall say to my servant Dauid, Thus says Lord Almighty, I took you from fold, from behind sheep, to be ruler over my people Israel.

**1 Chronicles 17:8**

And I was with you in all places where you went, and I destroyed all your enemies from before you, and I made for you name like name of great ones on earth.

**1 Chronicles 17:9**

And I will appoint place for my people Israel and plant him, and he shall dwell by himself and not be anxious anymore, and unrighteousness shall not again afflict him as from beginning,

**1 Chronicles 17:10**

and from days when I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I humbled all your enemies, and I will increase you, and Lord will build house for you.

**1 Chronicles 17:11**

And it shall be, when your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, who shall be from your belly, and I will prepare his kingdom.

**1 Chronicles 17:12**

He shall build me house, and I will set upright his throne forever.

**1 Chronicles 17:13**

I will be to him for father, and he shall be to me for son, and I will not remove my mercy from him, as I removed it from those before you.

**1 Chronicles 17:14**

And I will make him faithful in my house and in his kingdom forever, and his throne shall stand upright forever.

**1 Chronicles 17:15**

According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to Dauid.

**1 Chronicles 17:16**

And king Dauid came and sat before Lord and said, Who am I, Lord God, and what is my house, that you loved me unto forever?

**1 Chronicles 17:17**

And these things were made small before you, O God, and you spoke concerning house of your servant for long distance, and you looked upon me as vision of man, and you exalted me, Lord God.

**1 Chronicles 17:18**

What more shall Dauid add to you to glorify? And you know your servant.

**1 Chronicles 17:19**

And according to your heart you did all this greatness.

**1 Chronicles 17:20**

Lord, there is none like you, and there is none besides you, according to all things we heard with our ears.

**1 Chronicles 17:21**

And there is no nation on earth like your people Israel, whom God led to redeem for himself as people, to make for himself great and manifest name, to drive out nations from before your people, whom you redeemed from Egypt.

**1 Chronicles 17:22**

And you gave your people Israel to yourself as people forever, and you, Lord, became God to them.

**1 Chronicles 17:23**

And now, Lord, let your word which you spoke concerning your servant and concerning his house be made faithful forever.

**1 Chronicles 17:24**

Let them say, Lord, Lord Almighty, God of Israel, and let house of Dauid your servant be established before you.

**1 Chronicles 17:25**

Because you, Lord, opened ear of your servant to build him house. Therefore your servant found courage to pray before you.

**1 Chronicles 17:26**

And now, Lord, you are that God, and you spoke these good things concerning your servant.

**1 Chronicles 17:27**

And now you began to bless house of your servant, that it may be forever before you, because you, Lord, blessed; bless forever.

### Chapter 18

**1 Chronicles 18:1**

**1 Chronicles 18:3**

**1 Chronicles 18:4**

**1 Chronicles 18:5**

**1 Chronicles 18:6**

**1 Chronicles 18:7**

**1 Chronicles 18:9**

**1 Chronicles 18:10**

**1 Chronicles 18:11**

**1 Chronicles 18:12**

**1 Chronicles 18:13**

**1 Chronicles 18:14**

**1 Chronicles 18:15**

**1 Chronicles 18:16**

**1 Chronicles 18:17**

### Chapter 19

**1 Chronicles 19:1**

And it came to pass after these things, Naas king of sons of Ammon died, and Anan his son reigned in his place.

**1 Chronicles 19:2**

And Dauid said, I will do mercy with Anan son of Naas, as his father did mercy with me. And Dauid sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. And servants of Dauid came into land of sons of Ammon to comfort him.

**1 Chronicles 19:3**

And rulers of Ammon said to Anan, Does Dauid honor your father before you because he sent comforters to you? Did not his servants come to you to search city and spy out land?

**1 Chronicles 19:4**

And Anan took servants of Dauid and shaved them and cut away half their cloaks as far as garment and sent them away.

**1 Chronicles 19:5**

And men came to report to Dauid concerning men, and he sent to meet them, because men had been greatly dishonored. And king said, Sit in Iericho until your beards grow, and then return.

**1 Chronicles 19:6**

And sons of Ammon saw that people of Dauid had been shamed, and Anan and sons of Ammon sent one thousand talents of silver to hire for themselves chariots and horsemen from Syria of Mesopotamia and from Syria of Moocha and from Souba.

**1 Chronicles 19:7**

And they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots and king of Moocha and his people, and they came and camped opposite Maidaba. And sons of Ammon gathered from their cities and came to battle.

**1 Chronicles 19:8**

And Dauid heard and sent Ioab and all army of mighty men.

**1 Chronicles 19:9**

And sons of Ammon came out and drew up for battle by gate of city, and kings who came camped by themselves in plain.

**1 Chronicles 19:10**

And Ioab saw that front of battle had come against him before and behind, and he chose from every young man of Israel, and they drew up against Syrians.

**1 Chronicles 19:11**

And rest of people he gave into hand of Abessa his brother, and they drew up opposite sons of Ammon.

**1 Chronicles 19:12**

And he said, If Syrians prevail over me, you shall be for salvation to me, and if sons of Ammon prevail over you, I will save you.

**1 Chronicles 19:13**

Act like man, and let us strengthen ourselves for our people and for cities of our God, and Lord will do what is good in his eyes.

**1 Chronicles 19:14**

And Ioab drew up, and people with him, opposite Syrians for battle, and they fled from him.

**1 Chronicles 19:15**

And sons of Ammon saw that Syrians fled, and they too fled from before Ioab and from before Abessa his brother and came into city. And Ioab came to Ierousalem.

**1 Chronicles 19:16**

And Syria saw that Israel routed him, and they sent messengers and brought out Syrians from beyond river, with Sophach commander of force of Adraazar before them.

**1 Chronicles 19:17**

And it was reported to Dauid, and he gathered all Israel and crossed Jordan and came against them and drew up against them. And Syria drew up opposite Dauid and fought him.

**1 Chronicles 19:18**

And Syria fled from before Dauid, and Dauid killed from Syria seven thousand chariots and forty thousand footmen, and he killed Sophach commander of force.

**1 Chronicles 19:19**

And servants of Adraazar saw that they had fallen before Israel, and they made covenant with Dauid and served him. And Syria did not want to help sons of Ammon anymore.

### Chapter 20

**1 Chronicles 20:1**

And it came to pass in following year, at time when kings go out, Ioab led all force of army and ruined land of sons of Ammon and came and besieged Rabbah, while Dauid stayed in Ierousalem. And Ioab struck Rabbah and tore it down.

**1 Chronicles 20:2**

And Dauid took crown of Molchol their king from his head, and its weight was found to be a talent of gold, and in it was precious stone, and it was upon head of Dauid. And he brought out spoils of city very many.

**1 Chronicles 20:3**

And people in it he brought out and cut with saws and with iron picks, and thus Dauid did to all sons of Ammon. And Dauid and all his people returned to Ierousalem.

**1 Chronicles 20:4**

And it came to pass after these things, there was still war in Gazer with Philistines. Then Sobochai the Ousathite struck Saphou from sons of giants, and he humbled him.

**1 Chronicles 20:5**

And there was yet war with Philistines, and Ellanan son of Iair struck Leemi brother of Goliath the Geththite, and wood of his spear was like beam of weavers.

**1 Chronicles 20:6**

And there was still war in Geth, and there was oversized man, and his fingers were six and six, twenty-four, and he was descendant of giants.

**1 Chronicles 20:7**

And he reproached Israel, and Ionathan son of Samaa brother of Dauid struck him.

**1 Chronicles 20:8**

These were born to Rapha in Geth; all were four giants, and they fell by hand of Dauid and by hand of his servants.

### Chapter 21

**1 Chronicles 21:1**

And slanderer stood up against Israel and stirred Dauid to number Israel.

**1 Chronicles 21:2**

And king Dauid said to Ioab and to chiefs of force, Go, number Israel from Bersabee to Dan, and bring to me, and I shall know their number.

**1 Chronicles 21:3**

And Ioab said, May Lord add to his people a hundredfold as they are, and are not eyes of my lord the king seeing that all are servants to my lord? Why does my lord seek this, so that it should not become sin for Israel?

**1 Chronicles 21:4**

But word of king prevailed over Ioab. And Ioab went out and passed through all border of Israel and came to Ierousalem.

**1 Chronicles 21:5**

And Ioab gave number of mustering of people to Dauid, and all Israel was one million one hundred thousand men drawing sword, and Iouda was four hundred eighty thousand men drawing sword.

**1 Chronicles 21:6**

But Levi and Beniamin he did not count among them, because word of king overpowered Ioab.

**1 Chronicles 21:7**

And thing appeared evil before God concerning this matter, and he struck Israel.

**1 Chronicles 21:8**

And Dauid said to God, I sinned greatly because I did this thing, and now please take away evil of your servant, because I acted very foolishly.

**1 Chronicles 21:9**

And Lord spoke to Gad, seer of Dauid, saying,

**1 Chronicles 21:10**

Go and speak to Dauid, saying, Thus says Lord, I lift three things upon you; choose one of them for yourself, and I will do it to you.

**1 Chronicles 21:11**

And Gad came to Dauid and said to him, Thus says Lord, Choose for yourself:

**1 Chronicles 21:12**

either three years of famine, or three months for you to flee from before your enemies while sword of your enemies destroys, or three days sword of Lord and death in land, and angel of Lord destroying in all inheritance of Israel. And now see what word I should answer to one who sent me.

**1 Chronicles 21:13**

And Dauid said to Gad, All three press me very hard. Let me now fall into hands of Lord, because his mercies are very many; but into hands of men I shall not fall.

**1 Chronicles 21:14**

And Lord gave death in Israel, and seventy thousand men fell from Israel.

**1 Chronicles 21:15**

And God sent angel into Ierousalem to destroy it, and as he destroyed, Lord saw and relented over evil and said to angel destroying, It is enough for you; let go your hand. And angel of Lord was standing at threshing floor of Orna the Iebousite.

**1 Chronicles 21:16**

And Dauid lifted his eyes and saw angel of Lord standing between earth and between heaven, with his sword drawn in his hand, stretched out over Ierousalem. And Dauid and elders clothed in sackcloth fell on their faces.

**1 Chronicles 21:17**

And Dauid said to God, Was it not I who said to number among people? And I am one who sinned; I acted evilly with evil. But these sheep, what did they do? Lord God, let your hand be on me and on house of my father, and not on your people for destruction, Lord.

**1 Chronicles 21:18**

And angel of Lord said to Gad to tell Dauid to go up and set altar to Lord at threshing floor of Orna the Iebousite.

**1 Chronicles 21:19**

And Dauid went up according to word of Gad, which he spoke in name of Lord.

**1 Chronicles 21:20**

And Orna turned and saw king, and his four sons with him were hiding themselves, and Orna was threshing wheat.

**1 Chronicles 21:21**

And Dauid came to Orna, and Orna came out from threshing floor and bowed to Dauid with face to ground.

**1 Chronicles 21:22**

And Dauid said to Orna, Give me place of your threshing floor, and I will build on it altar to Lord. For silver at full worth give it to me, and plague will stop from people.

**1 Chronicles 21:23**

And Orna said to Dauid, Take for yourself, and let my lord the king do good in his sight. Behold, I have given calves for whole burnt offering, and plow and wagons for wood, and wheat for sacrifice; I have given all.

**1 Chronicles 21:24**

And king Dauid said to Orna, No, because by buying I will buy for full worth in silver, because I shall not take what is yours for Lord, to offer free whole burnt offering to Lord.

**1 Chronicles 21:25**

And Dauid gave to Orna in his place six hundred shekels of weight in gold.

**1 Chronicles 21:26**

And Dauid built there altar to Lord and offered whole burnt offerings and peace offerings, and cried out to Lord, and he answered him with fire from heaven upon altar of whole burnt offering and consumed whole burnt offering.

**1 Chronicles 21:27**

And Lord spoke to angel, and he put sword into sheath.

**1 Chronicles 21:28**

At that time, when Dauid saw that Lord answered him at threshing floor of Orna the Iebousite, he sacrificed there.

**1 Chronicles 21:29**

And tent of Lord which Moyses made in wilderness, and altar of whole burnt offerings, were at that time at high place in Gabaon.

**1 Chronicles 21:30**

And Dauid was not able to go before it to seek God, because he hurried in fear from before sword of angel of Lord.

### Chapter 22

**1 Chronicles 22:1**

And Dauid said, This is house of Lord God, and this is altar for whole burnt offering for Israel.

**1 Chronicles 22:2**

**1 Chronicles 22:3**

**1 Chronicles 22:4**

**1 Chronicles 22:5**

**1 Chronicles 22:6**

**1 Chronicles 22:7**

**1 Chronicles 22:8**

**1 Chronicles 22:9**

Behold, son is born to you. He shall be man of rest, and I will give him rest from all enemies around, because Salomon shall be his name, and peace and quietness I will give upon Israel in his days.

**1 Chronicles 22:10**

He shall build house to my name, and he shall be to me for son, and I to him for father, and I will set upright throne of his kingdom in Israel forever.

**1 Chronicles 22:11**

**1 Chronicles 22:12**

**1 Chronicles 22:13**

Then you shall prosper if you keep doing ordinances and judgments which Lord commanded Moyses for Israel. Act like man and be strong; do not fear and do not be dismayed.

**1 Chronicles 22:14**

And behold, in my poverty I prepared for house of Lord one hundred thousand talents of gold and one thousand thousand talents of silver, and bronze and iron without weight, because it is in abundance, and wood and stones I prepared, and to these add more.

**1 Chronicles 22:15**

And with you are workers in abundance, craftsmen and builders of stone and carpenters of wood and every wise man in every work,

**1 Chronicles 22:16**

**1 Chronicles 22:17**

And Dauid commanded all rulers of Israel to help Salomon his son:

**1 Chronicles 22:18**

Is not Lord with you and has he not given you rest all around? Because he gave inhabitants of land into hands, and land is subdued before Lord and before his people.

**1 Chronicles 22:19**

Now give your hearts and your souls to seek Lord your God, and rise and build sanctuary to Lord your God, to bring ark of covenant of Lord and holy vessels of God into house being built for name of Lord.

**1 Chronicles 23:31**
